items.summary: Cooling crude oil prices prompted reassessments of India's monetary path, with bond yields and rate expectations shifting toward a less aggressive Reserve Bank of India (RBI) stance. Brent crude moderated to $90 per barrel in November from around $117 in mid-October, prompting State Bank of India to revise its December call down from 50 basis points to 25 bps as it cooled its inflation alarm. The broader market consensus also moved toward a lower terminal rate; long tenured bonds had already priced in a 50–75 bps hike this cycle but now appear to price only a maximum of 50 bps, with the far end of the curve described as topped out and long-term yields rallying on better demand. Anshul Chandak, head of treasury at RBL Bank, cautioned that inflation remains a concern even as oil cools, noting November CPI was projected near 6.0% after October's 6.09%, which Barclays flagged as the highest in over two years with slowing momentum expected. Meanwhile, short-term yields hardened partly from tightening liquidity: daily average liquidity fell to ₹1.57 lakh crore in November from ₹2.37 crore in October (as reported), and rising inflation exerted upward pressure on short-end yields, flattening the G-sec yield curve—though it had not inverted, unlike the corporate bond curve per Sameer Karyatt of DBS Bank India. Separately, US Treasury yields declined sharply as investors rotated into safe-haven assets amid concerns about AI-related company debt and spending; the 10-year note fell below 5% for the first time in several months.
items.title: Bond market signals softer RBI tightening as crude prices retreat

items.summary: OCBC group chief executive Tan Teck Long, who assumed the role in January 2026 as the first Singaporean to lead the bank in over two decades, outlined a strategy centered on growing earnings while maintaining high return on equity rather than pursuing size alone. Under his leadership, OCBC's earnings grew across the first three quarters of 2026, supported by strong wealth management performance and its February
items.title: OCBC CEO Tan Teck Long Prioritizes Higher ROE and AI-Augmented Staffing Amid Expansion

items.summary: India's Sensex rose roughly 20% in dollar terms, crossing the widely cited (though informal) bull-market threshold of a 20%+ gain. Manishi Raychaudhuri, CEO of Hong Kong-based Emmer Capital Partners, attributed about 15-16% of this rise to climbing share prices and only 4-5% to rupee appreciation. The rally reflects emerging market investors—historically underweight on India—who are rotating out of crowded AI trades into Indian equities; Raychaudhuri characterized the move as still in its early stages with scope for continued inflows over coming months. Ben Powell, chief investment strategist at BlackRock Investment Institute's Middle East and Asia-Pacific team, added that India's expanding workforce, rising productivity, and digitalization offer diversification benefits amid markets increasingly viewed as an "AI trade in disguise." Foreign investors have pumped $14.33 billion (about ₹1.43 lakh crore) into Indian stocks since October 16, buying across 20 of the 24 trading sessions; FPIs invested $10.4 billion during the December quarter, India's second-highest inflow after Japan's $48 billion. This contrasts with heavy outflows elsewhere: South Korea and Taiwan saw -$26 billion and -$57 billion respectively in early 2026, while foreign investors sold nearly $55 billion of Indian equities between October 2024 and September 2026. The rally occurred as global markets corrected on AI/tech concerns, higher rates, inflation, and policy uncertainty—during which the S&P 500 fell 10%, Dow Jones and Nasdaq declined 5% and 16%, China's Shenzhen and Hang Seng lost 9% each, Japan's Nikkei dropped 16%, Taiwan's Taiex and South Korea's Kospi slid ~28%, Indonesia's Jakarta Composite fell 17%, the Philippines lost 8%, and the UK FTSE 100 and Germany's DAX slipped 4% (France's CAC 40 declined 0.5%). A stated limitation is that Raychaudhuri noted many investors remain on the sidelines, as India's prior underweight positions were so large that a neutral tilt was difficult to achieve in roughly three weeks.
items.title: Sensex Surges ~20% in Dollar Terms as Foreign Money Chases India

visual.alt: Bar chart. Share price gains 15; Rupee appreciation 4.

items.summary: According to a report by The Times of India's Ahmedabad bureau (Ashish Chauhan), an anti-immigration crackdown in the United States resulted in 1,389 unaccompanied Indian minors being placed in US custody over four fiscal years beginning with America's FY23. These children have not been repatriated as of reporting. The number of Indian minors travelling without parents or guardians declined across successive fiscal years: 730 in FY23, 517 in FY24, 91 in FY25, and 51 in FY26. The text presents these figures as reported data from the article; it does not independently verify them or provide additional context on custody duration, repatriation procedures, or underlying causes.
items.title: Anti-immigration crackdown in the US has placed 1,389 unaccompanied Indian children in custody since FY23

visual.alt: Bar chart. FY23 730; FY24 517; FY25 91; FY26 51.

items.summary: Countries failed to reach a major new climate agreement after deep divisions over fossil fuels and financing emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Antalya, Turkey. Negotiations ran late into Sunday, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history, but the final draft proved unacceptable because it never directly mentioned 'fossil fuels,' with only an indirect nod to the 2023 COP28 pledge to transition away from them. The EU's representative, Irish Minister Darragh O'Brien, said the deal fell far short of ambition and was unconscionable for omitting fossil fuels outright; Panama and the Marshall Islands also criticized it as insufficient. Meanwhile, poorer nations objected that richer countries offered no clear financial commitments for adaptation—despite last year's COP30 pledge to triple such finance—which raised fears of unmeasured 'wriggle room.' Oil-producing states pushed back against language on coal, oil and gas: Saudi Arabia argued its emissions were historically small, while Russia warned that moving away from fossil fuels too quickly could cause fuel poverty. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres called the outcome a disappointment and blamed powerful fossil fuel interests for distorting science and delaying policy; Australian PM Anthony Albanese attributed the failure to difficult geopolitical times.
items.title: COP31 Fails to Reach Major Climate Deal as Talks Expose Deep Divisions

items.summary:
Donald Trump is scheduled to headline his third cryptocurrency gala on Sunday night at the Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, rewarding holders of his $TRUMP meme coin as Democrats accuse him of improperly profiting from crypto ventures while in office. The event offers tiered perks for its 185 holders: fragrance, poster, commemorative ticket, and watch for 120 attendees; a VIP reception for the top 29 investors; and an 18K gold watch for the top four. This follows two similar galas since Trump took office in 2025.

Critics argue the dinner's structure is designed to boost $TRUMP investment, according to a letter from Senator Adam Schiff and eight others sent last month. Financial disclosures released in June indicate Trump has earned more than $1bn from crypto businesses since returning to the White House: over $500m from World Liberty Financial sales and about $600m from meme coin sales. The Trump family's stake in Trump Media & Technology Group is valued at roughly $430m, while their four main crypto ventures have collectively earned at least $2.3bn through April.

Interest in the dinner has declined sharply, with combined contestant holdings falling from $148m in May 2025 to $8.6m for this month's gala. A Public Citizen analysis of blockchain data found that more than half of the wallets on Sunday's leaderboard are tied to exchanges that bar US users, suggesting links to foreign nationals.

The White House denied any conflicts of interest through spokesperson Anna Kelly, while Trump family crypto ventures have fallen in value to record lows, with outside investors losing more than $5bn. Democrats plan investigations and legislation targeting such activities.
items.title: Trump to Host Third Crypto Gala for Meme Coin Amid Conflict-of-Interest Criticism

visual.alt: Bar chart. May 2025 148,000,000 $; Current Gala (this month) 8,600,000 $.

items.summary: Poundland, a UK and Irish discount retailer operating 600 stores under the Dealz brand in Ireland with approximately 11,000 employees, is facing a possible collapse into administration. Its owner Gordon Brothers listed it for sale in September but rejected offers to keep the business operational. The situation stems from what insolvency specialist Julie Palmer of Begbies Traynor describes as a funding and ownership problem rather than a trading collapse: while Poundland turned a corner over the year to September, moving from a £68m loss to an £18.1m profit before interest, tax and certain accounting charges, with first-quarter like-for-like sales up 7% and operational profits of £1.9m up £1.2m on the prior year, Gordon Brothers has restricted access to cash needed for restocking and day-to-day expenses by freezing about £50m in funds before releasing around £21m over two weeks. Analyst Catherine Shuttleworth of Savvy Marketing noted that shoppers have not abandoned Poundland, citing 11.4% higher Halloween sales as a positive indicator heading into Christmas. The core tension is that Gordon Brothers, which made roughly £18m from debt interest and fees since acquiring the business for £1 (including inheriting a £22.5m shareholder loan), also serves as Poundland's main creditor; Palmer explained that when the owner is the primary lender, its priority to recover loans can conflict with preserving jobs. Rescue bids have come from Irish firm Martin Property Group and London-based Xyra Group—though doubts remain about Xyra's credibility—with a third unnamed bid on the table, while Gordon Brothers has weighed breaking up Poundland, arguing buyers of the store estate would be required to retain employees. The immediate make-or-break issue is Christmas stock availability; for now Poundland avoided collapse after a 10-day deadline extension to secure a rescue deal, though Shuttleworth described its future as unclear amid owner-management disagreement and noted that Gordon Brothers appears unmoved by UK government pressure from Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds over the rejected Martin Property Group offer.
items.title: Poundland Faces Possible Administration Despite Trading Recovery

items.summary: San Francisco is experiencing an economic rejuvenation driven largely by the artificial intelligence sector. Leading firms OpenAI and Anthropic are headquartered in the city, with thousands of other AI start-ups emerging there; Anthropic recently listed on Nasdaq. The boom has manifested in soaring rents and house prices, falling office vacancies, and widespread AI advertising. However, concerns about a downward correction have grown: the International Monetary Fund warned last month that such a crash is possible, and recent scandal surrounding Nvidia's Jensen Huang contributed to wider AI stock falls—though Nvidia remains highly profitable after reporting doubled quarterly profits of $65bn (£49bn). Some workers in the city are pessimistic about whether leading US AI companies can sustain their spending amid cheaper models from China, while others view a market correction as less alarming than existential risks posed by AI. A key distinction is that San Francisco may be hit harder than Silicon Valley: one study found 60% of venture capital invested in US AI firms from 2023 to 2025 went to companies located in the city, dwarfing those in Silicon Valley, which lies about 40 miles south. Yet some factors suggest a softer impact—AI firms employ relatively few workers compared to previous tech booms, and much of their spending goes toward data centres and computing power outside the Bay Area; San Francisco remains roughly 35,000 jobs shy of its pre-pandemic peak. Economists note that while a correction could be painful through spillover effects on service-sector jobs like restaurants, retail, and personal services such as dog walking, diversification into healthcare and tourism may cushion the blow. City economist Ted Egan views any slowdown primarily as a 'hiccup' rather than a major course correction.
items.title: San Francisco's AI Boom and Concerns Over a Possible Crash

items.summary: A news item reports that the Russia-Ukraine war has produced incidents extending onto European territory, including attacks on ships, missiles in Poland, and fresh allegations of Russian operations inside Denmark. These events are framed as a recurring pattern of the conflict 'creeping' beyond Ukraine's borders into NATO-associated regions. The source notes it does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews, indicating editorial independence from external financial influence.
items.title: Ukraine War Incidents Reported on European Territory

items.summary: Former Bachelor contestant Sam Wood, 46, appeared at Maroochydore Magistrates Court on charges of assault occasioning bodily harm and strangulation allegedly committed against his wife while he was holidaying in a Noosa apartment complex. His new lawyer, Bradford Hill of BJH Law, told the court that they had just received the brief of evidence from police this morning and wanted to propose justice mediation to the prosecution; there was no further bail application and the charges were adjourned for two weeks. Wood remains remanded in custody after nearly two months behind bars following a bail refusal at Maroochydore Magistrates Court last month and again in the Supreme Court of Brisbane, with an appeal against that second refusal heard by Queensland's Court of Appeal last week. During the earlier bail proceedings, prosecution Crown prosecutor Jessica Guy relied on a prison call between Wood and his father to argue he was at risk of reoffending and interfering with witnesses; in the recording Wood said he needed to speak with his wife and asked whether the charges could be dropped if she changed her police statement. Defence lawyer Paula Morreau KC characterized the remark as ill judged but argued it reflected a desire rather than a request, contending that it did not establish an intention to breach bail conditions. The appeal decision was adjourned without resolution.
items.title: Sam Wood's Lawyer Proposes Justice Mediation as Domestic Violence Charges Remain Pending

items.summary:
The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) were blamed for drone strikes on Sudan's capital, Khartoum, that killed at least four civilians and injured at least nine others according to local reports. The attacks also damaged a United Nations building, per a statement from the UN. Explosions occurred in the early hours as air defenses responded to drones reportedly targeting government buildings and the city airport, with video showing a home reduced to rubble.

The Sudanese military said the drones were launched from Ethiopia, though Addis Ababa denies allowing attacks to be staged on its territory. The UN's coordinator for Sudan, Denise Brown, stated in response that drone strikes are causing "untold suffering." Drone warfare has surged recently, accounting for 80 per cent of civilian deaths in the first half of the year.

A report from the UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR) found drones killed more than 1,630 civilians between January and October 2026. The use of drones evolved this year amid an ongoing toll on Sudanese civilians. In one recent incident, 80 people were killed near a market in al-Dibab, West Kordofan, part of at least 39 drone strikes on markets this year.

More than three years of fighting has displaced more than 14 million people and left almost 34 million needing humanitarian assistance. Aid organizations say the war has killed more than 200,000 people and pushed parts of the country into famine, with experts noting the death toll is likely much higher.

The conflict began in April 2023 between army chief General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo. The Sudanese army secured Khartoum from the RSF in May 2025, with an international presence returning to the capital along with 2.5 million returnees as of October 2026 per the UN Refugee Agency.

The article attributes blame for the strikes and drone launches to specific parties but notes these are claims rather than confirmed facts; Addis Ababa denies staging attacks from its territory, and casualty figures rely on local reports.
items.title: Drone Strikes Kill Four Civilians in Khartoum and Damage a UN Building

items.summary: India A captain Tilak Varma attributed his team's 48-run defeat to Pakistan A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament on Sunday primarily to a lack of middle-order partnerships. Chasing 314, India A were struggling at 129/6 before Abhishek Sharma (70 off 42 balls) and Tilak Varma (unbeaten 100 off 149 deliveries) set up the chase; however, a seventh-wicket stand of 112 runs between Tilak and Shahbaz Ahmed was not enough as India A were bowled out for 265. Pakistan's Hasan Nawaz top-scored with 79, supported by half-centuries from Maaz Sadaqat (59) and Farhan Yousaf (56), posting 313 all out. Tilak said Shahbaz's dismissal came at a crucial moment just as the pair intended to accelerate scoring—despite an asking rate above 10 runs per over for much of the chase—and that another couple of overs from the all-rounder could have changed the result, with India A potentially sealing the game in the 47th or 48th over. He credited Pakistan's fast bowlers for good lines and lengths early on but acknowledged his team also lost wickets in quick succession.
items.title: Tilak Varma rues Shahbaz Ahmed's dismissal after India A lose to Pakistan A

visual.alt: Bar chart. Abhishek Sharma 70 off; Shahbaz Ahmed 56 off; Tilak Varma (not out) 100 off.

items.summary:
Howard Lutnick, US commerce secretary and a longtime friend of President Donald Trump, has remained politically resilient despite repeated clashes with senior officials and scrutiny over his past association with convicted offender Jeffrey Epstein. According to The Wall Street Journal, Lutnick nearly lost his position earlier this year after acknowledging that he had visited Epstein's private island; the prospect of removal reportedly faded following a $25 million donation to Trump's presidential library, per people familiar with the matter. This donation was previously reported in the book Regime Change.

Lutnick has retained Trump's confidence largely due to their friendship spanning more than two decades, even amid criticism from senior Republicans and administration members. His position came under fresh scrutiny last week when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed him for delaying restrictions on advanced chips central to an Nvidia controversy involving co-founder Jensen Huang and allegations of a suspected Chinese spy connection; Trump later defended the delay.

Lutnick's relationship with former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles had also been strained, but following her departure he reportedly told associates "I'm not going anywhere." A White House official stated that Trump continued to have complete confidence in Lutnick and recently praised his performance as commerce secretary. The reporting relies on unnamed sources, including people familiar with the donation matter and a single White House official.
items.title: $25 Million Donation to Trump's Library Reported After Commerce Secretary Lutnick Nearly Lost His Job

items.summary: Sarah Ann, a nurse based in Arizona, left her full-time nursing position after reportedly earning approximately Rs 82 lakh over seven months through content creation and brand collaborations. She stated that the income gave her confidence to quit her 9-to-5 job so she could spend more time creating content and with family. The details were shared via an Instagram video titled 'How much money I've made as a content creator in seven months. I just quit my 9-5 as a nurse.' No independent verification of the earnings figure is provided, and all claims derive solely from her self-reported social media post.
items.title: Arizona Nurse Quits Nursing Job After Earning Rs 82 Lakh in Seven Months From Content Creation

items.summary: The artist Jean-Michel Fourtou has transformed a site in Morocco into the sculpture park known as Ramakech, which opened to the public in 2024 after he began developing it in 1999. The park features surreal installations designed to evoke childhood memories and emotions; among them is 'The House Fallen from the Sky,' created in 2010 as a tribute to Fourtou's grandfather. This structure sits on its roof at a 17-degree angle, with inverted furniture, windows, and bathroom fittings meant to disorient visitors. Other attractions include oversized household objects such as chairs, tables, notebooks, and wardrobes intended to recreate the perspective of exploring his great-grandmother's home, along with figures like farmers and gardeners bearing oversized pumpkin- or plant-shaped heads, giant ants surrounding a mud-built structure, and colorful architectural installations. Fourtou describes these human-botanical combinations as designed to provoke curiosity and unease, while he frames the sculptures overall as explorations of emotions, family relationships, and formative memories rather than mere nostalgia. The park currently attracts around 5,000 visitors annually.
items.title: Morocco's Ramakech Sculpture Park

items.title: BepiColombo Begins Mercury Orbit Despite Thruster Glitch

items.summary: The author, frustrated by inconsistent and unattractive default HTML select box rendering across browsers—particularly in Chrome—had Claude Fable 5.2 generate a demonstration page illustrating the various ways these boxes can be styled, with plans to capture screenshots of each design across every desktop and mobile browser. After experimentation, they settled on their preferred CSS approach: removing native styling via appearance:none, setting text color (#1f2933), padding (0.5em 2.25em 0.5em 0.75em), a solid border (1px #c4cbd3), rounded corners (6px radius), and a white background overlaid with an inline SVG chevron drawn via data URI, sized at 0.75em and positioned right-aligned. The resulting appearance was then compared across three browsers.
items.title: Select Styling Specimens

items.summary: Solar module manufacturer Thornova Solar and tracker/structural solutions provider Nextpower signed a Master Supply Agreement (MSA) announced at RE+ 2026, marking an expansion of their existing strategic cooperation. The agreement combines Thornova's U.S.-made solar modules with Nextpower's domestically manufactured steel frame technology—specifically the NX CoreFrame system—to increase domestic content and improve structural performance for utility-scale and commercial/industrial (C&I) projects across the United States. According to both companies, integrating the steel frames addresses two market priorities: maximizing domestic content and enhancing module resilience under demanding environmental conditions. The combined solution reportedly offers up to 125% higher allowable panel loading in tracker applications, along with improved resistance to uplift, deflection, and glass breakage, plus simplified system integration through optimized mounting hardware and reduced Balance of System (BoS) requirements. Thornova's global marketing director Andrea Bodenhagen attributed the deal to strengthening their relationship and advancing a competitive U.S. solar manufacturing ecosystem, while Nextpower's vice president and general manager Jenya Meydbray cited NX CoreFrame as an opportunity to address glass breakage and demanding environmental loads. The companies presented these benefits and quotes in support of the announcement; independent verification of the agreement's commercial terms or performance figures was not provided in the source text.
items.title: Thornova Solar and Nextpower Sign Master Supply Agreement at RE+ 2026

items.summary: Crude prices have traded in a narrow range as forecasts of an imminent oil surplus collide with ongoing Middle East attacks and stalled diplomacy. Brent crude rose 1.1% to $92.88 per barrel on Thursday, well below its October peak above $110 but little changed from the start of the week, while WTI gained 1.7% to $84.69 per barrel. The International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its November Oil Market Report that the global market will return to surplus in Q4 as Gulf exports recover faster than demand; it raised October supply to 105.4 million bpd and now sees a 1.7 million bpd surplus in Q4 2026, reversing from a previous forecast of a 1.8 million bpd deficit. The IEA lifted its Q4 supply estimate by 3.3 million bpd, cut its 2027 demand projection by 80,000 bpd to 104.3 million bpd, and lowered the implied OPEC crude call by 220,000 bpd to 20.8 million bpd.
items.title: Oil Markets Price a Surplus That May Not Materialize

visual.alt: Bar chart. Q4 2026 surplus forecast 1,700,000 bpd; Previous Q4 deficit forecast 1,800,000 bpd; October supply estimate increase 3,300,000 bpd; 2027 demand cut 80,000 bpd; OPEC crude call reduction 220,000 bpd.

items.summary: The National Weather Service warned that San Francisco Bay could approach record-high water levels this week as unusually high king tides, storm surge, and warm-ocean seawater expansion combine during the busy Thanksgiving travel period. The greatest flooding threat was expected Tuesday and Wednesday, with forecasters projecting water to rise up to 2.8 feet above ground level in vulnerable coastal areas and warning that road closures could result. At San Francisco's tide gauge, levels were forecast to reach 8.4 feet on Tuesday morning and peak at 8.6 feet around 10:49 a.m. Wednesday—approaching the January 1983 record of 8.66 feet set more than four decades ago. NWS meteorologist Dylan Flynn noted that such high bay levels occur only occasionally in history, underscoring the significance of the threat. San Francisco International Airport prepared for potential disruptions by clearing drainage areas, checking pumping stations, and positioning sandbags and portable barriers; officials expect 6.7 million passengers between Thanksgiving and New Year's Day, an 8% increase from the prior year. Mayor Daniel Lurie urged residents to avoid nonessential travel Monday afternoon through Wednesday. The advisory context included a coastal flood warning for San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines running from Monday at 6 a.m. through Thursday at 4 p.m., Thanksgiving Day. The threat extended along much of California's coastline, with federal forecasters issuing advisories and watches from Humboldt County to Los Angeles County; the NWS warned waves could reach 20 feet on parts of the Central Coast while San Diego reinforced beach barriers. Although rain was expected Tuesday and Wednesday—potentially worsening flooding as high tides restricted drainage—the weather service said conditions should remain mostly dry Thursday, with heavy rain tapering off late Wednesday.
items.title: San Francisco Braces for Historic Coastal Flooding During Thanksgiving Travel Week

visual.alt: Dot chart. Jan 1983 record 8.66 feet; Wed peak (forecast) 8.6 feet; Tue morning (forecast) 8.4 feet.

items.summary: A panel discussion on 'funding your dream life,' held Nov 19, 2025 as part of The Straits Times' (ST) InvestMe financial-literacy campaign, emphasized that breaking large goals—such as buying a home, taking holidays, and retiring early—into monthly saving targets makes them more manageable. Endowus managing director Sheryl Choong said the starting point is deciding what a goal will cost and when it is needed, since the time frame affects whether to use less volatile options like money market funds (for purchases within one to three years) or fixed-income investments (with three to five years available), because money needed soon may be hard to recover if markets fall. Choong illustrated this with her own plan for $15,000 of European trips in 2026, noting that those spending about $15,000 annually on travel should set aside roughly $1,250 monthly a year ahead; she also suggested travelers can instead start with an affordable amount and adjust plans. ST business correspondent Rosalind Ang said planning home costs in stages made her HDB resale flat purchase less daunting, that DIY research cut their renovation bill by about 50 per cent, and that buying household items online helped—though she advised against buying beds online. For retirement, Choong recommended calculating desired income, accounting for CPF Life payouts, then saving or investing to cover the gap. All three speakers agreed it is not prudent for younger people to pursue early retirement so aggressively that little time or money remains to enjoy life in between. The Nov 19 event was the fourth of six planned courses; the final two are scheduled for January and March 2027, with the next session—Real Or Not: Important Real Estate Tips by Invest editor Tan Ooi Boon—to be held Jan 16, 2027 at the SPH Media auditorium in Toa Payoh North. Attendance requires an ST InvestMe subscription package priced at $29.90 per month, and earlier-session videos are available on the campaign's website.
items.title: ST InvestMe Panel Advises Breaking Financial Goals Into Monthly Targets

items.summary:
Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) shifted from net sellers to aggressive buyers of Indian equities in November, investing approximately ₹1.18 lakh crore during the month. This reversal contrasts sharply with a prolonged selling period spanning October 2024 through mid-October 2026, when FPIs offloaded roughly ₹5.51 lakh crore worth of Indian equities—equivalent to an average net outflow of about ₹175 crore per trading hour. Across the 503 trading sessions in that earlier period, foreign investors were net sellers on 314 sessions and buyers on only 189 sessions.

The comparison between the two periods is explicitly noted as not strictly comparable due to their substantial difference in duration; hourly averages are used solely to gauge the pace of FPI flows across both intervals. The November figures therefore reflect a marked acceleration in buying momentum rather than an equivalent volume, and no additional data on sector allocation or specific holdings was provided.
items.title: FPIs Turn Aggressive Buyers, Invest Rs 1.18 Lakh Crore into Indian Equities in November

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioned prosecution against five food businesses, including Bisleri International Pvt Ltd, for products found unsafe or substandard under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Prosecution was recommended for Bisleri after a sample of its packaged drinking water exceeded prescribed bromate limits and was independently declared unsafe by the Referral Food Laboratory due to detected polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons; Bisleri had not responded as of report filing. Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd faced prosecution because chilli powder contained difenoconazole, a pesticide residue, above permitted levels. Tit-Bit Foods (India) Pvt Ltd was targeted over pre-packed chilli powder with excess pesticide residues and turmeric containing tin beyond the allowed limit. Mimansa Industries Private Limited was prosecuted for substandard walnut kernels, while Asha Confectionery faced action because chocolate-filled cookies were misbranded, substandard, and unsafe due to discrepancies in declared sugar values. Separately, FSSAI suspended licences of Urmi Lifesciences LLP over poor hygiene and Gaur Ayurvedic Store over repacking issues. The report notes that Bisleri had not yet responded to the matter at time of filing.
items.title: FSSAI Sanctions Prosecution of Bisleri and Four Other Firms Over Unsafe Food Products

items.summary: Molly Meldrum, a prominent Australian music-industry figure who died on Monday aged 83, received tributes from politicians, entertainers, and industry organizations. He spent more than a decade hosting the ABC program Countdown during which he championed Australian artists and brought international acts to Australia. Anthony Albanese posted praise for Meldrum's interview style and his role in supporting both new and established artists; Jason Donovan described him as the 'very heart' of the music program and recalled an episode featuring Kylie Minogue and Guy Pearce; Richard Wilkins remembered traveling worldwide with Meldrum, noting that Meldrum had accumulated 13 passports over their time together. Gavin Wood, a longtime Countdown colleague, characterized Meldrum as one of the most colorful figures in Australian entertainment. Artists echoed these sentiments: Russell Morris credited Meldrum's production on his 1969 #1 single 'The Real Thing,' Peter Andre thanked him for helping launch his career, and Kate Ceberano praised his selfless dedication to artists' success. The Australian Recording Industry Association noted that both Meldrum and Countdown were the first non-recording-artist inductees into the Aria Hall of Fame in 2014, while the St Kilda football club remembered him as a lifelong supporter.
items.title: Tributes pour in for music industry figure Molly Meldrum after his death at 83

items.summary: Religare's Ajit Mishra, Motilal Oswal's Ruchit Jain, and Asit Mehta's Rohan Shah each published weekly equity strategies projecting the Nifty toward a 26,000–26,341 zone. Mishra recommends accumulating at 25,550–25,650 with a stop-loss of 25,350 and targets of 26,000 then 26,250–26,341; Jain cites four consecutive weeks of gains plus sustained FII buying, a strengthening rupee, and falling crude prices as drivers for his buy-at-25,500–25,600 plan (stop-loss 25,250) targeting 26,200–26,300; Shah warns that the Nifty's nearly 12% monthly advance has left momentum indicators overbought and advises buying futures at 25,300–25,400 (stop-loss 24,800) for a target of 26,000–26,300. On sectors, Mishra favours banks, auto, and realty while expecting IT and metals to face relative pressure; Jain prefers large-caps amid weak breadth and DII selling; Shah's view was not specified beyond the caution against chasing. The three analysts named different top stocks—Mishra Federal Bank (CMP Rs 373.50, target Rs 390) and Phoenix Mills (Rs 2,285 to Rs 2,590); Jain Apollo Hospitals (Rs 9,200 to Rs 9,800) and Indian Oil Corporation (Rs 150.50 to Rs 162); Shah SRF (Rs 2,515 to Rs 2,750) and HDFC Life (Rs 589 to Rs 650). All recommendations are forward-looking technical calls rather than confirmed outcomes.
items.title: Three Brokers Target Nifty at 26,300 with Divergent Entry Levels and Sector Calls

visual.alt: Bar chart. Mishra (Religare) 26,341; Jain (Motilal Oswal) 26,300; Shah (Asit Mehta) 26,300.

items.summary: A company working for President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner purchased 300 acres of Albanian land for more than $130 million in April to plan a luxury development. However, Albanians living in the area dispute this claim, telling NPR that the land is theirs rather than Kushner's.
items.title: Luxury development planned on land some Albanians say is theirs, not Jared Kushner's

items.summary: On Sunday, November 22 in Barcelona, Diego Simeone reached his 345th LaLiga victory—achieved in a 3-0 win over Getafe during his 567th match—to surpass Luis Aragones as the manager with the most top-flight Spanish league wins. The milestone came 189 matches fewer than those required for Simeone to reach 344, and it marked the first time the record passed from one Atletico Madrid coach to another since Aragones recorded his final LaLiga victory in 2004. Beyond the count of wins, the article notes that other managers have posted higher win percentages and larger trophy collections; Simeone's distinguishing attributes are instead longevity (having managed the club almost 15 years), consistency, and resilience after two Champions League final defeats to Real Madrid—one on penalties and one in extra time following a stoppage-time equaliser. In his own words, Simeone said reaching the record made him happy while acknowledging that 'there is an incredible amount of work behind this.' He also addressed criticism of Atletico as purely defensive, arguing that winning 345 matches cannot be achieved by defending alone. The piece frames these figures and quotes as reported claims rather than established fact, without independent verification.
items.title: Diego Simeone surpasses Luis Aragones with record 345th LaLiga win

items.summary:
A 20-year-old Singaporean named Chloe Chew has overcome osteosarcoma (aggressive bone cancer) that led to the loss of both legs. At 13 in 2017, shortly after completing her Primary School Leaving Examination, she developed a painful lump near her right knee and was diagnosed with the disease; doctors initially offered tumour removal but switched to below-the-knee amputation days before surgery. She spent much of that year hospitalised undergoing chemotherapy and at least seven surgeries to heal an unhealing wound. The cancer recurred in 2019, prompting a September 2020 procedure that removed the remainder of her right leg along with her right hip bone, after which she stayed in intensive care for two weeks.

Chew describes ongoing social and physical challenges tied to using a wheelchair: being overlooked or stared at in crowds on public transport, strangers pushing her wheelchair without permission, rough handling by bus captains during boarding, commuters failing to make space on trains, and unsolicited pressure from others that she says made her question whether something was wrong with her. These experiences contributed to self-doubt and a sense of being overshadowed by her disability while studying digital animation at the Institute of Technical Education.

She enrolled in Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) in 2025, where she reports regaining confidence through art; for one project she reimagined her wheelchair as a car and illustrated herself navigating Singapore to find accessible routes. The illustration was converted into a wheel-cover design among nine designs by five para-athletes displayed at Enabling Village during the upcoming Enabling Lives Festival on November 28–29, 2026. She also earned the Dare to Dream Scholarship for students with disabilities or special education needs facing financial difficulty.

Cancer-free but still occasionally feeling pain where her leg was removed, Chew began para-fencing in August and trains weekly to strengthen her core and wrists while learning to use a sabre; she plans to introduce visitors to the sport at the festival. The account is drawn from CNA Women (Mediacorp), which states it seeks to inform, empower, and inspire women.
items.title: Chloe Chew, a NAFA student who survived bone cancer and two amputations, is rebuilding her identity through art and para-fencing

items.summary:
Singer Miley Cyrus married her partner of four years, drummer Maxx Morando, on 21 November at a ceremony in Palm Springs, California. The event reportedly took place at a resort formerly owned by Frank Sinatra and followed an all-black dress code for guests; photos shared on Instagram showed the couple surrounded by white roses with their mother Trisha Cyrus and sister Noah Cyrus visible in the background.

Cyrus wore a Saint Laurent silk dress designed by Anthony Vaccarello, while Morando attended in a black suit from the same house. The newlyweds appeared alongside a golden retriever in one of the images posted under the caption "M+M" with a white heart and the ceremony date. Guests included Cyrus's sister Brandi Cyrus, singer Doechii, and designer Donatella Versace.

The couple met on a blind date, according to Cyrus's 2023 interview with British Vogue; Morando is a member of the LA-based band Liily. Their engagement was confirmed last year during an interview with Good Morning America, in which Cyrus described being surprised by the proposal that reportedly occurred during a trip to Asia. Morando later told Wonderland he "had to be really sneaky" about keeping the plans secret.

Cyrus previously married actor Liam Hemsworth in 2018 after a decade-long relationship; the couple separated in 2019.
items.title: Miley Cyrus Marries Maxx Morando in Palm Springs Ceremony

items.summary:
COP31 talks in Antalya, Turkey collapsed on Sunday without a political agreement, leaving negotiators to question the future of a three-decade-old process that has led the global fight against climate change. The failure follows weak outcomes at other recent conferences and comes as a U.N. report indicated the world was set to breach the 1.5 C warming threshold (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit). For small, vulnerable countries exposed to rising sea levels and extreme weather linked to carbon emissions, these annual U.N. conferences represent their primary opportunity to draw global attention to their plight and seek financial assistance.

The collapse underscores concerns about reforming a consensus-based system that some argue has lost credibility. Andres Martin Garrido Sanchez of Peru's Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated the process "needs in-depth reforms," while Simon Stiell, the U.N. climate chief, said the system could still function but acknowledged work was needed and announced he had engaged external knowledge leaders to advise on potential reform areas.

A key difference between Antalya and the 2015 Paris agreement—which established an aspiration to limit warming to no more than 1.5 degrees Celsius—was that the U.S. remained engaged in climate diplomacy during Paris, whereas Trump's withdrawal from the process preceded these talks. James Fletcher of CARICOM attributed the lack of a positive outcome partly to the absence of a major power with sufficient gravitas to unite divergent parties.

However, some delegates noted reduced reliance on COPs as renewable energy has become economically compelling rather than requiring multilateral direction. China's clean energy exports alone were projected to help the Global South avoid 257 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions per year once deployed—an amount equal to France's emissions—according to analysis by Lauri Myllyvirta of the Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air. Chris Dodwell of Impax Asset Management observed that COP decisions no longer meaningfully affect investment signals because economics now drive the transition.

Some participants also reframed the failure positively, with Sweden's chief negotiator Mattias Frumerie suggesting big oil producers' attempts to block fossil fuel language reflected accelerating progress and their frustration at the direction of travel. Meanwhile, like-minded governments have pursued smaller coalitions—such as TAFF (which Tuvalu will host next year), the Green Grids Initiative, the Global Methane Pledge, and the Beyond Oil and Gas Alliance—to achieve faster emissions cuts and rally finance initiatives.

The article notes a divergence in views about COP's future: Fiji's climate minister Lynda Tabuya described annual conferences as exhausting and disappointing without movement, while chief negotiator Sivendra Michael argued the consensus-driven process remained vital for maintaining legally binding commitments. The text presents these perspectives as reported statements rather than established conclusions, reflecting ongoing debate over whether reform or restructuring is needed.
items.title: Collapse of COP31 Talks in Antalya Raises Questions About the Future of Climate Diplomacy

items.summary: Despite remaining the fastest-growing major economy with FY27 growth projected above 7% by multiple agencies, India in 2026 confronts two external pressures—rising inflation and a depreciating rupee—that finance ministry officials describe as 'considerable' uncertainties. Growth momentum is expected to moderate from an estimated 7.5% year-on-year in the first half of FY27 to around 7.2% for the full fiscal, per UBS, which cites fading tax impulses, tighter global financial conditions, oil volatility, and monsoon drag; the IMF pegged growth at 7% for both FY27 and FY28 while flagging energy shocks, monetary tightening, AI-cycle adjustments, and El Niño as risks. Inflation rose to a two-year high of 6.09% in October with food inflation at 8.94%, driven by the West Asia war's oil price shock (Brent averaging above $110 versus $72.8 pre-war) and adverse monsoon conditions; Standard Chartered expects retail inflation near 5% in FY27, while EY projects CPI of 5.5-6%. The government responded with fuel duty cuts, scrapping import duties on over 40 petrochemicals, keeping petrol prices unchanged for 78 days (causing Rs 1.23 lakh crore under-recoveries), and supply-side food measures like Kanda Express trains and reduced oil customs duties. Oil prices have since cooled—the Indian crude basket fell from ~$120 to near $90 per barrel—with Brickwork Ratings expecting Brent volatility in the $90-105 range through March 2027, though sustained easing remains uncertain without conflict resolution. The rupee depreciated over 6% during FY27, hitting a record low of 96.85 against the dollar on October 7 amid capital outflows (Rs 2.95 lakh crore withdrawn from equities January-October) and an AI-driven shift toward safer havens; RBI intervention drew reserves down to $591.84 billion by mid-October, though sentiment improved with FIIs buying Rs 84,000 crore in early November and the rupee recovering to a seven-month high of 93.5 on November 17. Standard Chartered projects the rupee ending 2026 near 96 against the dollar and possibly at 99 by December 2027; DBS Bank notes YTD depreciation narrowed to about 4% with relative resilience, while EY's Srivastava attributes pressure partly to India's higher inflation versus other economies. The outlook remains clouded: if oil stays above $100 per barrel and the war continues, fiscal buffers could be limited as subsidy outgo rises (fertiliser subsidies expected at least 33% higher), though a FY27 fiscal deficit target of 4.2% is likely to be met.
items.title: India's Growth Faces a Twin Squeeze from Inflation and the Rupee

items.summary:
The BepiColombo mission, a joint European and Japanese effort costing $2 billion (1.7 billion euros), successfully entered orbit around Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year cruise through the inner solar system. The European Space Agency announced the arrival via social media, with German flight controllers confirming orbital capture several hours later despite their 94 million miles (152 million kilometers) distance from the spacecraft; thruster firings had slowed it enough for Mercury's weak gravity to hold it in orbit. BepiColombo is only the third spacecraft ever to visit Mercury and the first since NASA's Messenger orbited the planet in 2011 before crashing into it in 2015, following flybys by Mariner 10 in the mid-1970s.

The conjoined spacecraft shed their mother ship in September for the final leg of its route. Launched in 2018, BepiColombo reached Mercury via a slower path that included one Earth flyby, two Venus passes, and six Mercury assists, accumulating more than 6 billion miles (10 billion kilometers) traveled.

Lead project scientist Geraint Jones noted the mission will enable comparisons of "unprecedented measurements taken by two spacecraft at the planet at the same time." Once separated next month, ESA's satellite and JAXA's smaller craft will study Mercury's magnetic field, impact craters, volcanic plains, and mountain ridges reaching up to 3 miles (4.8 kilometers) high.

The mission faces significant challenges: surface temperatures can exceed 800 degrees Fahrenheit (427 degrees Celsius), requiring spacecraft cooling as a major technical hurdle. Officials aim to sustain operations for at least one Earth year—equivalent to four Mercury years. Despite its proximity to Earth, Mercury remains among the solar system's least explored planets, surpassed only by Uranus and Neptune in visitation.
items.title: BepiColombo Spacecraft Enters Mercury Orbit After Eight-Year Journey

items.summary: In the midterm elections, US Democrats won at least 258 of the 435-member House seats, gaining 44 from Republicans to achieve their strongest general-election performance since 1992. The final race was decided in North Carolina, where Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Virginia Foxx; four contests remained unresolved as Minnesota and Tennessee awaited results and two Louisiana races moved to December runoffs. This result exceeded the Democrats' gains of 40 seats during Trump's first presidency in 2018, leaving Republicans with no more than 177 seats—one of their smallest delegations in decades—and extending Democratic control into traditional Republican strongholds across the Midwest and East Coast. The wave was attributed to voter frustration over cost of living, the war in Iran, and alleged corruption surrounding the Trump administration.
items.title: US Democrats Secure Largest House Majority in Over Three Decades

visual.alt: Bar chart. Democrats 2018 40 seat; Republicans Midterms (max) 177 seat; Democrats Midterms 258 seat.

items.summary: Artist Philippe Fourtou transformed a site in Morocco into the sculpture park Ramakech, which opened to the public in 2024 after he began altering it in 1999. The park features surreal installations such as "The House Fallen from the Sky," created in 2010 as a tribute to his grandfather; this structure rests on its roof at a 17-degree angle and contains inverted furniture, windows, and bathroom fittings. Other attractions include oversized chairs, tables, notebooks, wardrobes meant to evoke a child's perspective, plus farmers and gardeners with pumpkin- or plant-shaped heads, giant ants around a mud-built structure, and colorful architectural installations. Fourtou stated these human-botanical combinations are intended to provoke curiosity and unease, while the enlarged household objects recreate sensations from his childhood exploring his great-grandmother's home. He described the sculptures as focused on emotions, family relationships, and formative memories rather than nostalgia alone. The park reportedly attracts around 5,000 visitors annually.
items.title: Morocco's Ramakech Sculpture Park Opens to the Public

items.summary: Between 2014 and 2024, the share of U.S. hourly workers paid below $15 in real terms fell by two-thirds, from 38 percent to 13 percent. Researchers Clem Aeppli, Soohyun Roh, and Nathan Wilmers analyzed this decline using panel data drawn from administrative records and job reviews, distinguishing between employer entry and exit (where high-paying employers replace low-paying ones) and organizational changes among incumbent employers—changes that may stem from external constraints like labor market tightness or arise from employers pursuing new opportunities. Contrary to predictions of creative destruction, the researchers found only a small share of wage gains attributable to the disappearance of low-wage organizations; instead, rising pay was driven primarily by low- and middle-paying incumbents in low-wage occupations increasing wages themselves. These increases coincided with tightening labor markets and higher minimum wages, though employers also independently pursued new opportunities for reorganizing work in low-skill jobs despite organizational inertia.
items.title: Increasing pay for lower wage workers

items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Sunday that an overly aggressive Federal Reserve rate hike could harm the economy, coming days after a tech-driven market correction heightened concerns about an impending AI bubble burst. The warning follows traders scaling back expectations of a half-point Fed rate increase on Dec. 9; sentiment was dampened by Anthropic's record-setting IPO and strong but unenthusiastic tech earnings that failed to lift the market. An analyst cited by Reuters suggested some investors fear the Fed may be 'tightening into an economic slowdown when both earnings and AI investment have peaked.' Separately, a Bloomberg columnist argued against treating the current AI boom as unique, pointing to historical technology-driven cycles—railroads, electrification, and the internet—that were followed by busts. The text presents these perspectives as reported claims from Bessent, analysts, and commentators rather than established fact.
items.title: Bessent Warns Fed Overtightening Risk Amid Mounting AI Bubble Fears

items.summary: A series of recent incidents across Europe has raised concerns that the Russia-Ukraine war is becoming more difficult to contain. These events include a drone strike on a Russian cargo ship near Finland, an alleged Moscow-orchestrated assassination plot in Denmark, and Russian missiles landing in Poland. According to an intelligence analyst speaking with NBC News, these actions have drawn European countries closer to direct involvement while remaining "just below the threshold of war," enabling Russia to destabilize the continent without triggering a full-scale confrontation. The escalation occurs against a backdrop of faltering US-led diplomatic efforts; as one Carnegie Endowment expert noted, diplomacy may be stalled because "the likelihood is that cannons will keep doing the talking." All claims regarding these incidents are attributed to their respective sources rather than presented as independently verified fact.
items.title: Escalating Hybrid Attacks Raise Fears That Ukraine War Is Harder to Contain

items.summary: Western Indore is set to receive a new 35-lakh-litre water tank at Hawa Bangla alongside a 22-km distribution pipeline network, forming an Rs 6.31-crore project that will benefit 4,496 domestic tap connections across municipal wards 82, 84, and 85. Mayor Pushyamitra Bhargav performed the 'bhoomipujan' for the work, which is expected to strengthen water supply in colonies including Sudama Nagar's E-Sector (ward 82), New Dwarkapuri Colony up to the 60-feet road (ward 84), and Rishi Vihar Colony with adjoining areas (ward 85). Bhargav stated that ensuring adequate, regular water supply is a priority of the municipal corporation and noted that work on the fourth phase of the Narmada water supply project was progressing rapidly, expected to double the city's existing capacity upon completion. He projected the expanded infrastructure would help meet growing population demand until 2045 while urging residents to adopt water conservation practices amid warnings that below-normal rainfall could cause scarcity in coming months.
items.title: Indore to Build ₹6.31 Crore Water Tank and Pipeline Network for Western Wards

items.summary:
The Supreme Court is set to hear the Bhopal sealing case on Monday, where residents and petitioners in Arera Colony are challenging a report (ATR) submitted by the Bhopal Municipal Corporation (BMC). The core dispute centers on allegations that misleading affidavits were filed before the court regarding the sealing of commercial establishments located in residential areas. Residents contend that shops, hotels, and showrooms across E-1 to E-5 sectors have reopened despite BMC's claims of enforcement action.

The supporting evidence for this case rests on figures attributed to the BMC: it conducted a three-phase drive after issuing notices against commercial activities in residential properties, sealing 348 properties during the final phase following 24-hour notices. Across all three phases, more than 10,000 notices were issued. Residents counter that over 200 residential buildings are being used commercially and that effective enforcement has not occurred.

The residents' challenge specifically targets a BMC affidavit dated Aug 3, 2026, alleging that several establishments remain operational even though they display posters declaring commercial activities have stopped. A stated limitation is that these claims originate from the petitioners themselves; the text does not independently verify whether the alleged reopenings or non-enforcement are accurate.
items.title: Bhopal Arera Colony Sealing Case Reaches Supreme Court Amid Resident Allegations of Non-Enforcement

items.summary:
DTE Energy announced plans to add up to 150 megawatts of new solar generation in Michigan, a move the company says will create construction jobs, support local communities, and reduce customer fuel costs. Because solar does not require purchased fuel, DTE states the projects would lower its exposure to changing fuel prices over their operating lives while supporting reliability, cleanliness, and affordability. The announcement is framed as an investment that brings new tax revenue into Michigan communities for schools, first responders, and other services.

The company stated it is seeking competitive proposals through PowerAdvocate, with a proposal deadline of January 19, 2027, contract execution expected in the second or third quarter of 2027, and commercial operation required by June 30, 2030. Projects must be located in Michigan and connect to either the MISO transmission system or DTE's distribution system. The procurement supports a settlement agreement under Michigan Public Service Commission Case No. U-21662, approved May 15, 2025.

DTE noted it already generates enough wind and solar energy from its renewable portfolio to power nearly one million homes as it works toward net zero carbon emissions while maintaining a balanced resource mix. The company's 2026 Integrated Resource Plan calls for an additional 15 gigawatts of renewable energy by 2042, though the article provides no breakdown of how much would come from solar versus other sources.
items.title: DTE Energy Plans Up to 150 Megawatts of Michigan-Based Solar Generation

items.summary:
For the first time, UK taxpayers held more than £1 trillion in offshore accounts within tax havens, according to data obtained by the TaxWatch thinktank through freedom of information requests. Between 2022 and 2024, balances held offshore rose by 10%, representing the latest available figures from HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC). The list of jurisdictions reflected in the data drew on a framework originally compiled by academics at the EU Tax Observatory and included Hong Kong, Jersey, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, and Panama.

While much of these funds appears to have been declared, large sums remain difficult for authorities to recover. HMRC secured an average of £125m in previously unpaid tax and interest each year from offshore accounts—partly enabled by information exchanged under the Common Reporting Standard (CRS). However, this figure falls well short of earlier estimates: a 2018 snapshot suggested £200m to £700m was going unpaid annually across all offshore accounts. TaxWatch noted that roughly one-fifth of UK taxpayers' offshore accounts were reported through CRS without a unique taxpayer identifier, complicating HMRC's ability to match undeclared accounts to individuals and suggesting the true scale of evasion is likely higher.

In response, HMRC announced measures targeting wealthy taxpayers, including assigning dedicated compliance managers to more than 200 billionaires. The agency estimates these efforts could raise at least £500m toward a broader goal of securing £10bn in additional tax revenues by 2030. HMRC also plans to deploy an additional 400 staff members against wealthy offshore non-compliance by that date.

A key limitation is the reliability and completeness of these figures: MPs questioned HMRC's grasp of compliance among about 1.3 million wealthy taxpayers, and TaxWatch criticized repeated delays in publishing full estimates of unpaid tax on offshore income and gains—hindering independent benchmarking of enforcement effectiveness.
items.title: UK Taxpayers' Offshore Holdings Exceed £1tn for First Time, HMRC Data Shows

items.summary:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepalese PM Balendra Shah will virtually flag off the Saryu-Kamala Express on Monday, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur in Nepal. The train is expected to be a major outcome of Shah's two-day state visit to India—his first bilateral overseas trip since assuming office in March 2026—and his talks are set to focus on expanding cooperation in energy, hydropower, railways, connectivity, and infrastructure.

The Saryu-Kamala Express will begin regular service from November 28, covering the 604-km route between Ayodhya Cantt and Janakpur Dham in approximately 19 hours without requiring passengers to change trains. It departs Ayodhya every Monday at 5:50 pm and reaches Janakpur on Tuesday at 12:40 pm (Nepali time), with the return journey leaving Janakpur Saturday at 1:10 pm and arriving in Ayodhya Sunday at 8:10 am. The service will run weekly, using modern 17-coach LHB rakes comprising eight AC coaches, seven sleeper coaches, one luggage coach, one disabled-friendly coach, and one power car.

The direct rail link is expected to strengthen the Ramayana circuit by connecting Ayodhya—the birthplace of Lord Ram—with Janakpur—associated with Goddess Sita—and boost religious tourism while creating trade, business, and employment opportunities in border regions. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will also participate in the flag-off event.

Beyond the train launch, Modi and Shah are expected to discuss energy cooperation under a long-term power trade agreement through which India has envisaged importing up to 10,000 MW of electricity from Nepal over 10 years; India currently imports around 1,200 MW annually. India is Nepal's largest trade, transit, and investment partner, receiving roughly 80 per cent of the country's goods exports and nearly one-third of its foreign direct investment. Indian companies are involved in hydropower projects such as the 900 MW Arun-3 project under construction, and both countries are exploring a proposed Raxaul-Kathmandu railway link.

The visit occurs against a backdrop of traditionally close ties that experienced some strain in May after Shah called for Chinese and UK involvement in resolving the India-Nepal border dispute over Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura, and Kalapani. New Delhi rejected any third-party role, maintaining an established bilateral mechanism to address the issue.
items.title: India and Nepal Launch Direct Ayodhya–Janakpur Train Amid Broader Bilateral Cooperation Talks

visual.alt: Bar chart. Current annual imports from Nepal 1,200 mw; Long-term target over 10 years 10,000 mw.

items.summary: Rising U.S. oil and gas production, expanding export capacity, and a shift in global trade flows following the war in Iran drove record-high crude, fuels, and LNG exports this year (attributed to Tsvetana Paraskova for Oilprice.com). Over the decade since 2016—when LNG exports began and crude shipments were permitted beyond Canada—the U.S. surpassed Qatar and Australia as the world's largest LNG exporter while exporting more crude than any OPEC producer except Saudi Arabia. Citing Kpler data via Reuters columnist Gavin Maguire, U.S. crude oil exports rose from up to 5% of global volumes in 2018 to up to 15% since then; its LNG share reached about 30% (up from roughly 5% in 2018); and propane market share hit a record 70% year to date. EIA data showed U.S. propane exports reaching 2 million barrels per day in the first half of 2026, up 11% year over year as Middle East supply disruptions affected South Asia, while ethane exports peaked at 794,000 bpd in August. The article notes that further export growth is expected but may not translate into additional market share gains, given rising rival capacity from OPEC+, Brazil, Guyana, and Canada (including a planned new pipeline to boost Asian sales), as well as Qatar's plans for expanded LNG output.
items.title: U.S. Energy Exports Hit Records as Global Competition Intensifies

visual.alt: Bar chart. Crude oil exports (2018) 5 %; Crude oil exports (recent) 15 %; LNG share (2018) 5 %; LNG share (recent months) 30 %; Propane market share (year to date) 70 %.

items.summary: At the FIFA Under-17 World Cup, Egypt secured their first Group A victory by defeating hosts Qatar 2-0 to move into second place in their group. After opening with a loss to Greece, Egypt scored twice within the first 10 minutes and then defended their lead; attacking centre-back Adam Mohamed described the performance as positive but emphasized that protecting the two-goal advantage was essential before their final match against Panama. In Group C, Mozambique recorded its first defeat, losing 2-1 to Argentina in a closely contested game. Forward Alirio Cuna Junior attributed his side's effort to strong mentality and expressed confidence about winning upcoming matches despite conceding the loss. Both Egypt and Mozambique finished second in their respective groups with three points each, though both will require wins in their final group games to improve their qualification prospects.
items.title: Egypt Record First Under-17 World Cup Win as Mozambique Suffer Defeat

items.summary:
Representative Virginia Foxx, an 11-term Republican from North Carolina's 5th district (NC-5), lost her seat in a closely contested election after responding dismissively and with climate disinformation to a letter written by Christian Mango, a 10-year-old constituent. The article reports that Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Foxx by 330 votes following a recount, making it the last decided House race of the election and giving Democrats a 258-seat majority in Congress.

Christian's letter addressed electric vehicles (EVs) and climate change, suggesting EV incentives with a $5,000 tax rebate—lower than the former $7.5k credit but higher than the current federal $0—and noting that EVs can receive energy from any generation method while gas cars rely only on oil. Foxx's response reportedly included six links sourced exclusively from climate-denying outlets (three from Murdoch-owned WSJ and Fox, one each from Washington Times and National Review), none of which concerned EVs.

The article asserts several claims about Foxx's voting record that it attributes to her own statements: she voted against lower-income-targeted EV incentives with MSRP caps on new vehicles, yet the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) had included such provisions for used vehicles; and she was one of 218 Republicans who supported a bill adding $4 trillion to the national debt. The article also claims the IRA reduced the deficit by $238B through enforcement against wealthy tax cheats, though most of it was repealed.

The author interprets Foxx's statement that "YOU and your classmates will be responsible for that debt" as mockery rather than a sincere warning, given her age (83) and the bill's projected impact. The article notes NC-5 swung 19 points to Democrats despite not being one of the redrawn districts, describing gerrymandering efforts by Republicans as having backfired in what analysts called a "Dummymander." It also states Foxx had previously projected a 97% chance of winning before the election.

The article frames these claims with strong editorializing and partisan language (e.g., labeling outlets propaganda, describing Trump's leadership as incompetent), so readers should treat its characterizations—particularly attributions about Foxx's voting record—as sourced assertions rather than neutral facts. The 330-vote margin represents only 0.12% of votes.
items.title: Virginia Foxx Loses NC-5 Seat After Dismissive Letter to Child Constituent on EVs

items.summary:
Former England football captain and UNICEF goodwill ambassador David Beckham praised Heema Ninama, a 17-year-old Bhil community girl from Jhabua district in Madhya Pradesh, for opposing an arranged child marriage and continuing her education. Beckham shared the story on Instagram on November 20, World Children's Day, noting that his two-decade association with UNICEF has shown him girls can lead and make decisions about their lives when given proper support. He credited teachers at Sandipani School in Kalyanpura for counseling Heema's family about the harms of child marriage and the importance of education; her refusal to marry combined with this intervention allowed her to continue schooling, pass Class 11 in the first division, and now study in Class 12 while participating in sports. UNICEF India documented her journey through a short film after visiting Jhabua, and Beckham praised UNICEF's partner organizations for protecting children's rights.

The story drew parallels to the 2002 film 'Bend It Like Beckham.' Madhya Pradesh Women and Child Development Minister Nirmala Bhuria issued a statement on Sunday evening affirming state commitment to ending child marriage through effective implementation of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006. Under that law, the minimum legal age for marriage is 18 for women and 21 for men, with specified offenses carrying up to two years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh. The government reportedly conducts awareness programs through anganwadi centers, schools, communities, and local institutions.

The article contains no stated limitations or caveats beyond attributing claims about Heema's circumstances and the government's actions to officials and news agency Press Trust of India.
items.title: David Beckham Praises Madhya Pradesh Tribal Girl Who Stopped Her Child Marriage

items.summary: The Sri Chandikamba Sametha Someshwara Swamy Temple at Kolanupaka, located about 80 km from Hyderabad and 6 km from Alair on the Warangal highway, is a center of attraction during Karthika Masam and Maha Shivaratri. The presiding deity, Lord Someshwara Swamy, is worshipped as a Swayambhu Lingam believed to have manifested on its own, with Goddess Chandikamba worshipped alongside him. According to tradition, the Veerashaiva saint Jagadguru Sri Renukacharya emerged from the lingam to propagate his faith. The temple complex is described by Yadadri district administration as having been established about 950 years ago during the Chalukya period, though it is believed to date back more than 2,000 years; the Someshwara temple specifically is associated with the Chalukya period. Historically a hub for religious scholarship and community governance, the shrine was reflected in 18 traditional maths or monasteries established around it. Devotees from Karnataka, particularly Veerashaiva Lingayats who revere Sri Renukacharya, visit in large numbers during Karthika Masam, as do visitors from Hyderabad and Secunderabad drawn by the temple's convenient location along the Warangal highway. Ancient inscriptions from the Western Chalukya and Kakatiya periods record royal patronage including grants of land and gold, with a Kakatiya-era inscription linked to the consecration of the Sahasralinga. The presence of the Nyaya Lingam suggests the shrine also served as a judicial center where local disputes were reportedly resolved through oaths administered in the deity's presence. Karthika Masam is considered among the most auspicious periods, with devotees visiting particularly on Mondays to light lamps, perform Shiva pujas, and take part in Sahasralinga rituals.
items.title: Kolanupaka Someshwara Swamy Temple Draws Devotees During Karthika Masam

items.summary: Journalist Paris Marx, in his book Hyperscale, argues that the rapid buildout of hyperscale data centers has become a bipartisan political flashpoint because their physical presence directly affects residents through power bills, water access, noise, and grid strain. He describes touring a facility in New Zealand as highly securitized—requiring advance passport submission and key cards for every door—and characterizing server rooms as utilitarian but extremely loud. Marx contends the buildout is 'fundamentally unsustainable' and 'completely out of line with a livable planet,' driven by tech industry hubris, while noting that promised generative AI benefits have not materialized alongside mounting environmental and social costs. He cites specific community pressures: Google's data centers in Chile contributing to water stress near Santiago; Irish data centers consuming more than 20% of the country's electricity—prompting a 2022 grid moratorium around Dublin before the generative AI surge—and Google using 29% of The Dalles, Oregon's water supply after suppressing disclosure. Marx distinguishes his opposition to hyperscale expansion rather than data centers generally and notes tech companies are shifting from renewable-energy claims toward abstract national water comparisons while pivoting to electricity-intensive closed-loop cooling systems that raise new concerns about coolant leakage. He expresses skepticism that dropping NDAs will meaningfully change outcomes, warns against simply replacing U.S. firms with foreign ones pursuing the same practices, and calls for greater public-sector technology development.
items.title: Paris Marx's 'Hyperscale' Frames Data Center Backlash as Bipartisan and Fundamentally Unsustainable
