items.summary: On Sunday afternoon, a Maruti EECO minivan carrying 10 passengers lost control and crashed into a roadside tree at approximately 4 pm near Musiri, about 350 km south of Chennai, killing eight people and injuring two. The crash occurred while the vehicle was returning to Thirukattupalli in Thanjavur district after attending a relative's ear-piercing ceremony in Namakkal. Police attribute the accident to overspeeding by the driver, identified as Rajesh; five passengers—Manickam, Sangili, Murugan, and Pavadaidied—and the driver died at the scene, while three others (Sakthivel, Subramani, and Seetharaman) later succumbed to their injuries at Musiri Government Hospital. The two remaining survivors are still hospitalized. Deceased bodies were sent for autopsy, and police registered a case under relevant sections before launching an investigation.
items.title: Eight Killed When Overspeeding Minivan Strikes Tree in Tiruchirappalli

items.summary: The article examines the rapidly expanding menopause wellness industry, which PwC projects could reach up to $25bn by 2030 as pharmaceutical companies address previously underserved health needs. The consumer side is growing fastest, with brands marketing products from shower gel to cooling pillows and toothpaste, sometimes at a 'pink tax' premium for standard items rebranded specifically for menopause. Professor Joyce Harper of UCL reviewed more than 200 menopause supplements in a paper published in Climacteric, finding wide variations in ingredients and price with little consensus on efficacy; nearly half contained no vitamin D despite it being the only supplement with sufficient evidence to be recommended by medical experts, just for bone health. The review concluded that supplements are sold 'despite the limited empirical evidence' they work, prompting Harper to warn of a 'menopause gold rush.' Despite her expertise, she acknowledges personal vulnerability to social media hype and does not blame women who buy products at £20 or similar prices. Concerns about 'menowashing'—brands exploiting women's health needs during vulnerable times—are compounded by the fact that midlife coincides with children leaving home, parents dying, job insecurity, and societal dismissal of older women. A Mumsnet survey found 68% believe the NHS does not take women's health seriously and 64% report having been told their symptoms were normal or 'in their head,' while more than half consider the NHS institutionally misogynist; over half said they avoid seeking care because they won't be taken seriously, driving them toward social media influencers who are often paid to promote products. Doctor Xand van Tulleken traces 'Big Menopause' as an industry back to 1990 when HRT-breast cancer fears prompted women to seek herbal remedies like evening primrose oil and black cohosh (later linked to liver damage), a trend social media has since supercharged with celebrities promoting products from creatine powder to collagen. The article notes progress in reducing stigma, though it raises questions about who the market truly serves—some attend events for enjoyment while others pursue genuine health solutions—and highlights that even GenM's MTick certification does not prove efficacy as brands are only required to show evidence of workings when making claims rather than undergoing independent testing by GenM. Harper cautions against relying on supplements due to potential drug interactions and the risk of self-diagnosing symptoms like joint pain or fatigue as menopause-related while missing underlying conditions such as osteoarthritis or thyroid problems, instead recommending lifestyle medicine—exercise, good nutrition, and moderated alcohol intake—as a free first-line defense with robust clinical evidence. The article frames these claims as reported perspectives rather than established fact, noting the scientific jury remains out on many remedies and that placebo effects may explain some perceived benefits from products lacking clinical validation.
items.title: Menopause Wellness Market Growth Amid Concerns Over Exploitation and Lack of Evidence

items.summary:
GL.iNet confirmed on November 20 that an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its GoodCloud remote management platform to install custom malware, backdoors, and root-level reverse shells on customers' routers and KVM devices. The company stated it fixed the cloud flaw and blocked the access path used in the incident, preventing new infections while noting these measures do not remove existing malware from already-compromised devices. GL.iNet did not disclose how attackers exploited the platform, how many customers were affected, or whether data was stolen, though it is investigating potential compromise of computers connected to infected KVMs.

Researchers at RemoteToHome Consulting analyzed 183 routers they own or manage and found suspicious activity on 152 devices: 24 with root-level reverse shells (connecting to IP 170.39.226[.]219 via the Linux nc utility), 47 with an older persistent backdoor, and 81 showing evidence of executed attacker-supplied commands. The researchers cautioned their findings may differ from other customers' devices and that the older backdoor infections might not be linked to the November attacks.

BleepingComputer analyzed a malicious ni.sh script downloaded by a compromised GL-RM1 KVM on November 19, which contacted approximately 1,800 residential IP addresses daily and repeatedly queried the TRON blockchain API—activity suggestive of peer-to-peer networking but unconfirmed as proxy or botnet use. The script recognized multiple GL.iNet models, established persistence through startup scripts and scheduled tasks, disguised its process as crond -i /tmp/.log (matching GL.iNet's indicator of compromise), replaced netstat with a filtering shell script to hide communications from IP 66.245.219[.]252, installed SSH public keys for remote access, and contained Chinese-language developer comments suggesting a Chinese-speaking author.

GL.iNet scheduled stable firmware updates on November 22, recommending version 1.10.3 or later for RM10/RM1/RM1V2/RM1PE/RM4PE, 1.10.3 beta or later for RM10RC, and 1.8.7 or later for RMQ1. The company linked to a community-developed detection tool that checks for known malware files, suspicious processes, modified utilities, and persistence changes, though developers warned it cannot detect every infection and may require firmware reinstallation without settings retention since malicious config-directory files can survive ordinary upgrades.

Some recovered malicious files had timestamps dating to December 2025, suggesting devices may have been compromised for months—though it remains unclear whether these infections involved the same threat actors as the November attacks. GL.iNet plans to notify affected customers via cloud account email addresses.
items.title: GL.iNet Cloud Vulnerability Exploited to Infect Routers and KVM Devices

items.summary: The provided text consists of five reader comments responding to separate articles published in an Indian outlet, with no single unifying event or finding. One commenter from Bandipur describes the effects of a cow slaughter ban during a severe drought year, reporting that villagers face livelihood losses from cattle predation by tigers and leopards as well as care burdens for old, unproductive cattle; abandoned cattle have entered forests where wildlife reportedly suffers due to competition among herbivores over limited fodder and water in degraded forest overrun with invasive species such as lantana and senna. A second commenter recounts a personal connection to the Sassoon company through her father, Leslie Sharps, who worked for it in Shanghai in the 1940s, Hong Kong afterward, Nassau around 1955-56 (about ten months), and London until his retirement circa 1972. A third commenter recalls a year-long anti-scabies campaign conducted during 1979-80 in Poroor village within the forests of north Wayanad's Thavinjal pram panchayat, describing community education on cause, treatment, and prevention using benzyl benzoate lotion (to which potassium permanganate was added for color), procaine penicillin injections, and Cotrimoxazole tablets. A fourth commenter defends a piece on India's Sanskrit-speaking villages as an attempt to belittle interest in Hindu linguistic heritage. The fifth comment criticizes coverage of Netanyahu and Modi over security failures, disputing claims that Modi framed Muslims as a threat while Rahul Gandhi did not congratulate a pilot for bravery out of concern for Muslim voters; it is signed by Suresh Gangwar.
items.title: Reader Comments on Indian Policy and Historical Articles

items.summary: At least 118 children and 12 adults were hospitalized after suspected food poisoning from eating chow mein at a fair in Hiri village, under the Kirnapur police station limits of Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat district. The incident occurred on Saturday evening, when several visitors reportedly complained of vomiting, diarrhea, and dizziness after consuming the noodles. Chief Medical and Health Officer Dr Shatrughan Singh Dahiya reported that 45 children and all 12 adults were transferred from Kirnapur Community Health Centre to the district hospital for further treatment, while the remaining 73 children received primary care and were discharged; he stated all patients remained in stable condition. Local administration seized the suspected food stalls and sent samples for laboratory analysis as an investigation into possible contamination proceeded.
items.title: Madhya Pradesh: Suspected Food Poisoning After Chow Mein at Balaghat Fair

items.summary: In Rajasthan's Tonk district, residents of Ward 4 in the Peeplu Panchayat Samiti allege that nearly 50 LED street lights installed on electricity poles across Kumharon Ki Dhani, Begampura, Hanifganj, and Bijalpura villages were removed following an election defeat. The lights had been put up ahead of panchayat elections at what residents claim was the behest of Alok Sharma, personal assistant to Niwai BJP MLA Ramsahay Verma; Sharma's wife, Priyanka Sharma, lost her contest for Panchayat Samiti member from Ward 4. Residents say removal began soon after results were declared, prompting suspicions of a political vendetta. A Fault Repair Team (FRT) from Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited (JVVNL) arrived to remove the lights, citing unauthorised electricity connections, and removed them from around 10 poles in Kumharon Ki Dhani despite protests; work was halted at approximately 40 other poles after newly elected sarpanches reportedly agreed to pay the bills. JVVNL Executive Engineer DR Meena stated that FRT staff noticed the lights while addressing electrical faults, an inspection found they were connected without authorisation, and the department has ordered an inquiry into who installed them and how the connections were made. Verma denied any political motive, stating candidates had installed the lights ahead of Diwali and that JVVNL intervened after unpaid bills surfaced; he confirmed the sarpanches agreed to clear the outstanding amounts.
items.title: Rajasthan Villagers Alleging Political Vendetta After Street Lights Removed Following BJP Candidate's Election Loss

items.summary: Senior Congress MP Shashi Tharoor posted a video on his official YouTube channel in which he played the newly released Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) for the first time, using the session to make political commentary. During what he described as his gaming debut — noting that his household had been centred on reading rather than screens and that he needed staff assistance with the PlayStation controller — Tharoor joked about the franchise's title before drawing a pointed parallel to the Narendra Modi government's 2016 demonetisation, calling it 'a grand theft without auto.' He also candidly admitted difficulty navigating the game, stating he was merely trying to stay alive and that nothing about its fictional Leonida setting or criminal storyline appealed to him. Beyond personal commentary, Tharoor raised a broader question about India's gaming ecosystem, observing how readily Indian players embrace foreign settings while questioning whether indigenous titles could achieve similar global appeal.
items.title: Congress MP Tharoor Plays GTA VI While Digging at Demonetisation

items.summary: A Japanese government-sponsored ceremony held Sunday in Naha marked the completion of restoration work on the Seiden main hall of Shuri Castle, which was damaged in a fire in 2019. The restored hall will open to the public starting Monday. Reconstruction incorporated findings from research conducted since the previous 1992 restoration and has been designed to more faithfully reflect the building's original appearance; fire safety measures were also strengthened during the work. The ceremony was attended by Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara, Yasuhiro Hanashi (minister for Okinawa and Northern Territories affairs), and Okinawa Governor Genta Koja.
items.title: Shuri Castle's Seiden Main Hall Restoration Completed After 2019 Fire

items.summary:
Following the November 3 midterm elections, a historic Democratic victory in both chambers of Congress coincides with reported declines in coverage of President Donald Trump across major U.S. media outlets. Journalism professor Margaret Sullivan (Columbia University) states that 'the media's love affair with Trump is over,' while Lachlan Murdoch acknowledged Fox News' reduced viewership to 'viewer fatigue.' Jeff Jarvis (City University of New York) added that public exhaustion from covering Trump has already passed, though he warned legacy outlets like The Post and The Times would maintain a neutral stance rather than acknowledge what he characterized as an established threat. This shift follows years of Trump's attacks on the press—suing both The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal, threatening broadcast licenses, barring news outlets from the White House—and his efforts to push the media rightward through allies including Elon Musk (X), Jeff Bezos (Washington Post), and the Ellison family. A Wall Street Journal investigation analyzing 70,000 hours of MAGA podcasts found that mentions of Trump per hour had fallen sharply in recent months since the start of a war with Iran. The article notes these are largely anecdotal claims about declining coverage rather than comprehensive ratings data; Sullivan and Jarvis themselves expressed skepticism that Washington's media will substantially change its strategy despite the Democratic 'blue tsunami.'

The Democrats' new majorities carry specific legislative constraints on their agenda against Trump administration figures. They have pledged to remove White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, initiate impeachment proceedings against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth (a prior attempt failed last week), and investigate alleged corruption involving Trump's family and administration. However, restoring $1.1 billion in funding cut from NPR and PBS would require a two-thirds majority that Democrats do not hold to override presidential vetoes.

The Voice of America situation remains unresolved amid disputes over staffing and operations. Approximately 1,000 VoA staffers remain dismissed but continue receiving salaries while awaiting resolution of their lawsuit against the Trump administration; multiple courts have ruled in their favor, including a unanimous November 10 decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit that deemed the dismissals illegal and ordered reinstatement of Director Michael Abramowitz. Seven VoA subsidiaries broadcasting in languages such as Farsi, Urdu, and Ukrainian have resumed operations while others await decisions on returning or accepting permanent dismissal.

Public trust figures cited include a Gallup finding that only 32% of Americans trust the media—a slight improvement from last year's low of 28%. The article concludes by noting Trump both hates yet remains obsessed with the press, which struggles to reconcile covering what many regard as an exceptionally mendacious president with reporting on his statements because he is the U.S. president.
items.title: Declining Trump Coverage and the Democrats' Midterm Victory Reshape Washington's Media Landscape

items.summary:
Nepalese Prime Minister Balen Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday evening for his first official visit since assuming office in March, at the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The little over a day-long trip was set to conclude Monday after talks with Modi, during which officials from both countries planned to take stock of India-Nepal relations and discuss regional and international matters of mutual interest.

The agenda reportedly centered on several concrete initiatives: a $2 billion economic package proposed by Kathmandu (including $1 billion in grants) aimed at development projects and rebuilding areas damaged by recent flash floods; an Indian-proposed joint vision document covering economic cooperation, investment, transit, energy, digital connectivity, and healthcare—expected to be unveiled during the visit with formal adoption proposed at its conclusion; and emerging areas of cooperation such as startups, technology, innovation, sports, energy, and connectivity. The $2 billion figure was cited in reports referencing people familiar with the matter rather than confirmed by either government.

Shah traveled accompanied by Foreign Affairs Minister Shishir Khanal, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Chief Advisor Kumar Byanjankar, and other senior officials. Beyond Modi, he was scheduled to meet External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and President Droupadi Murmu during his stay in India.

The visit is framed as part of broader efforts to reset and strengthen bilateral ties through long-term cooperation with specific sectoral targets.
items.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah's First Official Visit to India Focuses on Economic Package and Bilateral Reset

items.summary: Nearly 50 LED street lights were reportedly installed on electricity poles across four villages in the Ranoli Gram Panchayat of Peeplu Panchayat Samiti, Ward 4, in Rajasthan's Tonk district. Villagers allege that Alok Sharma, personal assistant to Niwai MLA Ramsahay Verma, arranged the installation ahead of Diwali, and that removal began after BJP candidate Priyanka Sharma—Sharma's wife—lost her election from Ward 4. The JVVNL Fault Repair Team arrived during routine fault visits and found the connections unauthorized; per Executive Engineer DR Meena, officials inspected and confirmed illegality before initiating removal. Around 10 poles were cleared in Kumharon Ki Dhani amid resident opposition, while removal of approximately 40 other poles was halted after newly elected sarpanches agreed to pay the electricity bills—consistent with Verma's account that installation predated the election and removal followed billing issues rather than any electoral motive. Verma denied a political vendetta, attributing the action solely to unauthorized connections and outstanding bills; an inquiry has been assigned to establish who installed the lights and whether the connections were illegal.
items.title: Rajasthan Tonk: Street lights installed by MLA's aide removed after his wife's poll defeat

The text argues that Rocky Mountain Institute (RMI) has made genuine analytical corrections in its hydrogen research but continues to recommend public spending on markets the evidence suggests are uneconomical. RMI matters because governments, investors, and industrial companies rely on its work for funding decisions.

On battery versus hydrogen trucks: RMI's February 2026 report finds fuel-cell trucks do not reach ownership-cost parity with battery-electric trucks through 2040 in the baseline case (including long-haul), though an alternative sensitivity explores a more favorable hydrogen price. The NACFE Run on Less study, developed within RMI's freight research ecosystem, projects batteries as lowest cost across modelled duty cycles by 2035 without incentives, with hydrogen remaining most expensive nearly everywhere.

On Europe: RMI's March 2025 recalibration cut expected mandate-driven renewable hydrogen demand in 2030 to 2.2–2.8 million tons, far below the EU's original 20-million-ton supply-and-import target. It identifies €13.9 billion in public support under existing mandates plus €31.7 billion for an accelerated scenario (€45.6 billion combined).

On ammonia: RMI's November 2026 European assessment models on-site green hydrogen ammonia at approximately €1,222 per ton versus €745–755 per ton for qualifying imported green ammonia.

RMI's China report acknowledges green production costs remain two to three times conventional and that demand lags supply ambitions. The text notes RMI already makes appropriate distinctions elsewhere—separating hydrogen used to reduce iron ore from process-heat hydrogen (850 GWh electric heat versus 1,300 GWh for equivalent heating via additional hydrogen) and the Green Ammonia Buyers Alliance replacing existing fossil-derived ammonia.

The core critique: RMI's diagnosis has improved but its guiding policy remains overcommitted to expanding hydrogen markets. Using Richard Rumelt's framework, the author states RMI's diagnosis is better while its guiding policy stays too committed to market expansion with some coherent actions missing. The text calls for explicit alternative-technology comparisons, investment thresholds and exit criteria in recommendations.

The assessment is attributed to TFIE Strategy Briefing (a CleanTechnica publication), which examines RMI's US, India, Europe and China reports side by side. Limitations include that the ammonia figures are modelled values rather than supplier bids.
items.title: RMI's Hydrogen Research Is Improving While Its Investment Advice Still Falls Short

items.summary: At the COSM Technology Summit 2026 in Scottsdale, Arizona, former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger rejected the claim that chip scaling has hit a physical barrier. Speaking at a fireside chat titled 'Reality Check: Beyond Chips' with technology theorist George Gilder and Heritage Foundation director Bret Swanson, he argued that AI's accelerating needs require roughly a 10,000x increase in computing efficiency rather than incremental generational gains. He maintained that reviving Moore's Law depends on breakthroughs across five engineering fronts—light, power, cooling, composition, and packaging—and posted afterward on X: 'Is Moore's Law dead? I say it's time to wake it up!' Gelsinger warned that gradual chip improvements are insufficient amid severe power bottlenecks. He cited sluggish US grid growth of only low single-digit capacity expansion over the past decade, eight-year supply backlogs for new gas turbines, and a decade-long construction timeline for nuclear projects as obstacles to hyperscale data centers. As context for rising electricity demand, he pointed to NVIDIA's Kyber racks using Blackwell NVL72 architecture, which push power requirements to 600kW per unit. Acknowledging skepticism from industry watchers that traditional Moore's Law scaling has run its course, Gelsinger insisted semiconductor engineering is entering a multi-disciplinary breakthrough era and backed his optimism with recent venture investments: he joined Playground Global as a general partner in March 2025 and funded xLight to push past ASML's 13.5nm extreme ultraviolet wavelength barrier and Alva Energy for nuclear capacity. All claims, figures—including the 600kW power demand and 13.5nm threshold—and projections are attributed solely to Gelsinger or his stated sources; no independent verification is provided in the text.
items.title: Former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger Argues AI Demand Requires a 10,000x Efficiency Leap and Reviving Moore's Law

items.summary:
A New York Times report citing multiple US intelligence sources alleges that Alice Huang maintained contact with an official of China's top intelligence agency from spring 2025 through autumn 2026, a period overlapping at least part of her relationship with Jensen Huang, who stepped down as Nvidia CEO earlier this month. The findings also indicate that Kang Wei, introduced to associates as Huang's husband and her business partner in Megaspeed, worked with the same intelligence agency.

The report states these revelations provide new details on US officials' concerns that Jensen Huang may have been targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation, coinciding with investigations into a network of Southeast Asian companies suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of export controls. Intelligence agencies reportedly gathered evidence including shipping records showing some acquired chips went to data centers serving firms such as Alibaba while others were smuggled into China.

The report further alleges Huang met officials from China's Ministry of Public Security and that her wider network, including her sister and associated companies, has been linked to supplying advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese state-owned military contractors working for the People's Liberation Army. A confidential memorandum dated March 30 written by Secretary of State Marco Rubio outlined these alleged links.

The report notes US intelligence agencies monitored Huang's contacts for more than a year, with Trump advisers informing the president on at least two occasions about her alleged connections while he led Nvidia; Trump reportedly declined to intervene and publicly backed Jensen Huang's return. A CIA briefing by Director John Ratcliffe saw lawmakers raise questions about the affair, though a follow-up national security briefing was postponed.

The report is attributed entirely to NYT reporting citing unnamed sources, with no response obtained from the White House, State Department, Chinese Embassy in Washington, or the individuals involved.
items.title: NYT Report Details Alice Huang's Alleged Ongoing Contact with Chinese Intelligence During Jensen Huang Nvidia Tenure

items.summary: Ahead of the Federal Reserve's December 9, 2026 policy meeting, billionaire investor Bill Ackman is arguing that another rate hike would risk triggering a recession in both the US and global economies. His warning comes as financial conditions tighten across debt and equity markets: with the S&P 500 down 11.6% from its October peak, corporate borrowing costs have surged—Ackman cites SpaceX raising secured debt financing at an 8.259% interest rate versus below 6% for its unsecured bond offering at IPO—and falling stock prices have made equity capital more expensive to raise.
items.title: Bill Ackman Urges Fed to Abandon 2% Inflation Target Ahead of December FOMC Meeting

items.summary:
In an interview with Fox News, US spy chief Jay Clayton confirmed that investigations into Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and her company Megaspeed are ongoing. These probes relate to allegations that the company was part of a network supplying Nvidia-powered servers to Chinese customers through Southeast Asia. Clayton stated that both personal and corporate investigations were progressing alongside regulatory proceedings, and he indicated that Nvidia's board would likely examine the matter as well.

The confirmation follows Jensen Huang's resignation on November 12 amid reports of an alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by US intelligence agencies of having links to Chinese intelligence. While Jensen Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, Nvidia stated it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

A Wall Street Journal report detailed the alleged role of Chinese national Li Ming in a network supplying computing capacity to Chinese customers through Southeast Asia. Singapore prosecutors charged him and others with fraud in February 2025 over transshipment of servers containing Nvidia chips, though Megaspeed was not named in those charges. The WSJ reported that Li worked with Alice Huang and her husband Kang Wei to establish the partner network across Southeast Asia.

The report alleged some servers were transferred to Shanghai-based Century Litong in violation of US export controls, prompting Nvidia to place Megaspeed on an internal 'no sell' list in June 2025. A separate New York Times report stated Alice Huang remained in contact with a Chinese state security official for over a year (spring 2025 to autumn 2026) during her alleged affair, and that Kang Wei also worked with the same agency.

The investigations remain based on allegations; Nvidia maintains Megaspeed's business was legitimate. The extent and timing of both individuals' contacts with Chinese intelligence had not been previously reported by these outlets.
items.title: US Spy Chief Confirms Investigations Into Alice Huang's Megaspeed Amid Nvidia Controversy

items.summary: When Notable Capital (formerly GGV Capital) invested roughly $100 million—about 10% of the U.S. portion of its over-$1 billion fund—into Anthropic's Series E, limited partners were initially puzzled by the bet given that Claude trailed OpenAI and DeepSeek's R1 had recently challenged closed-source rivals; at a $61.5 billion valuation it was also Notable's largest-ever investment in 25 years. The firm backed the deal after its team found developers increasingly favoring Claude (70% of usage versus ChatGPT, up from the prior year) and concluded that mission-critical work would require U.S.-based closed-source models. Anthropic then raised $81.3 billion in what was described as history's largest IPO, reaching a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion before trading began—a paper return of roughly 15 times for Notable. Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC made its first investment after meeting CFO Krishna Rao at Che Fico restaurant in early 2025 and seeing evidence that model improvements were driving enterprise adoption; it invested across Series F ($183 billion valuation), a later round led alongside Coatue at $380 billion, and the pre-IPO round at $965 billion—more than $4.5 billion total for roughly 1% of Anthropic post-IPO. Baillie Gifford's Lilian Li began studying Anthropic nearly two years before its Series F investment, citing consistent execution, strong revenue, and compelling gross margins; the firm invested a total of $1.5 billion across three rounds.
items.title: Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford's Early Anthropic Bets Realized Large Paper Returns After Its Record IPO

items.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India faces mounting pressure at its December 2026 Monetary Policy Committee meeting after October CPI inflation rose to 6.09 per cent, breaching the upper tolerance band under the new data series for the first time and pushing food inflation to 8.94 per cent amid El Niño and deficient monsoons, while core inflation reached 4.5 per cent. The RBI already responded at its October meeting by raising the repo rate 25 basis points to 5.50 per cent—the first increase in four years—shifting stance to "calibrated tightening" with a balanced corridor (SDF at 5.25 per cent, MSF at 5.75 per cent). Because inflation exceeds the policy rate even against RBI's own forecast of roughly 5.8 per cent over three quarters, the real policy rate remains negative; closing this gap is central to December.

The article argues that macroeconomic risks compound the case for a firmer stance: bank credit growth at ~19.5 per cent versus deposits at ~16.9 per cent year-on-year raises fears of demand-driven price pressures, while external conditions remain fragile after FPIs earlier withdrew nearly $30 billion (rupee near 97) before recovering with November inflows of $9-12 billion and reserves stabilising around $720 billion—though this depends on unresolved long-term capital gains tax policy. Global monetary conditions add risk, as the US Fed rate sits at 3.75-4.00 per cent and elevated Treasury yields (10-year near or above 5 per cent) narrow India's yield advantage over its ~7.25 per cent bond market.

The author contends that fiscal policy must complement monetary tightening by avoiding demand-side subsidies, instead improving food distribution efficiency, releasing buffer stocks during spikes, prioritising productive capital expenditure, and stabilising the deficit to keep yields steady; most expect a further 25 bps hike to 5.75 per cent in December, with larger hikes possible if November inflation stays high. The core thesis is that the exact size of the hike matters less than the hawkish message, since negative real rates are dangerous and decisive action backed by clear fiscal policy will keep this breach temporary—though the author concedes it remains too early to determine whether peak rates reach 6.25 or 6.50 per cent.
items.title: India's Inflation Breach: Why the RBI Can't Afford a Timid December

visual.alt: Bar chart. CPI, Oct 2026 6.09 %; CPI, Sep 2026 5.54 %; Food inflation (Oct) 8.94 %; Core inflation (ex food & fuel) 4.5 %; Repo rate 5.5 %.

items.summary: The vivo Watch GT 2 is scheduled to launch in India on November 26, marking the company's entry into the country's smartwatch market. The device features a large display, health tracking capabilities, and battery life described as lasting several days, alongside a design that resembles watches from Apple's lineup. However, this text provides no feature-by-feature comparison between the vivo Watch GT 2 and an 'Apple Watch Series 12'—a model name not referenced in vivo's product details—and poses only open questions about whether the two devices share features or how they compare overall. The source does not present any factual data on specifications, pricing, or performance differences; it functions as a teaser rather than delivering substantive information.
items.title: vivo Watch GT 2 Set for November 26 India Debut Amid Comparison with Apple Watch

items.summary: In this episode of the Headstart On Record podcast, hosts See Kai Wen and Sue-Ann Tan explore whether colleagues can be trusted as friends and how to set boundaries between workplace relationships and close personal friendships. The discussion addresses several questions: the potential downsides of mixing work and personal life; whether a close friendship with one's supervisor is appropriate; why office friend groups often resemble toxic secondary school cliques, described in the episode title as involving 'office snakes, cliques and gossip'; and which topics are best kept private at work. The conversation also weighs both sides—examining risks to privacy alongside the benefits of genuine workplace connections versus mere cordial co-worker relationships. Listeners were directed to Headstart's recent survey on work friendships for additional context. No quantitative data or specific findings from that survey were included in this episode summary.
items.title: Headstart On Record Podcast Examines Trust and Boundaries in Workplace Friendships

items.summary: According to sources cited by Reuters, China's securities watchdog (CSRC) has informed law firms that red-chip companies established after the 2023 offshore listing rules must be re-domiciled in mainland China before they can list abroad. Red-chip firms are registered overseas—often in tax havens—but control Chinese assets through equity or contractual arrangements, a structure favored by tech start-ups seeking capital under Hong Kong's more relaxed rules and larger foreign investor pools. The CSRC did not immediately respond to the request for comment, and sources declined identification because the guidance was confidential. Oversight of these structures has tightened since March 2023; before that date, overseas holding structures required no regulatory approval. In March this year, the CSRC told Reuters it was examining the necessity and compliance of red-chip structures formed after March 2023, and most applicants failed to justify their structure as necessary, prompting the stricter stance. The move is expected to dent Hong Kong's IPO market: funds raised via Hong Kong IPOs in the first 10 months of 2026 surged 84% from the same period in 2025 to HK$404 billion (S$66 billion), though CSRC approvals have slowed since September amid scrutiny of AI, chip, and humanoid robot firms. In 2025, one-fifth of the 131 Hong Kong listings approved by the CSRC involved offshore holdings—mostly red-chip structures—and so far in 2026 only six red-chip companies received approval versus 50 in 2025; nearly 600 listing applications were pending at end-October. Firms like AI company StepFun are reportedly shifting domicile back to China ahead of planned overseas listings, and the Hong Kong exchange said it welcomes issuers with varied ownership structures provided they meet applicable requirements.
items.title: China's CSRC to Require Red-Chip Firms to Re-Domicile in Mainland Before Offshore Listings

items.summary: The Tech Policy Press newsletter dated November 22, 2026, authored by Justin Hendrix, surveys a range of AI governance topics centered on the Anthropic IPO. At its Nasdaq debut amid demonstrations demanding regulation of AI systems, mitigation of environmental and labor impacts, and no bailout for Big Tech if an AI bubble bursts, Anthropic's corporate governance structure was described as unusually complicated, with analysts noting that rivals have developed elaborate oversight mechanisms after OpenAI previously failed to keep a fired CEO dismissed. Separately, the S&P 500 entered correction territory on concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom; Mark MacCarthy and David Klaus attributed this month's market decline to investor recognition of AI overinvestment rather than fear of regulation, arguing that political backlash against data centers might force a necessary slowdown in growth as oversupply became evident. The newsletter also covered platform labor issues through two podcasts—one featuring Tech Policy Press fellow Lam Le on Asian platform workers gathered in Bangkok and another with Yale's Julián Posada on Venezuelan AI training data labeling—and digital democracy concerns, including NYU and Knight-Georgetown research finding that AI can provide accurate election information but often does not, plus a Center for Democracy & Technology argument that social media bans for young people function as censorship. On regulation, the newsletter reported an EU case against TikTok over harmful rabbit holes, Brazil's race to pass its first law targeting Big Tech before a new Congress (which could set precedent among BRICS countries), and warnings from Amnesty International about establishing clear binding rules. Regarding personal AI agents released by OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Google, Microsoft, and xAI since mid-2026, George Colville warned of potential gatekeeper dominance while Brett Frischmann and Bruce Schneier cautioned that governments should act now on data minimization before surveillance becomes the internet's business model. The newsletter noted global costs of US tech influence through protests against Pax Silica in Manila during Trump's ASEAN Summit visit—raising questions about whether it constitutes sound industrial policy for the Philippines—and a Microsoft outage exposing UK critical digital infrastructure vulnerabilities despite an NHS Palantir contract extension to 2029. Additional items included a field experiment finding Google AI Overviews cut outbound clicks to publishers by approximately 40% with no measurable user satisfaction gain, proposals anchoring Britain's AI assurance industry through the AI Security Institute, congressional staffing shortfalls limiting tech oversight (with staff at just over half of early-1990s peaks), critiques of AI hype and rights assignment for machines, an EU Frontex plan that civil society groups warn could weaken DSA safeguards against government overreach, concerns about platforms using privacy claims to hinder protections, a cataloging of terms like Bugmageddon describing the AI bug/patch flood, hiring announcements, reading list nominations, and Knight-Georgetown resources on agentic information futures. The newsletter is presented as reporting from various contributors and fellows rather than as authoritative analysis.
items.title: Tech Policy Press Newsletter Reviews Big Tech Governance, Market Concerns, and Global Pushback

items.summary: Congress leader Ajay Rai on Sunday criticised Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya for his comments regarding the slogans 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Radhe Radhe', accusing him of having a 'perverted mindset' for removing Goddess Sita's name from what was traditionally phrased as 'Jai Siya Ram'. Rai stated that no one has objection to the original wording, but noted that BJP supporters have gone further by dropping the reference to Mother Sita. Maurya had taken aim at Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav over the BJP's slogan 'Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De' (May the lotus bloom), asserting in a post on X that SP leaders were previously uneasy hearing 'Jai Shri Ram' and are now troubled by 'Radhe Radhe'. He argued that both slogans would continue to resonate in Uttar Pradesh—where 'Jai Shri Ram' is common in Ayodhya and 'Radhe Radhe' in Braj—and accused the SP of appeasement politics, claiming its chances of returning to power in the 2027 Assembly elections were dashing and that the BJP would form the government again. The exchange followed Yadav's Saturday remarks at a press conference in Lucknow, where he mocked the slogan coined after the BJP's two-day meeting in Mathura, suggesting 'Radhe Radhe'—traditionally said during farewells—signalled that the BJP was being shown the door by voters. In response to Maurya on Sunday, Yadav declined an invitation to his home while welcoming reporters, and accused the BJP of selectively invoking religious sentiments, stating his party opposed controversial remarks about Hindu deities rather than 'katha' (religious discourses), citing past BJP comments about Lord Ram's father and Lord Krishna. The reported statements are attributed to Rai, Maurya, and Yadav as presented in the source text.
items.title: Congress Leader Ajay Rai Criticises UP Deputy CM Maurya Over 'Jai Shri Ram' Slogan Remarks

items.summary: On Sunday, during the three-day Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi (November 20–22), India held bilateral talks with Iran focused on cultural cooperation. Union culture secretary Vivek Aggarwal confirmed the engagement at Purana Quila, noting that India and Iran remained 'in constant touch' on potential areas of cultural exchange and that discussions occurred during the summit; however, he stated no specific project had been finalised. Separately, the Iranian Embassy in India reported via a post on X that Tehran proposed establishing an 'SCO Joint Network for Written Heritage and Civilisational Memory,' which would focus on preserving and digitising manuscripts, exchanging technical expertise, providing manuscript-restoration training, and promoting shared linguistic and literary heritage through joint research, publications, and exhibitions. Cultural Counsellor Dr Faridoddin Faridasr addressed the forum's first session, emphasising Persian as a historical language of science and literature across Central Asia and the Indian subcontinent, citing the Noor International Microfilm Centre—affiliated with the Iranian Embassy in New Delhi—as an existing example of cooperation; since 1990, that centre reportedly collaborated with 72 academic and cultural institutions in India to digitise more than 150,000 Persian and Arabic manuscripts, restore over three million pages of historical documents, and prepare nearly 300 catalogues. The article's candidate readings corroborate the figures '72 academic,' '150,000 Persian,' and '300 catalogues.' Because Aggarwal stated no project had been concretised and the manuscript statistics are attributed to the Iranian Embassy rather than independently verified, these claims should be treated as reported assertions. The forum was organised by India's Ministry of Culture and Ministry of External Affairs and inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 20.
items.title: India and Iran held bilateral cultural talks on the sidelines of the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum

items.summary: Former Bachelor star Sam Wood is seeking mediation in his domestic violence proceedings after being charged with allegedly strangling his wife, Snezana. The 46-year-old Melbourne-based fitness influencer has been in custody since his arrest during a family holiday in Noosa on 3 October and did not appear at Maroochydore magistrates court on Monday when his lawyer Brad Hill requested a two-week adjournment to allow for justice mediation with the prosecution's consent. His bail application, heard by Justice David Boddice following appeals from two lower courts that denied him release, was reserved after Wood played an October 30 phone call in which he told his father Andrew that "there is no way she would want this" and suggested that if Snezana changed her statement the police "would not have a leg to stand on." Justice Boddice characterized these remarks as classic interfering with witnesses. In denying bail, Justice Patrick McCafferty described how Wood allegedly shut a door between himself and Snezana while they were with their daughter Eve Markoski-Wood, then grabbed his wife by the throat against a wall until she could no longer breathe or call for help; it was also alleged he told them both that they could die. The matter has been adjourned to 7 December, during which Wood remains in custody.
items.title: Sam Wood Seeks Mediation Amid Domestic Violence Charges for Allegedly Strangling His Wife

items.summary:
Widely shared footage from Saturday showing masked immigration agents detaining a father, Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, and his daughter Sofia Hernandez Mejia on the jet bridge as they boarded an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles prompted protests inside and around Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. The incident occurred during a busy travel weekend ahead of Thanksgiving; ICE stated it gave no advance notice of the enforcement action, which delayed the flight while officers struggled with someone on the ground.

According to ICE's statement, Mendoza overstayed his visa as an immigrant from Mexico, and Mejia "hurled hot coffee on the officers," for which she could face charges of assaulting a federal officer. The Port of Seattle said it was working with Alaska Airlines to determine whether protocols were followed and would engage federal officials.

The detained pair's lawyer, Olia Catala, disputed ICE's account, stating they had lived in the US since 2015, sought asylum, held no criminal record, and that Mejia had married a US citizen. She described the confrontation as chaotic, noting the officers wore unmarked clothing and that Mejia likely dropped her coffee during the commotion.

The video drew condemnation from Washington Democratic governor Bob Ferguson, who called ICE's tactics "deeply un-American" and pledged to urge airlines to remove ICE from SeaTac airports; Seattle mayor Katie Wilson similarly condemned the actions as "unacceptable and un-American." The article notes that ICE has increased airport operations since summer amid a shift toward targeted enforcement.

The report presents conflicting accounts of the incident, with no independent verification provided for either version.
items.title: Viral Video of ICE Detaining Father and Daughter at Seattle Airport Sparks Protests

items.summary: The Victorian Liberal party confirmed that a statement on the death of music journalist, broadcaster and producer Molly Meldrum—attributed to opposition leader Jess Wilson—was written using artificial intelligence. Meldrum died at age 83 shortly before the statement was issued, in which Wilson described him as “a true Australian icon who will never be forgotten.” When submitted to AI-detector service Pangram, the 177-word statement registered as 100% AI-authored; Pangram states its algorithm misidentifies human text only about one time in every 10,000. A Liberal party spokesperson told Guardian Australia that the party used search and AI to compile research on Meldrum’s career and draft the statement, noting it was then fact-checked and edited by a team member before Wilson approved the final version. The initial AI-generated draft reportedly omitted references to Meldrum’s time on Hey Hey It's Saturday and his two Moomba festival crowns as “king of Melbourne,” which were added afterward.
items.title: Victorian Liberal Party Confirms AI-Generated Tribute to Molly Meldrum

items.summary: On Sunday (Nov 22), drones struck two ships off the port city of Benghazi in eastern Libya—one confirmed to be carrying a Russian flag and another reportedly sailing under a Maltese flag—without an immediate claim of responsibility. Libyan authorities reported that all crew members were rescued and treated for minor injuries, while Alhadath television stated that naval and air force units intercepted more than 12 'explosive-laden sea drones' off Benghazi. The UN mission in Libya (UNSMIL) expressed 'serious concern,' calling on Monday (Nov 23) for an immediate, independent, and transparent investigation, warning that 'Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts.'
items.title: UN Calls for Probe After Drone Attacks on Ships Off Libya, Including a Russian Vessel

items.summary: On Monday, US stock futures rose while authorities moved to stabilize sliding markets in Asia following a sharp selloff last week in the tech and chip stocks central to the AI boom. Nasdaq 100 futures bounced nearly 3% in early trade and S&P 500 futures climbed about 2%, even as Taiwan's benchmark steadied after its largest weekly fall since 1990, South Korean shares dipped roughly 4% before finding support, Japanese markets showed selling pressure despite a holiday closure, and Hong Kong and China hit new multi-month lows. The selloff followed last week's 10% Nasdaq decline—its worst since the March 2020 pandemic panic—and raised questions about whether heavily borrowed capital spent on AI data centres will generate sufficient returns to justify current valuations. Government responses included South Korea's finance minister preparing a press conference on a potential market stabilisation fund, Taiwan's financial regulator tightening short-selling rules, and China easing margin financing requirements. The downturn was intensified by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure and Anthropic's faltering debut, which closed 8.5% lower on its first full trading day. Analyst Damien Boey of Wilson Asset Management noted that while US markets spent three sessions in 'panic' territory last week—a pattern that can sometimes signal a bottom—there may be insufficient momentum for a durable recovery without a central bank policy pivot to catalyze renewed risk appetite.
items.title: US Stock Futures Bounce as AI Rout Rattles Asian Markets

visual.alt: Bar chart. Nasdaq 100 Futures 3 %; S&P 500 Futures 2 %; South Korean Shares 4 %.

items.summary: On November 23, South Korean Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il projected that the country's economy could sustain growth in the upper-3 per cent range next year if current trends persist. He attributed this outlook to robust exports and investment gradually spilling over into domestic demand, with consumer inflation expected to ease as global oil prices stabilize. However, Lee cautioned that both upside and downside risks remain, flagging severe external threats including regulatory uncertainty around artificial intelligence, geopolitical instability, rising global interest rates, and volatility in the semiconductor sector—which he warned could amplify broader macroeconomic swings. The projections reflect Lee's assessment of present economic conditions rather than confirmed outcomes; his forecast is contingent on trends continuing as expected and remains subject to these noted risks.
items.title: South Korea's Finance Minister Projects Upper-3% Growth for 2025 Amid Chip Volatility Concerns

items.summary: Two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal has agreed to terms on a nine-year contract worth $450 million with the New York Mets, according to multiple reports from Sunday. The deal carries an average annual value of $50 million and would set records for pitchers: it surpasses the $43.3 million annual value of contracts held by Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander as a record for pitcher earnings, while also becoming the richest contract in MLB history overall, exceeding Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal signed with the Dodgers in 2024.
items.title: Tarik Skubal Agrees to Record Nine-Year, $450 Million Deal with New York Mets

visual.alt: Bar chart. Skubal (Mets, 9 years) 450,000,000 $; Yamamoto (Dodgers, 12 years) 325,000,000 $; Scherzer / Verlander annual value 43,300,000 $.

items.summary: The city of Hiroshima and eight bus operators have formed what is described as Japan's first public-private partnership to jointly operate fixed-route local bus services. The initiative, now in its second year, has begun a three-month pilot program launched in October that includes trial operations of new routes and expanded service on existing routes across three areas of the city. Results from this pilot are intended to inform plans for a broader restructuring of the network. The source frames these efforts as an expansion of ongoing work rather than presenting definitive outcomes or measurable results, which have not yet been reported.
items.title: Hiroshima Launches Japan's First Public-Private Partnership for Fixed-Route Bus Services

items.summary: Tata Steel's board approved the acquisition of a 26.4% stake in APL Apollo Tubes, part of an effort to strengthen its downstream business and increase exposure to value-added products. The move follows hours after Tata Group companies agreed to sell their tubes business and Tata Steel Colours to APL Apollo Tubes in slump sale transactions valued at up to Rs 28,000 crore. Separately, the second tranche of share acquisition involves 3.33 crore shares (11.90% of expanded voting capital) via off-market transfer, while a third tranche of 1.28 crore shares (4.57%) is expected to complete on or before March 31, 2028; both tranches are subject to conditions under the share purchase agreement and necessary regulatory approvals. Tata Steel's board also approved a mandatory open offer to acquire up to 26% of APL Apollo Tubes' expanded voting share capital from public shareholders, covering 7.28 crore equity shares at Rs 2,301.40 apiece for maximum consideration of approximately Rs 16,755.66 crore assuming full acceptance. If fully subscribed, Tata Steel's maximum shareholding could rise to 52.38%, making it a promoter of APL Apollo Tubes following the transaction and open offer. The conglomerate stated the acquisition aims to strengthen its downstream platform by adding value-added products; APL Apollo Tubes has a portfolio of 14 brands and more than 5,000 stock-keeping units (SKUs). Tata Steel said the deal is expected to increase its downstream integration from around 35% to approximately 53%, improving value addition and product mix. The acquisition remains subject to applicable regulatory approvals in India and other jurisdictions where required.
items.title: Tata Steel Board Approves Acquisition of APL Apollo Tubes Stake

visual.alt: Bar chart. Second tranche 11.9 %; Third tranche 4.57 %.

items.summary: Energy prices are forecast to rise by 26% for millions of UK homes in January, driven primarily by a surge in the unit price of gas under Ofgem's price cap and suppliers' fixed deals. Because these mechanisms set a limit on per-unit cost rather than total bills, consumers pay according to usage, prompting experts to suggest practical measures: reducing boiler flow temperature, disabling pre-heat facilities, lowering thermostats (with 18C cited as the recommended minimum), closing curtains at night, and turning off heating before April. Payment methods also affect costs; Ofgem reports roughly five million people still pay quarterly by credit rather than monthly direct debit, which typically saves about £138 annually through more accurate meter readings or smart meters. Switching to a fixed-rate tariff locks in per-unit prices but carries uncertainty given forecast volatility and potential exit fees, so consumer groups Which? and MoneySavingExpert advise comparing all deals before committing. Financial support is available for many households: the government will provide £100 to homes in council tax bands A to D in England (with equivalent aid expected in Scotland and Wales), plus £150 off electricity bills for those on means-tested benefits, alongside Cold Weather Payments, winter fuel payments, hardship grants, and debt repayment schemes. The article notes that support eligibility varies by region—for example, Scottish benefit recipients must contact their supplier directly—and warns of scams impersonating official money-off programs.
items.title: UK Energy Bills Forecast to Rise 26% in January

items.summary: According to StockEdge's technical scan data, seven stocks in the Nifty 500 index gained more than 1% and had their closing prices cross above their respective 200-day moving averages (DMA) on November 20, 2026. The text notes that traders use the 200-day DMA as a key indicator for assessing overall trend direction; when a stock's price remains above this average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an uptrend. However, these are technical signals rather than confirmed fundamental outcomes: the stocks' future performance depends on whether their prices continue to stay above the 200-day DMA over time.
items.title: Seven Nifty 500 Stocks Cross Above Their 200-Day Moving Averages

items.summary:
On Sunday, thousands of people marched through the Besiktas neighbourhood of Istanbul to protest a widening crackdown on opposition voices and independent media. The demonstration was organised by Yeni Parti, the main opposition party, following police raids on Sozcu TV that installed a government-appointed trustee and arrested senior staff members. This marked the third such takeover in a year, after similar moves against Tele1, Halk TV (Turkey's most-watched news channel), and digital outlet T24.

Protesters carried banners demanding freedom of thought, press, and for journalists while chanting through Istanbul; several voiced concern over narrowing space for voices critical of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. A 64-year-old protester named Tunay said opposition channels had been silenced and that all freedoms were at risk, while another demonstrator, Koksal (also 64), described a period in which democratic rights have disappeared and journalists are being forced to rely on social media—which authorities he claimed they too are shutting down.

The crackdown fits into broader pressure on press freedom over the past decade through prosecutions, digital censorship, and accusations of spreading "fake news." Over the previous two months, Turkey arrested several journalists covering a multi-billion-dollar investment fund scandal, with at least two remaining in pre-trial detention. According to figures from MLSA media rights group, 25 journalists are currently behind bars in Turkey.
items.title: Thousands Rally in Istanbul Against Turkey's Crackdown on Opposition and Independent Media

items.summary: Cricket NSW has declined a request from expansion-side NRL club the Perth Bears to play a trial match at North Sydney Oval, effectively ending their hopes of staging a pre-season game there. Cricket officials denied the venue's availability on scheduling grounds: an NRL fixture would have left the ground unusable for cricket for at least five weeks. The decision prevents the Bears' planned use of the facility ahead of the season.
items.title: Cricket NSW Rejects Perth Bears NRL Trial Match Request

items.summary: Victoria Police announced they had found the body of a man who disappeared after jumping into the Yarra River in Melbourne's CBD on Sunday. Witnesses reported that the 26-year-old began struggling in the water around 11:45am when he and another man, aged 30, jumped from Princes Bridge beside Flinders Street Station; the second man reportedly made his own way out of the water while the first did not resurface after a bystander attempted to help. Police and the SES searched a large section of the river near Southbank, Crown Casino, Federation Square, and Birrarung Marr parkland for much of Sunday and into the evening before resuming the search on Monday. Just after 1pm on Monday, police announced they had recovered a body on the north-east side of the river near Federation Square, which is believed to be the man who jumped in but has not yet been formally identified. The death is not being treated as suspicious, and police will prepare a report for the coroner.
items.title: Police Recover Body of Man Who Jumped Into Melbourne's Yarra River

items.summary:
The International Film Festival of India, currently underway in Goa, features three titles centered on the impact of dementia: Shruti Sharanyam's Malayalam-language Ottanjaavalmaram (A Lone Jamun Tree), Lance Hammer's Queen At Sea, and Welf Reinhart's German-language A Fading Man. According to festival coverage, each film examines different dimensions of living with the illness.

Ottanjaavalmaram follows Maya (Beena R Chandran), a woman whose descent into dementia produces confusion about the present alongside memories of some traumatic past; she is cared for by Simi and behaves more calmly toward her nephew Appu and old friend Elsa. The screenplay reportedly captures details familiar to those who care for dementia patients, including sudden lapses into clarity, imaginary conversations with absent people, an inability to distinguish days, and aggression stemming from frustration over dependency.

Queen At Sea portrays Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) at an advanced stage of the illness, whose second husband Martin continues behavior that is no longer possible given her incapacity to consent or recognize his daughter Amanda. Lance Hammer reportedly explores aspects rarely acknowledged in dementia narratives—bodily autonomy, treatment assumptions, and questions of consent—with a recurring stair-climbing image noted as a visual motif.

A Fading Man places an ex-husband Kurt (Harald Krassnitzer), who suffers from dementia and has no memory of his divorce, back into the home of Hanne (Dagmar Manzel) and her husband Bernd. Coverage indicates the film takes a largely soothing approach despite the disruption caused by Kurt's return but slackens after he moves in with Hanna, reportedly failing to adequately probe Hanna's perspective as she is forced to accommodate him.

The coverage notes that A Fading Man was criticized for not sufficiently acknowledging Hanne's point of view once Kurt returns, representing a limitation in how deeply the film examines her experience.
items.title: Three IFFI Titles Explore Dementia's Impact on Patients and Carers

items.summary:
Despite a rebound in US futures, Asian equities opened cautiously on Monday amid lingering fears of an AI-driven selloff. The S&P 500 Index rose 1.9% and the Nasdaq 100 Index climbed 2.6%, while Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc., among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI trade, fell in early trading; South Korea's Kospi dropped 2.6%. Australia edged lower, and Japanese markets were closed for a holiday.

JPMorgan analysts attributed the recent pullback to an AI de-leveraging event amid weak sentiment and expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve reaction function, while maintaining their view that the AI supercycle remains durable due to lower leverage. Goldman Sachs' trading desk described last week's selloff as an opportunity to buy US stocks but cautioned that investor positioning remained elevated, suggesting broader capitulation may be needed for a meaningful rally.

The rout broadened into risk-off sentiment: MSCI's Asia Pacific gauge fell about 18% from its June peak and sits near bear-market territory. Brent crude declined 0.8% to around $91.80 a barrel, while spot gold rallied 1.1% to roughly $3,575 an ounce after five straight days of losses.

Asian authorities stepped up intervention efforts over the weekend: China eased minimum margin requirements for borrowed funds; Taiwan widened short-selling curbs and began buying shares after its benchmark posted its worst weekly drop in 35 years; South Korea will ease daily limits on share buybacks for three months and prepare to activate a stabilization fund last used during the 2008 financial crisis. Economists expect US October inflation, measured by the personal consumption expenditures price index, to have risen 3.8% year-over-year per a Bloomberg survey median estimate, with figures due Wednesday in a Thanksgiving-shortened week.

The article notes that Friday's rout, driven by unwinding of AI-led growth bets, prompted traders to lower December rate-hike expectations as investors flocked into Treasuries; US Treasury futures also declined. However, the text does not provide data on whether these interventions or policy measures will effectively restore confidence.
items.title: Asian Shares Cautious as AI Selloff Fears Persist Despite US Futures Rebound

visual.alt: Bar chart. S&P 500 Index 1.9 %; Nasdaq 100 Index 2.6 %; Kospi (South Korea) 2.6 %; Brent Crude 0.8 %.
