In May 2025, amid an Indian crackdown on 'Bangladeshi migrants' following the Pahalgam terror attack, Amin's family was among roughly 40 Rohingya flown to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands before being forced off a navy vessel into the sea toward Myanmar; his parents were never returned. India is not a signatory to UN refugee law or protocols and maintains that existing foreigner laws suffice. On economic grounds, Amin reported struggling to earn enough for rent of Rs 5,000–6,000 per month, sometimes skipping meals. Sabber Kyaw Min of the Rohingya Human Rights Initiative cited an estimated 22,000 Rohingya refugees in India as of latest figures. Amin's family had secured U.S. visas through UN resettlement but were blocked after Donald Trump took office in January 2025 and imposed travel restrictions; he also noted that Indian courts dismissed petitions against the deportations, with one bench calling it a 'beautifully crafted story.' The account reflects one refugee's perspective on India's policies and does not represent verified official statistics or comprehensive coverage of all Rohingya experiences.
items.title: Rohingya Refugee Hopes ICJ Genocide Verdict Will Improve India's Treatment of Refugees

visual.alt: Bar chart. Rohingya killed by Myanmar military operations 10,000 rohingya; Rohingya fled to Bangladesh (at least) 40 rohingya.

items.summary: Companies active in alternative energy and related technology have criticized the European Union for plans to reduce the size of the European Competitiveness Fund as part of a broader budget cut. A group representing 75 companies and industry associations, including France's EDF, argued via a letter that the fund is essential for European businesses to compete with China and the United States in key industries (Reuters). At the end of last week, Antonio Costa, president of the European Council, proposed cutting the bloc's budget by €40 billion (~$44 billion) for 2028-2034 from an earlier Irish presidency proposal. However, compared to the European Commission's original budget proposal, Costa's version would shrink the budget by a much larger €180.6 billion (Reuters). The debate centers on competitiveness: critics blame EU-level energy policies for higher costs that undermine industry, while supporters argue accelerating the transition from hydrocarbons to low-carbon electricity could enhance competitiveness. The European Parliament also opposed the cuts; chief budget negotiator Siegfried Muresan called the proposal unacceptable and stated it cannot form the basis for consent, describing the EU budget as an investment budget rather than a strategy of repeated cuts (Reuters). In response, the energy company group insisted on boosting the fund by €26.6 billion to support industrial decarbonization and accelerated buildout of wind, solar, and battery storage.
items.title: EU Green Energy Giants Slam €40 Billion Budget Cut

items.summary:
The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, concluded two days after its scheduled end without reaching an agreement on the cover text. The primary sticking point was the omission of fossil fuels from draft texts; Saudi Arabia and Russia blocked any reference to them, while Australia and Turkey proposed dropping fossil fuel language in exchange for support for electrification with maximum clean energy use. This compromise drew backlash from the European Union along with Panama, the Marshall Islands, Vanuatu, and Belize, who rejected the cover text. The EU led a revolt that shattered the consensus needed to adopt the Turkish-Australian-proposed text.

The article notes this rejection does not signal an end to the COP process or the Paris Agreement, as these texts are non-binding political add-ons rather than formal requirements. However, it may indicate international climate cooperation will look different going forward. Fossil fuels remained unmentionable in official outcomes despite being explicitly addressed three years earlier at COP28 in Dubai with a transition-away commitment.

In response to the deadlock, Brazil launched a global fossil fuel phase-out roadmap outside the formal agenda that attracted support from India, Germany, and Nigeria, while EU member states are developing similar roadmaps. Frustration is likely to drive more nations toward informal channels: 57 nations attended a first conference on transitioning away from fossil fuels in Santa Marta, Colombia earlier this year, with another meeting planned for next year co-hosted by Tuvalu and Ireland.

Leadership figures avoided fossil fuel commitments—Turkish President Erdoğan announced two new Turkish oilfields while Australian PM Albanese made no commitment to halt new coal and gas projects. Both leaders emphasized the "35 by 35" electrification pledge, aiming to raise electricity's share of final energy use from about 23% currently to 35% by 2035; more than 75 countries and 180 businesses signed on outside official negotiations.

As an "implementation COP," the summit focused on existing pledges. Developed nations called for faster emissions cuts while developing nations cited insufficient financial support, with African countries stressing that implementation is meaningless without actual resources from rich nations. Progress was achieved in supporting a just transition via a phased approach and improving alignment in climate adaptation, but broader efforts on the Global Goal on Adaptation remained unresolved.

On finance, EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra had warned talks were "dead in the water" before the summit; no concrete progress occurred toward tripling adaptation funds pledged at COP30. Australia flagged boosting the Pacific climate fund, which ended A$450 million short of its $749 million 2026 target after rich nations merely re-announced existing pledges. The most notable pledge came from Solomon Islands PM Matthew Wale's commitment of $600,000 to the Green Climate Fund.

Climate science was unusually prominent; a small bloc of fossil fuel-producing countries obstructed IPCC report publication, and this marked the first UN summit since confirmation that the world will overshoot 1.5°C by 2030. With cover text support collapsing, statements supporting release of latest climate science were not approved—only technical conclusions expressing concern about increasing impacts remained.

Australia oversaw negotiations as president between 195 countries and the EU; Climate Minister Chris Bowen declared Australia had left "nothing on the field" after facing unbridgeable red lines. Outgoing UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres blamed powerful fossil fuel interests, while some nations called for reform of voting processes—though any such change would itself require consensus.

The article frames the collapse as potentially a catalyst rather than pure failure: former UN climate chief Christiana Figueres characterized more than 130 countries' refusal to sign an inadequate deal as "a sign of courage".
items.title: COP31 Climate Summit Ends Without a Global Agreement

items.summary: A family of smooth-coated otters (Lutrogale perspicillata), a species listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, is being spotted increasingly along Kuala Lumpur's Klang River, raising hopes that years of water-quality improvements are restoring urban wildlife habitat. The river was once one of the world's most polluted waterways, rated Class 5 (severely polluted) under Malaysia's ranking system; cleanup efforts have since improved it to Class 3 (moderately polluted). Malaysian wildlife ecologist Woo Chee Yoong attributed the otters' return to this improvement and noted that their presence indicates a functioning food web—where otters are found, fish exist, which signals a clean and healthy river. However, several details remain uncertain: experts do not know how many otter groups exist or how they move through the city, whether these animals have genuinely returned versus having been hidden in less visible urban environments before 2019 (when Woo first learned of them via local media), or why their numbers appear to be growing. To address this gap, MON—the conservation group co-founded by Woo—hopes to establish a citizen science system for reporting sightings.
items.title: Smooth-coated otters resurging along Kuala Lumpur's Klang River signal river cleanup progress

items.summary:
A post-midterm survey conducted by Precision Strategies and data firm Tunnl, titled Beyond the Manosphere: The Vote Moved Together. The Culture Didn't — examined American attitudes two years after what has been called the 'manosphere election.' The report found that Joe Rogan remains the most trusted media figure among men even as their electoral leanings shifted toward Democrats. Forty-nine percent of men said they trust Rogan, including 41% of Democratic-identifying men, a higher share than any other individual polled; no single person earned more than 22% of women's trust. Tunnl attributed part of this dynamic to the finding that 63% of men reported having no male role models in their lives, and noted that Rogan's longform interview format has inspired imitators ranging from Theo Von to the U.S. military.

The survey also found partisan divisions on media regulation: half of Republicans (51% of men, 50% of women) support government restriction of access for outlets deemed biased, while a slight majority of the overall population prioritized press access. On partisanship broadly, Americans — particularly Gen Z — shifted toward Democrats without developing lasting party loyalty amid ongoing economic concerns about job losses and financial hardship; 45% of men under age 30 identified as independents despite this Democratic swing.

The report also indicated growing weariness with certain MAGA cultural initiatives: only 16% of men and 11% of women said the Trump administration's anti-DEI efforts helped them, while most reported no difference. On gender roles, just 13% of women and 19% of men expressed a desire for more full-time homemakers — an incentive the Trump administration has pursued.

On AI usage, about one-fifth of respondents said they had used AI chatbots for companionship at higher rates among younger Americans; Asian, Black, and Hispanic respondents reported using AI more often than white Americans. Tunnl's Brent Seaborn characterized the landscape as shifting toward understanding who people trust rather than only what they believe.
items.title: Post-Midterms Report Finds Joe Rogan Remains Most Trusted Media Figure Among Men Despite Democratic Electoral Shift

items.summary:
Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has issued open tenders under Contract Package ORE/01 to procure renewable energy from an Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS)-connected project combining solar photovoltaic generation with a co-located Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). The tender follows a competitive bidding process, including an electronic reverse auction conducted online through the Central Public Procurement (CPP) e-tendering portal. A selected developer must complete the project within 15 months of receiving the Letter of Award and meet technical and financial qualification requirements set in the Request for Selection document.

The tender specifies a non-refundable tender document fee of ₹20,000 excluding GST, payable via RTGS, NEFT or IMPS. Bidders must also submit an Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) of ₹23.9 crore as tender security, either electronically through the same payment channels from their own bank account—or for joint ventures/consortiums from a constituent member's account—or as an original Bank Guarantee or Fixed Deposit Receipt valid for at least 45 days beyond the 120-day tender validity period (extending to May 3, 2027).

The schedule runs through December 2026: tender document sale opened November 19 and closes December 10; pre-bid meeting registration by November 25 with the meeting held November 26 at Metro Bhawan's seventh-floor conference room (A Wing); clarification requests due November 27, with addenda issued by December 1. Online bid submission opens December 3 and closes December 10, coinciding with physical EMD delivery to the Senior General Manager (Contracts) office; technical bids open December 11 at 3:00 PM.

Bidders must register on the CPP portal using a valid Class-II or Class-III digital signature certificate issued to an authorised signatory. Financial bid opening and e-Reverse Auction dates will be announced separately for technically qualified bidders, with deviations from RfS conditions potentially resulting in rejection.
items.title: DMRC Invites Bids for ISTS-Connected Solar Project with Battery Storage

visual.alt: Bar chart. Tender Document Fee 20,000 ₹; Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) / Tender Security 239,000,000 ₹.

items.summary: Record-setting volatility in global equities, triggered by the US$119.5 billion (S$154 billion) initial public offering of Anthropic, has clouded the outlook for share sales by China's artificial intelligence leaders—DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and StepFun—who are competitors to Claude maker Anthropic but whose plans do not depend solely on its stock performance. The faltering global AI trade is adding complexity to these highly anticipated listings, with timing and pricing potentially affected by a shifting regulatory environment and steep losses from earlier deals. Anthropic's listing became the catalyst for a broad sell-off across Asian markets; in China specifically, what once made tech giants among the world's most sought-after stocks has turned into a US$1.7 trillion rout as IPO pace slowed and former standouts like Z.AI and CXMT struggled. The overall Chinese IPO market has abated amid volatility, with both the China Securities Regulatory Commission and Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission urging banks and intermediaries to improve deal quality. Meanwhile, AI fundraising helped lift Hong Kong first-time share-sale proceeds to a six-year high of US$52.3 billion in 2026—the second-best year on record—keeping 2010's peak of US$57.8 billion within reach. Evidence of how quickly AI enthusiasm can reverse includes Z.AI, which plunged more than 85% from its June peak after soaring roughly 2,000% in under six months before listing in Hong Kong in January; MiniMax broke below issue price in November; and Anthropic itself surged 17% above offer price on debut to reach a US$1.8 trillion fully diluted market value before falling 8.5% the next day amid what became the MSCI All Country World Index's longest losing streak since September 2023. Despite fluctuations, having the market leader traded publicly—possibly followed by OpenAI in 2027—could help other model makers set benchmarks and align reporting standards for recurring revenue, per Kieron Poon of Aberdeen Investments. Regulatory signals include reports that the China Securities Regulatory Commission gave informal instructions to investment banks about pausing IPOs in November. On specific deals, Moonshot (developer of Kimi K3) closed a final private round at roughly US$50 billion valuation and is heading toward a Hong Kong IPO in Q1 seeking up to US$5 billion; DeepSeek eyes an early-2027 listing after nearly securing 80 billion yuan (S$15.4 billion), above its initial 50 billion yuan target; Infinigence AI filed confidentially for a first-half Hong Kong listing; and StepFun is considering raising about US$500 million. Thea Jamison of Change Global Investment cautioned that IPO fervor in China/Hong Kong is unlikely to return until market sentiment improves, though she expects Moonshot's IPO—already in the works—to be the most anticipated AI name near term.
items.title: China's AI IPO Wave Clouded by Global Sell-off After Anthropic Record Listing

visual.alt: Dot chart. Z.AI rise from offer price, Jan 2026 2,000 %; Z.AI fall from June peak (post-listing) 85 %; Anthropic rise above offer price on debut day 17 %; Anthropic fall from peak on second trading day 8.5 %.

items.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and director on Nov 12, reportedly over personal relationships with security implications, leaving the company led by interim CFO Colette Kress while a permanent successor is sought. The departure prompted analysis of how dependent listed companies—especially founder-led or family-owned firms—are on charismatic leaders who may become unavailable unexpectedly. Huang had at least 60 executives reporting directly to him with no publicly identified successor, raising questions about board oversight when authority and institutional knowledge concentrated in one person.
items.title: Singapore Governance Protections Amid Nvidia Founder-CEO Departure

items.summary: Vyoma.AI, a data centre company within the L&T Group, has secured a multi-year deal with an inference infrastructure provider to deploy additional NVIDIA B300 GPUs at its Chennai Data Centre. The transaction is being executed through Vyoma.AI's subsidiary, LTN Compute. While the specific value and GPU count remain undisclosed by the company, the deal falls into a large category valued between ₹2,500 crore and ₹5,000 crore. The deployed GPUs will power the inference infrastructure provider's AI-native platform to train, fine-tune, and deploy specialised AI models for high-performance commercial-scale inference. This deployment is part of Vyoma.AI's integrated AI Factory in Chennai, which combines hyperscale data centre infrastructure, accelerated computing, high-performance networking, ultra-low-latency interconnects, high-throughput parallel storage, and comprehensive AI operations. The factory is being developed as a gigawatt-scale hub with Phase 1 designed for 250 MW. S N Subrahmanyan, Chairman & Managing Director of Larsen& Toubro, stated that the additional GPU deployment marks another milestone in L&T's vision to build world-class AI infrastructure in India and strengthen its position as a leading next-generation computing hub. The article was published on November 23, 2026.
items.title: Vyoma.AI Secures Large Deal to Deploy NVIDIA B300 GPUs at Chennai Data Centre

items.summary:
Following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation—attributed to an extramarital affair with a company executive and a relationship with a woman whom US intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy—the Trump administration has sought accountability from Nvidia over its chip sales to China. On Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS's "Face the Nation" that the government had contacted Nvidia's temporary management, lead directors, and lawyers, stating it needed answers about the company's compliance culture after Huang left. Reports of these relationships triggered Huang's resignation along with investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal review, and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit.

Bessent emphasized that officials wanted to determine who held responsibility for compliance oversight: "We do need to see who was in charge of compliance there... Was it at the lower levels? Was it at the middle level? Did it go all the board level?" He expressed confidence that Nvidia's board would provide thorough answers and said, "I think we have to see where the buck stops."

Separately, Trump announced on Friday his desire for Huang to apologize and return to Nvidia; Bessent declined to endorse this without more information.

The article notes a prior policy action: days after Huang's resignation, the administration issued a rule restricting China's access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia, tightening controls ahead of Trump's trip to China last week for talks with President Xi Jinping. The reporting is attributed to Reuters.
items.title: US Treasury Secretary Seeks Answers on Nvidia's China Chip Sales After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: Meta has published a detailed report on TLX (Triton Low-Level Extensions), an extension to the Triton compiler that exposes warp groups, barriers, TMA, clusters, and optional layouts to Python kernels. It is not a new language but adds orchestration control—what Meta calls the MIMW model—to ordinary Triton code, targeting NVIDIA Hopper (H100) and Blackwell (B200, GB200), plus AMD MI300 and MI350-series GPUs. The extension is MIT-licensed and ships in Meta's facebookexperimental/triton fork as well as a triton-utlx plugin on PyPI that loads into upstream Triton without forking it; AMD has also published a GEMM-plus-activation guide using TLX with CDNA4.
items.title: Meta Publishes TLX: A Triton Extension for Warp-Group GPU Control on Hopper, Blackwell, and AMD GPUs

items.summary: An increasing number of older drivers are using Tesla's Full-Self-Driving (FSD) system to extend their time behind the wheel, even as safety experts question whether the technology is being over-sold. Joan Spalding, an 89-year-old in Colorado who previously suffered a serious crash while making a left turn, now relies on FSD for her steep, winding commute and says it lets her live independently at home rather than relocating. Her son Mike encouraged the purchase after testing the system himself. Tesla reports that FSD has more than 1.7 million active subscriptions, up 67% from the prior year, though the company does not disclose how many subscribers are seniors or whether it tracks their age. Safety experts caution against complacency: Bryan Reimer of MIT says he would not drive with the system due to safety gaps and notes Tesla has 'continually over-promised and under-delivered,' while Alexandra Mueller of the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety warns that older drivers may lack the ability to take control in an emergency if they grow too reliant on the technology. The company claims FSD is up to nine times safer than human driving, but Reimer says these figures cannot be independently verified given Tesla's limited data disclosure; he also emphasizes that 'full self-driving' remains supervised and requires constant driver attention. Elon Musk has publicly endorsed senior use of the system, reposting a viral video—viewed more than 3.5 million times—of 98-year-old Larry Dimmock praising his Tesla as flawless over several months.
items.title: Seniors Embrace Tesla Automated Driving Despite Safety Concerns

items.summary:
At a Data Users Conference organised by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said on Monday that revisions to India's Consumer Price Index (CPI) series are expected to narrow the disconnect between measured and perceived inflation. The revised CPI, released in February 2026, uses consumption weights from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey of 2023-24 instead of the older 2011-12 survey, reflecting changes in household spending amid rising incomes; food and beverages now carry a lower weight while non-food items have increased. Gupta said these revisions should narrow the disconnect between measured and perceived inflation and add value to monetary policy under India's inflation targeting framework.

The revised series incorporates several methodological changes: it excludes free Public Distribution System (PDS) items so that the index better captures prices actually paid by households, improves handling of missing data for seasonal items, and excludes employer-provided and government accommodation from house rent following Pay Commission revisions while extending rural coverage. For the first time, prices are collected from 12 online markets to reflect growing online consumption. Dissemination is more granular now, with item-level indices released separately for rural, urban and combined sectors as well as for all states and Union Territories.

Gupta said that because food prices have historically been more volatile, the lower weight on food should make headline inflation less volatile and reduce uncertainty in monetary policy. She also noted improvements to GDP estimates through double deflation for manufacturing and agriculture, wider use of surveys and administrative data, and a supply-use table framework; nominal GDP from demand and supply sides is now closer aligned while the real-terms gap has narrowed, though she acknowledged a small residual gap may persist because the two sides are deflated differently. On the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), higher weights for technology- and consumption-oriented sectors such as motor vehicles, pharmaceuticals and electronics, along with lower weights for refined petroleum products, basic metals and mining, should better capture changing industrial dynamics.

The statements describe expected outcomes rather than measured results; Gupta characterised these revisions as improvements to be realised through the updated series. Separately, she explained that RBI's economic assessment relies on high-frequency indicators because official data lag, incorporates global trends and international agency forecasts, and validates alternative big data against official statistics before use, noting such data has limitations including noise, short time series and lack of representativeness.
items.title: RBI Deputy Governor Says Revised CPI Series Should Narrow Gap Between Measured and Perceived Inflation

items.summary: Samsung began rolling out its One UI 9.5 beta to Galaxy S26 users in select regions, introducing several changes aimed at giving device owners more control over personal information, content sharing, and storage management. Among the additions are new ways to protect data: an application lock that lets users secure individual apps without depending on Secure Folder, alongside updates to existing Samsung features for safeguarding personal information. The update also adds a method for transferring content between compatible devices and introduces interactive options for lock screen wallpapers. These changes reflect Samsung's stated goal of improving everyday usability rather than only refining established functionality.
items.title: Samsung One UI 9.5 Beta Adds Application Locking, New Sharing Method, and Interactive Wallpapers

items.summary: A causal evaluation of Tamil Nadu's First-Generation Graduate Scholarship (FGGS), a tuition waiver for undergraduate technical education introduced in 2010, finds that targeting students from households with no prior college graduate raised degree completion among first-generation youth. Eligibility required that no household member had previously completed college and was independent of caste, income, religion, and gender; by January 2021 more than 2.2 million students had benefited at an annual cost estimated at roughly 10–16% of the state's higher-education budget. Using repeated nationally representative surveys with a difference-in-differences design comparing Tamil Nadu first-generation youth to those in neighbouring Karnataka and Kerala, plus synthetic comparisons from other states, Annadurai and Sahoo (2026) estimate that technical enrolment rose by about 3.7 percentage points and degree completion increased by roughly 3.6 percentage points among eligible students—implying the programme raised both entry and graduation rather than merely attracting additional entrants. The authors note a back-of-the-envelope cost of approximately INR 22,280 (US$315 at an exchange rate of INR 70.64 per dollar) per additional technical enrolee. Effects extended into the labour market: among first-generation adults aged 25–29, regular salaried employment increased by about 4.3 percentage points with a shift toward services and associate-professional occupations, though the share seeking or available for work also rose, which may reflect higher aspirations or slower job matching; household per-capita expenditure likewise increased among potential beneficiaries.
items.title: Tamil Nadu's First-Generation Graduate Scholarship Raised Technical Degree Completion and Early Employment

visual.alt: Bar chart. Technical course enrolment 3.7 percentage; Probability of choosing technical field (among attendees) 8.1 percentage; Technical degree completion 3.6 percentage; Regular salaried employment (ages 25–29) 4.3 percentage.

items.summary:
In a Friday service alert reviewed by BleepingComputer, Microsoft confirmed that some Forcepoint users may encounter printing problems after installing the November 2026 Windows 11 hotpatch (KB5132043). The issue is limited to systems running Windows 11 version 24H2 or later and results from a compatibility conflict between KB5132043 and the Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent. Affected users report that the print option appears greyed out or throws errors when selecting a printer, because the Print Spooler service fails to start. Microsoft states no fix is currently available while customers turn to the Forcepoint support portal for assistance.

This printing problem mirrors another recent warning: last week Microsoft cautioned that KB5132043 was also causing installation and launch failures in Office and third-party applications on Windows 11 systems. Both issues are attributed specifically to the hotpatch updates distributed through Microsoft Autopatch, a cloud-based enterprise service for automating Windows and Microsoft 365 updates; they should not affect devices receiving only the standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates.

Separately, Microsoft had confirmed two weeks earlier that those same Patch Tuesday updates could break printing of complex-format documents on server (Windows Server 2016 or later) and client (Windows 10 or later) devices. Autopatch was introduced in April 2022 for Windows 10/11 Enterprise E3 license holders, reached general availability in July 2022, and Microsoft announced in March that hotpatch security updates would be enabled by default for eligible Intune- and Graph API-managed devices running the May 2026 updates. A related Autopatch bug affecting EU customers was fixed about a month later.

The article ends with promotional content from Adaptive Security advertising AI-based email threat detection, which is unrelated to the technical reporting.
items.title: Microsoft Confirms Windows Printing Issues Affecting Forcepoint Users After November 2026 Hotpatch

items.summary:
A letter by Andy Tan argues that while Singapore's nationwide rollout of the Mediation Direction framework in September—extending to private estates—is a positive development, it leaves condo residents unable to address persistent residential nuisances such as excessive air-conditioning causing condensation and mould on shared walls, and second-hand smoke drifting from balconies. The author contends these issues are compounded by managing agents lacking statutory power to penalise offenders beyond polite advisory letters, particularly when the offending unit is tenanted with an absentee landlord who ignores management communications.

Tan identifies specific limitations in existing mechanisms: a Mediation Direction can compel attendance at mediation but cannot force settlement or halt ongoing nuisance, and registering an agreement as a binding tribunal order still requires both parties' consent. The Community Relations Unit's enforcement powers are described as limited to severe noise and hoarding cases only. Meanwhile, the Strata Titles Boards and Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals place cost, time, and technical proof burdens on innocent residents.

The letter concludes with a recommendation that authorities review the Building (Strata Management) Act to grant management corporations practical enforcement levers and expand binding administrative recourse to cover clear-cut residential nuisances. The claims are attributed solely to Tan's opinion piece; no independent verification of these assertions is provided in the text.
items.title: Forum Letter: Mediation Direction Framework Falls Short on Condo Nuisance Enforcement

items.summary:
A new orchid hybrid, the Dendrobium 'Aiko Naishinno Denka,' was named after Princess Aiko of Japan and planted at the Japanese Garden in Jurong on November 19. The bloom features a cherry blossom-pink blush on its petals, which one commenter describes as symbolizing the "chrysanthemum meeting the orchid"—a gesture representing mutual respect between Singapore and Japan.

The hybrid is part of a three-generation botanical legacy at the National Orchid Garden in the Singapore Botanic Gardens. It shares genetic roots with hybrids named after Princess Aiko's parents, created in 1993, and those dedicated to her grandparents from 1970. The commenter frames this lineage as evidence of roughly six decades of bilateral relations that developed following Singapore's Japanese Occupation.

Orchid hybridisation was pioneered at the Botanic Gardens in 1928 through cross-breeding distinct varieties over years to produce rare colours and resilient blooms. According to the text, nearly a century of such work has produced what is described as the world's largest display of tropical orchids, with Singapore characterised as "the spiritual home of the orchid." The commenter attributes ongoing naming of bespoke hybrids after visiting dignitaries to the National Parks Board.

The piece reflects the personal perspective and interpretation of a single forum contributor rather than verified institutional claims. Assertions about bilateral history are presented through this individual's lens, and descriptive superlatives such as "world's largest display" lack independent confirmation within the text.
items.title: New Dendrobium Orchid Hybrid Named After Princess Aiko Reflects Japan-Singapore Ties

items.summary: Campello and Junqueira (NBER Working Paper 36039, forthcoming in Tax Policy and the Economy) investigate whether tax subsidies can broaden venture capital's geographic reach. They examine the 2009–2010 enhancement of the Qualified Small Business Stock (QSBS) program, which eliminated federal capital gains taxes on investments in qualifying startups. The authors argue that by raising potential payoffs, the reform made riskier investment—including entry into unfamiliar markets—more attractive, an effect they say is especially strong for VC funds relative to angel investors, who receive the same tax benefit but showed no comparable expansion.
items.title: Democratizing Venture Capital: Tax Incentives and the Geographic Expansion of Startup Investing

items.summary: In a 2026 NBER Working Paper, Cong, Liao, Prasad, and Zhang document five facts about payment stablecoins using wallet-level blockchain data from 2020 to 2025. First, they report that onchain volume exceeds Bitcoin's despite a much smaller supply, with velocity rising sharply and transactions shifting toward low-value transfers—indicating stablecoins function as a transaction currency. Second, refining exchange-based attribution using transaction timing reveals activity spread across the Americas, Europe, and Asia, along with fewer cross-regional flows than standard methods imply. Third, estimating a structural cash-management model on holdings data shows that costs of accessing stablecoin wallets have fallen since 2023. Fourth, they find stablecoins are becoming the settlement currency of a fast-growing onchain credit market whose growth appears to reallocate rather than destroy credit. Fifth, smart contracts participate in about one-third of Ethereum stablecoin transactions and over two-thirds of volume, with protocols such as x402 enabling sub-cent machine-to-machine payments. The authors conclude that stablecoins behave as tokenized money with implications for financial markets and regulation.
items.title: Stablecoins Function as Tokenized Money Across Global Markets

items.summary:
On November 22, Bengaluru-based Sarvam AI released Sarvam-105B-1711, an upgraded version of its open-source 105-billion-parameter language model. The company positioned the release within its 'Flash-Lite' class of lightweight models and claimed it sets a new Pareto frontier—improving accuracy relative to cost—in instruction following, chat, tool calling, and Indian languages. An independent X post by user Pratham cited benchmark averages of 73.9 across eight conversational-agent benchmarks versus 74.0 for Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and 66.3 for OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna; these figures are unverified, drawn from internal testing rather than third-party evaluation, and the model card did not independently audit them.

On pricing, Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar stated output costs Rs. 25 per million tokens (about $0.15), compared with $0.85 for Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite—a fivefold gap at near-identical scores—though the company did not independently verify this conversion. As a mixture-of-experts system, roughly 10.3 billion of its parameters activate during inference, and a compressed 65GB NVFP4 version on Hugging Face reportedly runs on a single Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell card with 96GB memory; Sarvam also released inference and training recipes alongside the weights.

The launch followed public discussion about funding. Kumar said the IndiaAI Mission provided GPU access at a 40% discount to roughly 20 startups, which Sarvam used to train its original model from scratch (completed February), but that no direct government payment was made—the subsidy went to cloud providers. He defended his Token Factory inference service against claims it strays from building indigenous models, arguing it runs open-weight models on privately procured GPUs and addresses Indian enterprises' needs for data residency and low latency.

Kumar stated the company has optimized its training stack for Nvidia Blackwell GPUs and plans to release additional vision, speech, and edge-device models over the next two weeks. He framed Sarvam's goal as climbing from India toward frontier capability while building a commercial business; however, he dismissed some criticism of the company as 'manufactured,' which limits independent assessment of these claims.
items.title: Sarvam AI Releases Open-Source Sarvam-105B-1711, Claims Google-Level Performance at Lower Cost

items.summary: At The New York Times DealBook Summit, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella argued that retailers refusing to accept AI shopping agents risk losing customers to competitors who do. Speaking with Andrew Ross Sorkin, he said if one retailer declines an agent while another accepts it, shoppers will migrate toward the open platform—illustrated by his claim that 'if Amazon doesn't [accept], Shop will,' though he did not specify whether 'Shop' referred to Shopify or a broader concept. The exchange arose partly from Meta's announcement of its personal AI agent, Muse, and Amazon's September decision to block it over allegations that the software accessed the site without permission or identifying itself as an AI, raising concerns about account security and login credentials. According to Meta, Muse operates in a dedicated virtual computer with its own browser, requests approval before purchases, records its actions for users, and plans to add Shop Pay and PayPal as payment options; it reportedly already has access to Shopify's catalogue, through which eligible merchants can enable direct checkout via Microsoft Copilot. On the competitive side, Amazon offers Alexa for Shopping on its website and app—capable of comparing products, tracking prices, building carts, and automating routine purchases—while Shopify provides a separate option letting customers find eligible products and enter payment and shipping details in chat or complete purchases at their own storefronts. Nadella compared this shift to the transition from web portals like Yahoo to search engines, warning that agents bringing shoppers directly to checkout reduce retailers' opportunities to display ads, which could make transaction- or click-based revenue more important than his current advertising model; he said businesses attached to an existing business model 'have to kind of scramble.' He also raised unresolved questions about how these systems would interoperate and where liability falls when an agent acts on a customer's behalf. The claims throughout are attributed solely to Nadella, Meta, or Amazon as reported at the summit, with no independent verification provided in the source material.
items.title: Satya Nadella on Competition Between Amazon and Meta Over AI Shopping Agents

items.summary:
At a conference organised by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta stated that revised statistical series for gross domestic product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI), and Index of Industrial Production (IIP) would enable the Reserve Bank of India to assess economic conditions more accurately. She attributed this benefit to the series' capture of structural changes in the Indian economy, including evolving consumption patterns, shifting sectoral contributions, and new growth sources.

Gupta described specific methodological revisions across each index. The revised GDP series uses 2022-23 as its base year and incorporates wider surveys, administrative data, and double deflation for manufacturing and agriculture; she said these changes should improve the reliability of growth estimates and reduce successive-data revisions. Because the RBI relies on early indicators and provisional figures when assessing growth and inflation trends, more stable GDP estimates would support better-calibrated monetary policy.

On CPI measurement, Gupta pointed to a revised series that uses consumption weights from the 2023-24 Household Consumption Expenditure Survey rather than older 2011-12 data. The updated basket reflects changing household spending patterns and incorporates prices from 12 online markets for the first time; it excludes free public distribution system items, employer-provided and government accommodation, while expanding house rent coverage to rural areas.

For IIP, she noted increased weights for technology- and consumption-oriented sectors such as motor vehicles, pharmaceuticals, and electronics, alongside reduced weights for petroleum products and mining. Gupta concluded that better-quality economic data is essential for understanding the changing economy and strengthening policy decisions.

The text presents these statements solely as Poonam Gupta's assertions at a MoSPI conference; it offers no independent verification of the revisions' accuracy or their measurable impact on RBI policy outcomes.
items.title: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta Says Revised GDP, CPI Data Will Improve Monetary Policy Decisions

items.summary: Jakub Pachocki, OpenAI's chief scientist, proposed in a Sunday post that AI companies agree to industrywide limits on developing increasingly powerful models until researchers can better understand and monitor their behavior. The suggested thresholds could be based partly on perplexity—a measurement of how well an AI model predicts the next piece of text—though Pachocki did not specify what initial limit should apply or when it would take effect. He warned that AI might accelerate its own development as early as 2027, potentially outpacing researchers' ability to monitor and understand the technology. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman endorsed the proposal on X, describing it as "the most important thing OpenAI has published in awhile" and saying common limits would help ensure safety and control. The suggestion arrives amid renewed debate over AI regulation following Democrats' midterm election gains across the House, Senate, and governorships, which could increase congressional scrutiny of technology companies; some lawmakers are also considering a dedicated Senate committee on AI policy, while President Trump has opposed broad restrictions, setting up potential clashes with the incoming Democratic Congress. The proposal is attributed to Pachocki's essay via Bloomberg, though its specific details remain unspecified by him.
items.title: OpenAI Chief Scientist Proposes Industry Limits on Powerful AI Models

items.summary: The WTO's 33rd report on G20 trade and investment measures, covering data through 30 June 2026 with annual figures for 2025 and semi-annual figures for the first half of 2026, finds that new restrictive trade policy accelerated sharply while facilitation efforts rose in parallel. In the first half of 2026 alone, G20 economies introduced 206 new non-facilitating measures versus 194 across all of 2025; these import-related restrictions covered an estimated USD 2.0 trillion (12.9% of G20 imports), the highest level on record and roughly ten times the past-15-year average, while export-related restrictive measures reached USD 711 billion (4.8% of exports). At the same time, trade-facilitating measures increased: import facilitation covered an estimated USD 977 billion (6.4% of imports) versus USD 1.1 trillion in all of 2025, and export facilitation reached USD 560 billion (3.8%), more than five times the 2025 level of USD 101 billion — largely reflecting temporary responses to trade disruptions from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
items.title: Trade-facilitating measures help offset rise in new G20 trade restrictions

visual.alt: Bar chart. Import restrictive, H1 2026 2,000,000,000,000; Export restrictive, H1 2026 711,000,000,000; Import facilitating, H1 2026 977,000,000,000; Export facilitating, H1 2026 560,000,000,000.

items.summary:
Robert Kiyosaki publicly stated his intention to increase holdings in physical gold, silver, Bitcoin and Ethereum as he anticipates a market crash potentially larger than 2008. In an earlier X post on Friday (November 23, 2026), however, he advised investors to wait for prices to stabilize before buying volatile assets, warning that purchasing during a sharp decline is like catching a falling knife.

This stance follows recent price movements: gold and silver had fallen to over one-year lows after weeks of selling, then rebounded on Monday by Rs 2,800 per 10 grams and Rs 3,600 per kg respectively. Bitcoin was trading at $61,438.86 after reaching its lowest level since early July.

Kiyosaki attributed his strategy to distrust of the Federal Reserve and global financial institutions such as BlackRock, which he claims are eroding wealth through money printing. He cited figures including a claim that US debt reached $49 trillion in 2026 (with an unspecified growth rate), and referenced job losses at Volkswagen (100,000 workers) and European unrest.

The article notes Kiyosaki previously began buying Bitcoin at $20,000 after a prior crash and intends to wait for another bottom. The reporting includes standard disclaimers that the author is not a registered investment adviser and that views are those of the source rather than the publication.
items.title: Robert Kiyosaki Increases Holdings in Gold, Silver and Bitcoin Amid Crash Fears

visual.alt: Dot chart. Kiyosaki's prior Bitcoin purchase price 20,000 $; Bitcoin current trading price 61,438.86 $.

items.summary:
The 'ZHU·GE' (Zone-to-global Holistic Understanding by Generative Earth-system modeling) platform was launched on Monday at the 2026 Xiongan International Symposium on Meteorological Artificial Intelligence. Its stated goal is to advance AI for Science in Earth sciences, enabling understanding across scales from local observations to global scientific insight and translating research into operational capabilities.

The system reportedly allows researchers to submit objectives in natural language after which it can search literature and data, devise approaches, write code, run experiments, analyze results, and adjust direction based on feedback. Its applications include studying mechanisms, developing forecasting methods, modeling, and model optimization.

According to the article's figures, ZHU·GE reportedly integrates about 10 petabytes of public scientific data, an initial 1 petabyte authorized by the China Meteorological Administration (CMA), roughly 2 million literature records, more than 5,000 code tools, and over 10 general-purpose research skills. Additional CMA data is being integrated.

The platform was reportedly jointly developed under the leadership of the CMA and the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, built on the Tianqing meteorological big data cloud platform and the Duanyan·Lingtai research agent. It will reportedly be rolled out across institutions under the CMA and made available to members of the National Meteorological Science and Education Integration Innovation Alliance via a research token service; international services are also being explored.
items.title: China Launches AI Platform for Earth System Research

items.summary: On Monday, the Supreme Court—through a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana—instructed the appellate tribunals handling appeals under West Bengal's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) electoral rolls to separate cases challenging voter exclusions from those contesting inclusions, giving priority to the exclusion-related pleas. The bench reasoned that inclusion appeals 'do not involve any urgency' and may be deferred for the time being, while exclusion appeals should receive preference in final disposal. Within the exclusion category, the court further directed prioritization of cases under Kolkata Municipal Corporation jurisdiction because civic body elections are imminent. In a separate directive, the Supreme Court asked the Election Commission to increase the number of appellate tribunals addressing SIR grievances, working in consultation with the Calcutta High Court chief justice. These orders were issued while hearing petitions seeking measures to streamline and expedite appeal disposal; on August 25, the same bench had directed the EC to submit details of pending and disposed appeals along with separate counts for exclusion- versus inclusion-related cases, and to specify how many additional tribunals would be needed to meet a stipulated timeframe. The reporting draws partly on PTI inputs.
items.title: Supreme Court Directs West Bengal SIR Tribunals to Prioritize Voter Exclusion Appeals

items.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that a resolution to rename the state from West Bengal to 'Paschim Banga' would be tabled in the Legislative Assembly on December 9. The proposal was approved by the state Cabinet during a meeting earlier that same day, with Adhikari confirming the date for moving the item before the House. The text provides no further detail on the rationale behind the renaming or any public response to the initiative. It should be noted that this source includes an unrelated biographical note about journalist Subhadra Srivastava of The Times of India, which appears to be extraneous and is not connected to the announcement itself.
items.title: West Bengal Cabinet Approves Proposal to Rename State 'Paschim Banga'; Resolution Set for Assembly

items.summary: SG Mart shares surged approximately 14% following reports of fundraising plans, building on a rally of roughly 200% since the start of 2026. The move coincided with Tata Steel's board approving an acquisition of about 26.38% of APL Apollo Tubes for around Rs 15,510.6 crore (reported as ~Rs 15,511 crore), alongside a mandatory open offer covering up to 7.28 crore equity shares at Rs 2,301.40 each—potentially costing about Rs 16,755.66 crore if fully subscribed and raising Tata Steel's maximum holding to ~52.38%. The link between the two stocks is that Sanjay Gupta-led families are promoters of both companies; APL Apollo Tubes' board had cleared its downstream expansion strategy earlier in the day. Following these developments, APL Apollo Tubes fell about 14% and Tata Steel dropped roughly 7%, while SG Mart's Q2 results showed revenue of Rs 156 crore (down 8% year-on-year but up 19% sequentially), net profit of Rs 54 crore (+104% year-on-year, +19% quarter-on-quarter), and EBITDA rising ~157% to Rs 72 crore with a margin expanding to 4.6%. SG Mart operates in B2B metal trading, steel service centres, and downstream distribution across products including TMT bars, structural steel, HR coils/sheets, binding wire, welding rods, fasteners, electrical products, and home appliances. The article notes these figures are reported by Veer Sharma, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or Investment Adviser and holds no financial interest in the mentioned companies as of publication; readers were advised to consider original research reports for their own investment decisions.
items.title: APL Apollo Tubes Acquisition and SG Mart's Multibagger Rally

visual.alt: Bar chart. Revenue 8 %; Net Profit 104 %; EBITDA 157 %.

items.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence announced on Sunday that the country has joined 10 other nations—Belgium, Canada, Finland, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Türkiye, and the Republic of Korea—in a NATO-led initiative called STARLIFT. The program aims to develop a network of flexible satellite launch services across participating countries to ensure more reliable access to space and strengthen security for military users. According to NATO, STARLIFT will work with commercial launch providers and spaceport operators to secure launch slots on commercial rockets, including for urgent launches, while supporting improvements to launch infrastructure, logistics, and air and maritime traffic management.
items.title: UK Joins NATO STARLIFT Satellite Launch Initiative

items.summary: Adora Flora City, China's second domestically built large cruise ship and the larger of two sister vessels, embarked on its maiden commercial voyage from Guangzhou in Guangdong Province. Carrying more than 3,800 passengers aboard a six-day, five-night itinerary to Hong Kong and Hue, Vietnam, the ship measured 341 meters in length with a gross tonnage of 141,900, featuring 2,130 cabins and capacity for up to 5,232 passengers. Construction began in August 2022; operated by Adora Cruises under China Tourism Group, the vessel was delivered in Shanghai on November 6 and completed its first trial voyage on November 9. Shi Dai, chairperson of China Tourism Group, stated that cruise operations aim to develop integrated cultural tourism products and set a new benchmark for sea vacations. The ship is larger than its sister vessel Adora Magic City, which began commercial service in January 2024 after completing about 250 voyages. Hu Zhenyu, deputy director of the Qianhai branch of the China Development Institute, characterized the entry into service of both ships as a new phase for the industry that would expand marine tourism offerings and create consumption drivers in coastal areas. For 2027, Adora Flora City is scheduled to undertake over 50 international voyages from Guangzhou, including no-scheduled-port-call itineraries; these plans are projections rather than confirmed figures. The maiden voyage coincided with the opening of a duty-free store at the Nansha International Cruise Home Port terminal and drew commentary from Wu Qingsong of Guangzhou's tourism bureau on integrating port, shipping, and tourism resources. Adora Cruises' Guo Jia outlined plans to expand year-round operations across multiple home ports in east and north China plus the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. The launch aligns with a 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for cultural tourism that calls for boosting cruise spending, amid reported strong industry growth: total cruise passenger throughput rose 25.3% year on year in 2025 according to the Ministry of Natural Resources.
items.title: China's Second Domestically Built Large Cruise Ship Begins Maiden Voyage

items.summary: During a meeting with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Singapore on Sunday, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang—who also serves as a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee—called for deeper bilateral cooperation between China and Singapore. The remarks were made while Ding co-chaired bilateral cooperation mechanism meetings with Singaporean Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong; he had traveled to Singapore following Wong's visit to China and attendance at the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, which Ding congratulated him on. Ding stated that both countries should fully utilize their existing bilateral cooperation mechanism and expand mutually beneficial collaboration in areas including artificial intelligence and green development, noting that past meetings have enriched the partnership's dimensions and laid a foundation for an all-round high-quality future-oriented relationship. He also emphasized sustaining exchanges in education, science and technology, culture, and other fields to strengthen public support for the two countries' relations. Wong echoed this sentiment, expressing confidence that the mechanism meetings would consolidate and expand cooperation across sectors such as AI and the digital economy while enhancing people-to-people exchanges. He added that Singapore will assume rotating chairmanship of ASEAN next year and intends to use that opportunity to advance ASEAN-China cooperation in various fields.
items.title: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang Calls for Strengthened China-Singapore Cooperation

items.summary: Shares in outsourcing firm Capita fell approximately 70% after chief executive Adolfo Hernandez agreed to leave with immediate effect, acknowledging the company had 'not delivered' for members of the UK's Civil Service pension scheme. The scheme manages pensions for about 1.7 million public sector workers and has been mired in controversy over tens of thousands of retiring civil servants facing payment delays; one Cabinet Office minister described Capita's progress as 'abysmal.' Hernandez, to be replaced by current chief financial officer Pablo Andres, attributed the shortfall partly to failing to deliver promised automation, AI, and digital tools for managing the 1.7 million members. The company took over administration of the scheme on December 1 from MyCSP under a seven-year deal worth £239m. Capita has cut its profit forecast, now expecting underlying operating profit for 2027 to fall by between £85m and £95m—up from a previously expected reduction of up to £40m—with the loss driven partly by an extra cost recovery plan and two other 'major' contract losses in defence and pension solutions. The firm plans to raise about £190m through an equity issue in the first half of next year to stabilize its finances, though it did not specify a single definitive target for that raise beyond citing both figures (£190m) in the text.
items.title: Capita Shares Plunge and CEO Steps Down Amid Civil Service Pension Saga

items.summary: Almost eight years after a viral video of leader Santiago Abascal riding a horse through Andalucía drew ridicule, the far-right Vox party has become Spain's third-largest political party and is poised to win nearly 20% of the vote in the snap general election on 29 November. This represents a dramatic reversal from its earlier status as a fringe outfit that captured just 0.2% of the vote in the 2016 general election, when prevailing wisdom held that Spain's Franco-era history had inoculated it against far-right politics. Vox won its first breakthrough with 12 seats in Andalucía's regional parliament three weeks after the video went viral. According to El País journalist Miguel González and author of The Extremist Galaxy: Funders, Allies and Strategies of the New Far Right, Vox's initial growth was driven by a reaction to Catalan nationalism following the autumn 2017 independence crisis, which allowed it to position itself as an uncompromising defender of Spanish unity. This enabled its most significant move—dragging immigration into mainstream politics and forcing the conservative People's party (PP) to adopt some of Vox's positions. González notes that Vox initially focused on areas with high immigration levels such as El Ejido in Almería and parts of Murcia, but successfully put the issue on the political agenda. The mass influx of more than 80,000 people from Morocco into Ceuta this summer exemplified this dynamic, prompting PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo to urge expulsion regardless of age or circumstances. Professor Vicente Valentim of IE University argues that when centre-right parties adopt far-right language and postures, they legitimize the movement; he notes a two-step process where center-right parties first enter parliament and then move closer ideologically, which can be electorally costly as some voters prefer 'the original to the copy.' Alongside immigration fixation, Vox has brought hate figures into mainstream politics—targeting secessionist Catalan president Carles Puigdemont, Podemos leader Pablo Iglesias, and Sánchez—with Abascal's manifesto vowing legal proceedings against Sánchez over his handling of the Ceuta invasion. The party increasingly refuses to sever ties with extreme figures; Fernando Paz was dropped from its 2019 candidate list after Jewish groups objected to his Holocaust denialism but now sits on a Vox-aligned foundation board, while neo-Nazi-linked Jordi de la Fuente is standing as Vox's Tarragona candidate despite awaiting trial. Alejandro Baer of the Spanish National Research Council notes that Vox appears sufficiently consolidated and legitimate to openly incorporate people with extremist backgrounds who previously represented liabilities. In Rioja, an eastern Andalucía town long a socialist stronghold where Vox finished first in May's regional election resulting in another PP-Vox coalition after conservatives lost their absolute majority, divisions appear more generational than political—29-year-old Patricio López attributes the rightward shift among young people to feeling shortchanged on housing and social issues over eight years, while 63-year-old Rafael Ruiz Martínez views it as protest-driven partisan theatre reminiscent of Game of Thrones rather than a rejection of Vox's socialist past.
items.title: Spain's far-right Vox transformed from mocked fringe party to mainstream electoral force

items.summary: On Sunday (reported Monday, 23 November 2026), Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed responsibility for sinking the Russian corvette Merkury at a naval base in Benghazi, Libya. In a post on X accompanied by video of the ship being struck, he said seven Ukrainian-made naval drones were deployed to sink it, describing the vessel as one commissioned in 2023 during the full-scale war; Zelenskyy also stated that the Russian dry cargo vessel MV Angara was sunk and described both actions as part of Kyiv's response to Russia's aggression. The claims are attributed solely to Ukraine and remain unverified by other parties: Albania denied reports that its territory hosted or facilitated the drone launch, calling such allegations inaccurate and unsupported by evidence; the Kremlin said it would defer questions about the incident to Russia's Defence Ministry. Separately at a Nato parliamentary assembly meeting in Berlin, Zelenskyy addressed broader regional security, urging partners to strengthen air defence ahead of winter while noting that four-way peace talks between Ukraine, Russia, the US and Europe are reportedly being pursued before Christmas; he also pushed back against Article Five-like guarantees for Ukraine, arguing instead that membership should be allowed. Nato's Mark Rutte called for continued military supplies to Ukraine and increased collective defence investment toward a 5% GDP spending pledge by 2035, while NATO and UN meetings were scheduled to discuss Friday's Russian missile strikes on Poland and attacks on consulates in Kyiv.
items.title: Ukraine Claims Responsibility for Sinking Russian Warship in Libya

items.summary:
Inside Climate News' staff podcast 'Climate Hope,' hosted by Kiley Price, frames its Thanksgiving edition around stories of environmental progress despite a year marked by catastrophic climate events. Co-hosts Teresa Tomassoni and Katie Surma discussed reef resilience and the rights of nature respectively, while clean energy reporter Dan Gearino analyzed how Democratic midterm election gains could drive state-level climate policy.

On U.S. politics, Gearino reported that Democrats exceeded expectations in the midterms, gaining trifectas (governor plus both legislative chambers) in states like Wisconsin and Pennsylvania—both high-emission or wind-rich areas—and projecting major renewable energy legislation within two years. He noted a House majority large enough to pass climate bills even with Trump's expected vetoes, while observing that campaigns increasingly emphasize consumer pricing over explicit climate messaging ('climate hushing'). Gearino attributed the Democratic wins partly to data center interests spending heavily against candidates like Sherrod Brown and Talarico without voter support for their issue set. He characterized the election as a once-in-multiple-generations opportunity.

On coral reefs, Tomassoni cited a scientific assessment stating 96 percent of the world's shallow coral reefs—including the Great Barrier Reef—face collapse risk within 50 years (by roughly 2075), which could end their function as habitat for at least 25 percent of marine life. She highlighted hopeful research identifying climate-resilient 'super reefs' in the Marshall Islands and lab-based breeding programs for endangered elkhorn coral in the Dominican Republic, while noting that rising ocean temperatures from a Super El Niño remain the primary threat.

On rights of nature, Surma reported Ecuador as the only country to recognize nature's rights constitutionally (2008), with courts striking down mining permits and Indigenous groups like Sarayaku resisting oil projects. She noted Brazil re-elected Lula da Silva despite his government greenlighting an offshore oil project affecting four Indigenous territories, where environmental defenders were killed at twice the prior year's rate—26 people total last year—with threats often preceding violence.

The episode also covered midterm ballot measures: Corpus Christi voters approved steep drought fees for industrial water use; Colorado rejected a constitutional amendment protecting fossil fuel companies' gas sales rights (reinforcing a 2024 emissions-reduction law); and California's proposition to weaken its Environmental Quality Act failed after supporters spent at least $36 million.

The text presents these as reporters' accounts, projections, and pending legislative actions rather than confirmed outcomes. All figures are drawn from the podcast content.
items.title: Inside Climate's Thanksgiving Edition Highlights Progress Amid Severe 2026 Climate Events

items.summary: South East Water, which serves approximately 2.4 million customers across south-east England (Kent, Sussex, Surrey, Hampshire, and Berkshire), reported a pre-tax loss of £22.9m for the six months ending 30 September, down from an £18.2m profit in the same period last year. The reversal was driven by penalties and roughly £29m spent responding to summer supply interruptions that affected more than 286,000 customers across Kent and Sussex during heatwaves; spending included bottled water distribution, emergency water stations, and customer compensation. Regulator Ofwat separately ordered the company in July to spend £30.5m on improvements following those outages. The results also set aside £14.6m for a redress package covering affected customers. Separately, in October the company asked shareholders for £50m after earlier warning it needed additional funding to remain solvent; leadership changes followed parliamentary criticism of repeated supply failures, with John Halsall appointed chief executive and Richard Morse due to become chair on 3 December.
items.title: South East Water Reports Half-Year Loss After Summer Supply Disruptions

items.summary:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed on Monday that Ukrainian sea drones sank a Russian navy corvette, the Merkury, moored at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya. According to Zelenskyy's post on X and a live address to the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin, Ukraine deployed seven domestically made sea drones about 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from the front line — roughly 800 miles into Libyan territory — to strike one of Russia's newest vessels. Zelenskyy described the operation as 'exemplary' and said its targets were achieved.

Libyan officials briefed on the attack provided a more limited account: at least four drones were intercepted while two hit the corvette, which is designed for coastal patrol and escort duties. They reported that at least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were wounded, though they spoke anonymously as affiliates of the self-styled Libyan National Army controlling eastern Libya. Ambrey, a U.K.-based maritime security firm, said some explosions may have resulted from ammunition detonating aboard the ship.

The corvette had docked to refuel under a cooperation agreement between Russia and the eastern-based Libyan government. In related strikes, Ukraine reportedly hit the sanctioned Russian cargo ship MV Angara — which it says was used to transport military equipment — and destroyed a Ka-27 helicopter; SBU officials said drones were launched from a 'mothership' near the target while Russian defenses attempted air, sea, and land counterattacks. A separate drone strike later damaged a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel off Benghazi.

The eastern Libyan government sent letters to U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres and the Security Council calling for an investigation into whether western Libya was used to prepare or launch the attack — though Zelenskyy's account of drones operating from Misrata, Tripoli, and Zawiya in western Libya conflicts with this framing.

The article notes that Russian officials made no immediate comment. It also contextualizes the strike as part of a broader pattern of long-range Ukrainian attacks, citing June's Operation Spiderweb, which Zelenskyy said hit over 40 aircraft across Russia; it further reports that a separate Russian strike on an apartment block near Kyiv killed 11 people, including a 7-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman. All casualty figures are attributed to regional police or rescue services.
items.title: Ukraine Claims Drone Attack Sank Russian Warship at Libyan Naval Base

items.summary: The chief executive of Capita, Adolfo Hernandez, abruptly resigned with immediate effect after admitting the company had failed to deliver pension services for retired civil servants. He is being replaced by CFO Pablo Andres. Shares in Capita fell 67% on Monday morning to as low as 80p — its lowest price since October 1991 — following cut profit forecasts and a proposal to raise £190m of extra capital, which was supported by activist investor Oasis Management Company. The company expects adjusted operating profit in 2027 to be £85m to £95m lower than previously projected, citing additional costs related to the UK Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS) contract and short-term contract headwinds. Capita agreed the CSPS contract with the former Conservative government in 2023; it came into force in December 2025 and covers a 1.7 million-member scheme. The company has faced criticism for delays administering payments, leaving thousands of civil servants waiting for payouts and retirement quotes, while pensioners have reported being forced to borrow from family or use food banks due to lost income. MPs blamed the problems on operational failures including overwhelmed revision teams, poor technology, and incorrect pension quotes; a Cabinet Office minister described progress as 'abysmal,' and in July the government said it hoped to take the scheme back in-house after 'unacceptable' service levels.
items.title: Capita CEO Departs Amid Civil Service Pension Failures and Share Collapse

items.summary: Advanced Magnesium Alloys Corp., a magnesium recycler in Anderson, Indiana with about 40 employees, was the country's largest emitter of sulfur hexafluoride (SF6), the most potent greenhouse gas known. In 2023 it used 10 metric tons of SF6 as a cover gas to prevent molten magnesium from burning during ingot production; those emissions equaled roughly 60,000 automobiles' annual output and were about 24,300 times more warming than CO2 per pound. The company switched to an alternative fluorine-based cover gas (BestSolv Zulu) in 2024, driving its SF6 use to zero and seeking carbon credits for the reduction—though it remains unclear whether credit revenue will offset transition costs. Its decision followed years of failed trials: Shaked, who earlier oversaw a switch from SF6 to sulfur dioxide at an Israeli plant, initially resisted alternatives because fluorine-based gases are corrosive and toxic, with prior failures attributed by him to low winter temperatures, incorrect gas mixtures, or insufficient quantities before the company found BestSolv Zulu effective across its process. Nationally, U.S. magnesium production and casting SF6 emissions fell 74 percent from 1999 to 2010 but have since plateaued at about 1.1 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent in 2023 (roughly a quarter-million automobiles' annual output), with no federal or Indiana rules restricting the gas—only California and the EU banned it for these uses roughly a decade ago, while EPA and industry partners pursued voluntary best practices instead.
items.title: Advanced Magnesium Alloys Eliminated SF6 Emissions While Other Midwest Producers Remain Dependent

items.summary:
The UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, concluded without consensus after nations could not agree even to reaffirm the commitment made at Dubai (2023) to transition away from fossil fuels. The deadlock reflected a deeper divide over climate justice: developing countries, speaking through India's Like-Minded Developing Countries group led by environment minister Bhupender Yadav, demanded recognition of developed nations' historical responsibility and predictable finance before accepting greater costs—arguing they could not be forced to choose between climate action and their right to development. The proposed statement collapsed as its drafts progressively stripped fossil-fuel language: the November 16 version reaffirmed Dubai's commitment, but versions on November 19 and November 22 removed those references entirely before talks broke down two days past schedule.

The failure was compounded by a parallel declaration from China, Russia, and the U.S. in Shenzhen (November 19) to increase production and supply of refined petroleum products without targets or timetables—contradicting climate goals while citing energy security concerns relevant to import-dependent nations like India. UN Secretary-General António Guterres expressed frustration that governments continued expanding fossil-fuel production despite the 1.5°C target, warning that those profiting from destruction must not dictate terms.

The political deadlock has immediate consequences: a 2025 Lancet Countdown assessment for India estimated heat exposure caused 247 billion lost potential work hours in 2024 (66% agriculture, 20% construction), with associated income losses of $194 billion. While Antalya produced separate decisions on adaptation, the Adaptation Fund, and the Just Transition Work Programme, broader draft decisions—including those on Mitigation, climate policy effects, and the Global Environment Facility—failed to secure agreement.

A key limitation is that these figures represent potential work hours and income losses rather than realized economic impact. The unresolved questions now face COP in Ethiopia: how governments can accelerate fossil-fuel transition without consensus on direction or financing.
items.title: UN Climate Summit in Antalya Ended Without Consensus on Fossil Fuel Transition

visual.alt: Bar chart. Agriculture 66 %; Construction 20 %.

items.summary:
India plans to expand pumped-storage capacity (PSP) substantially, with a January roadmap from the Central Electricity Authority projecting total installed PSP capacity of 87 GW by 2034 and over 100 GW by 2036 through an average annual addition of 9 GW. The same report identifies the Western Ghats as having the highest PSP potential nationally, led by Maharashtra with 56,355 MW across its projects at various stages—400 MW operational, 2,500 MW under construction, 6,300 MW approved but unbuilt, and 24,800 MW in survey or investigation. PSPs store surplus electricity by pumping water uphill into reservoirs and releasing it downhill to generate power, which experts such as Disha Aggarwal of the Centre for Energy, Environment and Water describe as a viable long-duration storage technology that helps manage renewable-heavy grid fluctuations.

The concentration of these projects in the Western Ghats has drawn concern from geologists and disaster specialists. The Geological Survey of India lists 90,000 square kilometres—about 30% of Maharashtra—as landslide-prone across the Western Ghats and Konkan uplands. Historical incidents underscore this risk: a June 2005 heavy-rainfall landslide at Thane's Ghatghar project trapped nearly 22 workers; an August 2021 rain-triggered slide in Mahad taluka killed 85 people, and a 2014 Malin village collapse near Junnar-Ambegaon claimed 153 lives. The Maharashtra State Disaster Management Plan's Landslide Management Plan identified 485 high-priority villages across ten districts and recorded 145 landslide-related deaths between 2018 and 2024, with the most concentrated in 2021-2022 (105).

Experts argue that current assessments inadequately address these hazards. Shishir Rao of the University of Texas at San Antonio notes that project evaluations focus mainly on slope stability rather than historical landslide vulnerability, while Vivek S. Kale of IIT Bombay stresses assessing geological frameworks and planning alignments carefully as done with older projects like Khopoli hydropower. Parineeta Dandekar of SANDRP warns against attributing single events to climate change but links the rise in extreme weather to its growing influence, and cautions that blasting and tunnelling destabilize slopes.

The decision-making process further limits safeguards: developers primarily assess site suitability, with CEA concurrence required for projects needing Central Water Commission (foundation/seismic), Geological Survey of India (geological) and Central Soil and Materials Research Station (geotechnical) approvals. Ecologists and social scientists typically enter after locations are set, reducing their influence over decisions. Recent regulatory easing also weakened protections: a 2025 MoEF&CC exemption allowed exploratory drilling in forest areas without treating it as land diversion.

The absence of enforceable climate assessments is highlighted by the August 2026 Nepal disaster, where flash floods on the Nepal-China border destroyed or damaged 281 MW installed capacity plus 388 MW under construction; the 216 MW Upper Trishuli-1 project—financed partly by ADB and AIIB—was worst hit after an expert panel flagged in December 2024 that no climate resilience assessment had been done. India's Environmental Impact Assessment framework does not require climate assessments, and voluntary safeguards like ADB's November 2024 memorandum of understanding with Tata Power lack enforcement power.

The article notes these are reported claims from experts and officials rather than established conclusions; the roadmap figures reflect projected capacity targets, landslide death tolls span specific years, and causal links between projects and climate risks remain asserted by critics without definitive attribution.
items.title: India's Pumped-Storage Expansion Targets Raise Climate-Risk Concerns in the Western Ghats
