items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong announced on Monday (Nov 23) that an upgrade to the China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement—designated CSFTA 4.0—and deeper financial connectivity were among the key outcomes of this year's bilateral meetings, which he said could bring significant benefits to Singaporeans. The announcement followed his meeting with Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang and the 22nd Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC), the annual apex platform that co-chaired the discussions; both leaders jointly chaired the session. Gan described CSFTA 4.0 as a major undertaking expected to take one to two years to complete, with negotiations launched during Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's visit to China when he met President Xi Jinping. The upgrade would facilitate trade between the countries, particularly in digital trade and cross-border data flows, and include a digital economy component covering areas such as artificial intelligence (AI), its applications, and governance.
items.title: Singapore and China Announce FTA Upgrade, Financial Cooperation as Key Outcomes of Bilateral Talks

items.summary: World Rugby announced on Monday that South African hooker Malcolm Marx, the previous year's winner, is among a four-man shortlist for this year's world men's player of the year award. He is joined by Springboks teammate prop Ox Nche, who would become the first prop to win if selected; France winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey, 2026 Six Nations Player of the Championship; and New Zealand centre Jordie Barrett. Separately, World Rugby's breakthrough player of the year award has a six-person shortlist featuring French players Fabian Brau-Boirie and Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, alongside South Africa's Paul de Villiers and Japan flyhalf Ryunosuke Ito. The winners for both awards are scheduled to be announced at the Nations Championship Finals at Twickenham this weekend.
items.title: Malcolm Marx and Ox Nche Shortlisted for World Rugby Player of the Year

items.summary: On November 23, CrowdStrike announced an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler valued at approximately $43.9 billion, part of its strategy to expand into network security and zero-trust services. The deal positions the combined entity as one of the world's largest pure-play cybersecurity providers, targeting enterprise customers seeking to consolidate their vendor relationships. In terms of execution, Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share held, implying a value of about $260.41 per Zscaler share and representing roughly a 34 percent premium to its last closing price. Following the transaction's completion, existing CrowdStrike shareholders are expected to retain approximately 84.1 percent ownership of the combined company. Market reaction was mixed: Zscaler shares rose more than 13.4 percent in premarket trading while CrowdStrike declined about 5 percent. The companies project a starting point of more than $10 billion in combined annual recurring revenue and aim to generate around $1 billion in annualized revenue synergies.
items.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler in All-Stock Deal Valuing Company at ~$43.9 Billion

items.summary: On November 23, LaLiga announced that personal data had been extracted from one of its digital platforms in a cyber attack. The breach occurred between November 14 and 16, though the full extent remains undetermined as analysis is ongoing; affected systems reportedly include a fan platform and club-related data. LaLiga became aware of the intrusion on November 16 and took containment measures at that time. Its security team has since analyzed activity to identify compromised information while increasing supervision of digital services to prevent further incidents. The Spanish Agency for the Protection of Data was notified, and authorities have referred the matter to the National Police's Central Unit of Cyber-Delinquency.
items.title: LaLiga Reports Data Breach Affecting Fan Platform and Club Information

items.summary:
On Sunday, Kenya's President William Ruto and DR Congo's President Felix Tshisekedi agreed to restore full diplomatic ties between the two countries in a joint statement issued after a summit held in Oyo, Congo-Brazzaville. The meeting was facilitated by Congo-Brazzaville's President Denis Sassou Nguesso, with Togolese leader Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé serving as mediator. Both leaders affirmed their commitment to sovereignty, territorial integrity, non-interference in states' internal affairs, good neighbourliness, peaceful dispute settlement, and strengthened cooperation within regional mechanisms such as the East African Community (EAC), of which both are members—DR Congo having joined in 2022.

The agreement follows a deterioration in relations since 2023 when DR Congo accused Kenya of hosting leaders behind rebel alliances, including M23. This led Kinshasa to recall its envoy from Nairobi and refuse to accredit Kenya's nominated ambassador. Tensions intensified after the Congo River Alliance (AFC), which included M23, was launched in Nairobi in 2023; DR Congo viewed this as an attempt to destabilize it. Further friction arose when Kenya named a consul-general to Goma—the North Kivu capital that fell to M23 forces—and hosted Congolese opposition figures including former President Joseph Kabila in October 2025, who was sentenced to death in absentia and has since led the FRN rebel coalition.

Beyond diplomacy, the leaders discussed deepening trade cooperation, economic development, regional integration, and collaboration on controlling Ebola's spread. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus noted that attack frequency across DR Congo's east increased after late October, disrupting the response; he cited more than 5,700 deaths and 11,000 infections since the Bundibugyo-species outbreak was declared in May, with cases also reported in Kenya, Uganda, and Nigeria. The text presents these figures as WHO-reported counts without independent verification.

The article offers no stated limitations or caveats beyond attributing casualty and infection numbers to WHO reporting.
items.title: Kenya and DR Congo Agree to Restore Diplomatic Ties After Conflict-Related Tensions

items.summary: European gas prices jumped sharply as a forecast cold snap raised concerns about supply shortages during the winter peak-demand period. The Dutch month-ahead contract, which serves as Europe's benchmark for four-week-ahead pricing, rose by up to 8.6% to €96.08 before settling at +4% on €92.50. Continental gas supplies have been constrained by a slowdown in exports from Qatar due to the Middle East war and elevated summer consumption driven by cooling during a prolonged heatwave. As a result, storage levels fell to about 69% full against a typical seasonal level of 80%. In the UK, energy system operators indicated that sufficient gas and electricity would be available through the coldest months because suppliers have paid higher market prices than neighbours to secure imports; however, this is expected to translate into some of Europe's highest household bills. The regulator Ofgem was anticipated to announce a 26% rise in its quarterly price cap from January, adding roughly £443 to an average annual dual-fuel bill and potentially representing one of the largest quarterly increases on record. Charitable and industry responses highlighted hardship concerns: Citizens Advice chief executive Clare Moriarty warned that millions of households would enter winter with depleted budgets and called for targeted support beyond Chancellor John Healey's recent £100 council-tax top-up to 20m households in bands A to D, which she said would not reach those most in need. Centrica chief executive Chris O'Shea expressed concern about rising numbers of people unable or unwilling to pay their bills.
items.title: European Gas Prices Surge on Cold-Snap Fears Amid Low Storage

visual.alt: Bar chart. Gas storage level (full) 69 %; Typical seasonal storage level 80 %; UK quarterly price cap rise from January 26 %.

items.summary: The provided text is not an article but a paywall notice from Heatmap that blocks access to content titled 'Transcript: How AI Ate the American Economy.' The notice states that readers have reached their free-article limit and must subscribe via a paid membership or log in/create a free account to continue. It describes three tiers of offerings without providing any substantive information about the article's contents, findings, mechanisms, data, limitations, or authorship. Because the text contains only promotional descriptions of Heatmap memberships—unlimited access, virtual briefings, member events, exclusive polling, and VIP reception tickets—it offers no verifiable claims to summarize beyond its function as an access barrier.
items.title: Heatmap Paywall Notice for 'How AI Ate the American Economy'

items.summary: This first-person essay recounts the author's transition from a reluctant computer science major to an enthusiastic programmer, and ultimately describes how generative-AI coding tools transformed—and for him ended—his profession. The narrative begins with his pragmatic switch from philosophy to computer science as an international student seeking visa eligibility, followed by years of work at a health care startup where he found genuine enjoyment in Haskell, compiler construction, and open-source editing. His central claim is that the arrival of ChatGPT in November 2022, then AI command-line tools released in early 2025—which he describes as improving 'gradually, then suddenly'—fundamentally altered software engineering by shifting it from human hand-coding to machine operation. He cites a report that more than 90 percent of code at companies like Anthropic and Coinbase is now AI-written, framing this shift as the end of programmers rather than programming itself: humans have become 'operators' prompting agents instead of craftspeople writing code. The author attributes his own rapid skill decline to reliance on these tools, comparing it to a neurodegenerative effect that blunts cognitive faculties. He provides concrete evidence of this dependence through personal metrics from Claude Code usage: building 239 features and 17 extensions mapped to 141 keyboard shortcuts in an open-source editor project; spending 10 hours coding on one Sunday, then eight the next day; and attempting self-imposed limits that he admits were undermined by the tool itself. He also notes having built 12 additional iOS and Mac apps without learning Swift syntax through AI assistance. The essay concludes with his decision to leave programming as a career to finish writing a book, while acknowledging the loss of polyglot-programming pleasure.
items.title: A Programmer's Account of AI-Driven Decline in Hand-Coded Software Engineering

items.summary: Mumbai-based entrepreneur Arjun Vaidya, known for advocating living in India over abroad, posted on Instagram about how deteriorating air quality has affected his family. His daughters developed croup and one nine-month-old required a nebulizer, while his father—who had bypass surgery with four stents—suffered breathing difficulties after fluid accumulated in his lungs. Vaidya questioned whether the conveniences of Indian life justify these health risks but clarified he does not intend to leave India. The post prompted social media users to debate the trade-offs between everyday convenience and public health, including a comment asking 'Would you trade lungs for 10 minute delivery?' Air quality readings from November 23 supported broader concern: Delhi recorded an AQI of 249 per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), while Mumbai's Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology system logged an AQI of 266 in Colaba at 8 am and 206 in Malad. Other cities—Pune, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Ahmedabad—also reported elevated levels, indicating the problem extends beyond Delhi's winter crisis to coastal regions as well. The article notes that AQI figures can vary depending on monitoring station and measurement system.
items.title: Mumbai Entrepreneur Questions India's Convenience Economy Amid Worsening Air Pollution

items.summary: Photographer Rankin publicly condemns generative AI as 'disgusting,' despite having produced substantial AI output since Damien Hirst introduced him to the technology in 2021. His nine-month conceptual project, Faik (thefaik.com), featured artificially generated images—ranging from a skateboarding granny to magazine covers of Elvis, Frida Kahlo, Nelson Mandela, and God—and billboards warning that 'The people who control AI will control history itself.' This exploration prompted his return to traditional photography through the new book Contact. The 500-plus-word tome compiles images Rankin shot between 1987 and 2006 of bands (Oasis, Blur), public figures (Tony Blair), models (Kylie, Kate Moss), and musicians (André 3000, Hugh Grant). Rather than presenting single cover selections, it displays contact sheets that emphasize the photographer-subject encounter; its title references human connection. Rankin describes his approach as seeking genuine exchange with subjects—'Forget about me – connect through the lens.' Born in Glasgow in 1966 and trained initially in accountancy before photography, he co-founded Dazed & Confused in 1991 (with Jefferson Hack) and Hunger magazine in 2011. His next major project will be a sequel to his 2006 book Tuulitastic about model Tuuli Shipster, whom he has married for 17 years; he is also planning wet-plate photography as an antidote to AI. He expects AI to devastate the industry and replace jobs within less than a year—spanning image-retouching agencies to hair, makeup, and styling—but does not believe it will end people wanting 'proper photos.' Published by Hunger for £30, Contact is accompanied by an exhibition at his Annroy Gallery in London from 3 December to 3 February. The article also presents six sample images with Rankin's commentary: Liam and Noel Gallagher (2002, Q issue 190), Björk (1994, Dazed & Confused issue 9; reportedly ~200 rolls of film used), David Bowie (1995, Dazed & Confused issue 14), Vivienne Westwood (2002, POP magazine), and Goldie (1999). The text offers no quantitative data suitable for a chart.
items.title: Rankin's AI Critique and Return to Analog Photography

items.summary:
The Teatro Real in Madrid won the best opera house award at this year's International Opera Awards gala held at Vienna's Theater an der Wien, marking its second victory. The institution was first recognized in 2021 and received a sustainability award in 2025; only two other theatres—the Bayerische Staatsoper and Komische Oper Berlin—have previously won the prize twice. Artistic director Joan Matabosch accepted the honor on behalf of staff, casts, technical teams, and administration across all areas of the institution, attributing success to harmony and shared purpose rather than any single individual.

The Teatro Real entered the competition with four nominations, more than any other finalist: best opera house; best new production for 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'; best world premiere for 'Enemy of the People' by Francisco Coll; and an equal opportunities award tied to the Agrupación Musical Inclusiva. Matabosch noted that the recognition raises public awareness of the theatre as a top-level cultural institution deserving support.

Addressing broader industry concerns, Matabosch referenced budget difficulties raised by other winners such as the Bregenz Festival in Austria and Theater an der Wien itself, while asserting that Teatro Real's lower reliance on public subsidies grants it greater independence. Regarding allegations of censorship and political pressure made by Washington National Opera artistic director Francesca Zambello—attributed to conditions since President Donald Trump's election—he expressed skepticism about their applicability to Spain or other countries with deeply embedded cultural institutions.

The awards, established in 2012 through the initiative of British businessman Harry Hyman and supported by 'Opera' magazine editor John Allison as jury chair, also recognized Ópera de Tenerife (for 'Yerma'), soprano Saioa Hernández, Louise Alder (best female singer), Lawrence Brownlee (best male singer), conductor Riccardo Chailly, and the Ibáñez Atkinson Foundation. The text presents these statements from Matabosch and Zambello as their own views rather than established fact.
items.title: Madrid's Teatro Real Named World's Best Opera House for Second Time at International Opera Awards

items.summary:
The European Commission launched an investigation on Monday into a surge in low-cost imports of composite resins and glass fibre materials, primarily from China. The probe targets inputs widely used across renewable energy, electricity infrastructure, transport, aerospace, and defence sectors. According to the text, cheap Chinese imports have risen 25% over the past year, while the EU's trade deficit with China reached a record €1 billion per day. The investigation is expected to run nine to 11 months and could result in quotas or tariffs on composite materials entering the bloc.

Although China is the main focus, any safeguard measures would apply to imports from all of the EU's trading partners rather than just Beijing. This broader approach follows earlier findings that Chinese producers were circumventing previously imposed duties by shifting production abroad, prompting European manufacturers to seek stronger protection. Ludovic Piraux, president of Glass Fibre Europe, stated that the investigation confirms the seriousness of the situation facing Europe's composite input materials industries and frames it as essential for reducing energy dependency, strengthening defence, transforming mobility, and maintaining advanced manufacturing capacity.

The probe had been delayed while the Commission pursued bilateral negotiations with China. Those talks produced an October agreement covering only hybrid cars, which allows 350,000 Chinese hybrid vehicles onto the European market annually over four years at a fixed annual adjustment rate of 6%. Officials expect this deal to more than halve current Chinese hybrid car exports, and EU countries backed it on Friday with effect set for December 1. However, the agreement has done little to ease broader concerns about cheap Chinese imports across other sectors.

The Commission hopes to extend negotiations beyond cars; Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is expected to hold a video call with China's Wang Wentao in January, ahead of a meeting scheduled for March 2027. The text notes these are expectations and future dates rather than confirmed arrangements.
items.title: EU Launches Trade Defence Investigation Into Cheap Chinese Composite Imports

items.summary: The Tamagotchi, a digital pet toy created by Japan's Bandai and first launched in November 1996, marked the 30th anniversary of its release. It initially gained popularity among high school girls before becoming a social phenomenon; however, as initial demand faded, Bandai was left with large unsold inventory and recorded a special loss of ¥6 billion for the fiscal year ending March 1999, after which it halted sales. The company resumed selling Tamagotchi in 2004, this time targeting elementary school girls, and has since expanded its lineup to reflect changing trends—for example, the 2021 model added food-delivery features inspired by pandemic-era services, while a 2025 model allows players to connect devices for shared play. By summer of that year, cumulative sales of the Tamagotchi series had surpassed 100 million units. Following the 2004 revival, merchandise and anime gained popularity in Japan and abroad, including an official Bandai shop opened in Tokyo in 2007. To mark the milestone, Bandai held a Times Square event on Sunday featuring models from across its history and costumed performers; Taro Tsuji, chief Tamagotchi officer at Bandai, attended with fans. The text notes that Bandai began selling the series internationally in 1997.
items.title: Bandai's Tamagotchi digital pet toy marks its 30th anniversary

items.summary: According to Bloomberg's reporting citing Senator Bernie Moreno of Ohio—the Republican leading the legislative effort—negotiators have reportedly resolved all major issues in a proposed bill that would block Chinese automakers such as BYD from entering the American market. Moreno stated on Friday at the Capitol that lawmakers are 'super, super, super close' and that 'all the big issues are resolved.' The legislation aims to formalize existing restrictions by targeting connected vehicles made by automakers more than 15% owned by Chinese entities; under an earlier version of the bill, this threshold would have placed Mercedes-Benz above it due to combined Chinese shareholding. However, Moreno indicated the Mercedes issue is no longer on the table in the revised proposal, reasoning that the law targets only vehicles posing a threat to US national and economic security—claims he asserts do not apply to Mercedes-Benz. The article attributes specific ownership figures as reported: roughly 20% of Mercedes-Benz owned by Chinese entities (with state-owned BAIC Motor Corp. holding nearly 10%), and Geely founder Li Shufu also holding nearly 10%. Moreno noted that technical details remain unresolved, including battery technology provisions, and that the bill could pass independently or be attached to another legislative package such as annual defense policy legislation. The article frames this development within broader US efforts to limit China's influence in electric vehicles, batteries, and automotive technology, while noting these are reported claims rather than established fact.
items.title: US lawmakers nearing agreement to ban Chinese automakers from US market, exempting Mercedes-Benz

visual.alt: Bar chart. Chinese entities total in Mercedes-Benz 20 %; BAIC Motor Corp. (state-owned) in Mercedes-Benz 10 %; Li Shufu/Geely stake in Mercedes-Benz 10 %.

items.summary:
A report titled 'Negative prices in EU power markets,' prepared by economic consultancy Compass Lexecon for European industry association Eurelectric, argues that negative electricity prices do not necessarily signal market failure. Instead, when they reflect genuine supply and demand conditions rather than regulatory distortions or infrastructure constraints, these episodes can direct investment toward energy storage, demand-side flexibility, and electrification.

The analysis distinguishes between negative-price episodes driven by actual economic conditions—supportive of flexible resources—and those sustained by poorly designed support mechanisms that create inefficiencies. The report notes significant variation in the frequency of negative prices across European markets: Spain and the Netherlands recorded them during approximately 7% of hours in 2025, while Finland saw a decline from 8.3% of hours in 2024 to 5.3%, reaching roughly 1% in the first half of 2026.

Eurelectric attributes Finland's improvement partly to electrification and battery storage expanding the system's ability to absorb surplus electricity. However, the study cautions that price signals alone may not spur investment when regulatory barriers or infrastructure limitations persist. It also warns that some generation support contracts—particularly older schemes—encourage facilities to keep producing during negative-price periods to retain payments, leading generators to bid below variable costs and distort market signals.

The report examines contract for difference (CfD) configurations, including designs that suspend support during certain negative-price windows or decouple support from actual output. It also assesses long-term flexibility procurement mechanisms as a way to improve revenue predictability while avoiding distortion of competition with unsupplied assets in balancing and ancillary markets.

The findings arrive amid EU member states' national flexibility needs assessments (FNAs). Citing Entso-E estimates, the report projects that European electricity system flexibility needs could double by 2033 due to renewable growth, electrification, and shifting consumption. It recommends that these assessments distinguish market-meetable from structurally limited needs.

Compass Lexecon identifies three action areas: limiting distortive incentives in support mechanisms, removing barriers to flexible resource participation, and using additional procurement instruments where market-driven investment falls short.
items.title: Compass Lexecon Report Frames Negative EU Electricity Prices as a Flexibility Signal

items.summary: Foreign Minister Penny Wong is set to deliver a major foreign policy address to the Senate on Tuesday, warning that rivalry between the United States and China is eroding international stability and raising the risk of conflict. She argues both powers are increasingly willing to act without regard for the rules that historically prevented great-power confrontation, leaving institutions like the UN paralysed by tensions and unable to resolve disputes effectively. Wong contends Australia must strengthen ties with other nations—including in Africa and Latin America—to safeguard its independence as superpowers compete across every domain. She notes China is intensifying efforts to reshape the multilateral system amid what she describes as the largest military build-up since World War II, while also observing that US policy direction remains contested domestically following midterm elections. Wong frames Australia's approach around 'amplified middle power diplomacy,' arguing that mid-sized powers have nearly doubled in number since the Cold War even as US and Chinese shares of global GDP have plateaued; however, she cautions that growing instability makes it more costly for smaller nations to maintain their positions. She rejects abandoning multilateralism despite its imperfections, instead calling for reform including changes to the UN Security Council, warning that vacuums left by institutional failure are 'rarely filled by peace.' The speech follows recent summitry involving Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, which produced a joint declaration omitting references to Ukraine and Iran. Coverage reflects Wong's stated positions as reported ahead of her address; specific claims about China's military build-up and US policy shifts are attributed to her assertions rather than independently verified evidence.
items.title: Australia's Foreign Minister Warns of US-China Rivalry Undermining Global Stability

items.summary: During the inaugural Jordan-EU Investment Conference, Jordan's Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources announced plans to invite private investors to develop a 200 MW solar project and a 100 MW/400 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in the new year. Both projects will follow a build-own-operate model, with state-owned National Electric Power Company purchasing electricity from the solar project and serving as beneficiary of the storage project. The solar project is estimated to require $100 million to $130 million in investment, with initial requests for investor prequalifications expected in February 2027; the BESS is projected to cost between $70 million and $90 million, with an initial request anticipated in March 2027. Further details, including project locations, remain unannounced. These two projects are part of a broader investment package that also includes plans for a 100 MW wind project, a 450 MW pumped-storage hydropower project, shared infrastructure for green hydrogen and green ammonia production, and natural gas infrastructure projects. According to the Jordan News Agency, the initiatives aim to attract international investment, expand private sector participation in energy infrastructure, strengthen energy security, and support cleaner energy transition. Contextual figures show that Jordan's cumulative solar capacity stood at 2,195 MW by the end of 2025 per IRENA data (unchanged from the prior year), and the country's energy regulator approved its first 200 renewable energy systems in September under a revised regulatory framework. The text notes these projects are part of Jordan's efforts to attract international investment, expand private sector participation in energy infrastructure, strengthen energy security, and support cleaner energy transition.
items.title: Jordan Unveils Plans for New Solar and Battery Storage Projects at Jordan-EU Investment Conference

visual.alt: Bar chart. Solar project capacity 200 mw; BESS capacity 100 mw.

items.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attributed a drone attack on Sunday to Ukraine, stating that seven Ukrainian-made naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury and struck the cargo vessel MV ANGARA near Benghazi. According to Zelenskyy's post on X, the Merkury was one of Russia's newest ships commissioned during the 2023 invasion, while he described the ANANGA as a ship Moscow used to transport weapons; he also claimed a combat military helicopter was destroyed in the operation. Russian officials made no immediate comment.

Libyan sources provided independent confirmation that the attack severely damaged a Russian navy corvette at the Benghazi Naval Base, with residents reporting explosions and fire early Sunday before civil defence extinguished it. Libyan authorities said the vessel had docked to refuel as part of an unspecified Russia-Libya cooperation agreement, though they did not identify the ship or its cargo.

The United Nations mission in Libya expressed serious concern over the strikes, calling for an immediate, independent and transparent investigation and warning that Libya must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts. The attacks followed a separate drone strike on Saturday against a Russian cargo ship near Finnish waters in the eastern Baltic Sea; Kyiv did not comment on that incident but the Finnish military assessed it was likely carried out by Ukraine, with all 16 crew evacuated to a nearby Russian ship and one person slightly injured.
items.title: Ukraine Claims Drone Attack Sank Russian Warship Off Libya

items.summary:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed Ukraine conducted drone strikes near the Libyan port of Benghazi that sank a Russian corvette (Merkury) and hit another vessel. According to his account posted on X, seven Ukrainian-made naval drones were deployed against two targets: the Merkury, which he described as one of Russia's newest ships commissioned in 2023 during the full-scale war; and the dry cargo vessel MV ANGARA, allegedly used by Russia to transport weapons. Zelenskyy also stated that a Ka-27 combat helicopter was destroyed during the attack on the Merkury.

The strikes occurred amid reports of Ukraine expanding its operations against Russian vessels beyond front-line areas, including a drone strike near Finland's border waters in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday. The United Nations expressed serious concern over the attacks and called for an immediate, independent, and transparent investigation, warning that Libya must not become 'a battleground for foreign conflicts.'

The incident follows precedent: in March, a Russian liquefied natural gas carrier sank off the Libyan coast after an attack that Putin blamed on Ukraine. This vessel was part of Russia's shadow fleet used to circumvent Western restrictions. Ukraine has previously acknowledged attacking elements of this fleet, including in the Mediterranean last December.

The Tripoli government rejected attempts to use Libya as a venue for international conflicts or military activities threatening its sovereignty. The country remains divided between Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah's administration and rival commander Khalifa Haftar since 2011.
items.title: Ukraine Claims Drone Strikes on Two Russian Ships Off Libya, UN Condemns Attacks

items.summary:
Data center developers increasingly face electricity supply constraints and are turning to on-site fossil gas plants, but those plans carry high equipment costs, long turbine backlogs, and public opposition. A report from the think tank Energy Innovation proposes an alternative: hybrid thermal power systems that store heat in rocks or bricks—reaching temperatures above 1,000 degrees Celsius (1,832 degrees Fahrenheit)—and convert it to electricity via steam turbines when solar and wind generation is unavailable. The approach can be cost-competitive with gas in many regions while delivering power within a year or two, faster than the multi-year waits for backlogged gas plants.

The core tradeoff is efficiency: thermal energy storage recovers only about 40% of input energy due to losses converting heat to steam and then electricity, versus the low-to-mid-90% round-trip efficiency typical of lithium-ion batteries. Report author Eric Gimon nonetheless found it cost-effective because cheap renewable power offsets those losses; over longer durations thermal storage can be cheaper than conventional battery systems.

Gimon estimated hybrid thermal "brick" systems could provide reliable, around-the-clock power at roughly $120 per megawatt-hour—including the cost of developing their solar and wind supply—comparable to dedicated gas plants. Location-specific references range from about $72 per MWh for a West Texas data center to $140–$165 per MWh, which investment bank Jeffries estimated Meta pays for an off-grid Ohio gas plant.

Despite the report's optimism, Gimon noted he is unaware of any U.S. data center currently using this approach, even though heat batteries from companies including Antora, Brenmiller Energy, Electrified Thermal Solutions, and Rondo Energy are available—most installed systems today supply industrial process heat rather than electricity.

Startup Cache Energy's CEO Arpit Dwivedi said the industry could scale quickly; his technology uses standard steel components with limestone-derived pellets. He cited current capacity of about 1 GWh per year, projecting scaling to 10 GWh in 12 months and 100 GWh in 24 months without major difficulty.

The report's projections carry notable caveats: Dwivedi emphasized that adoption at scale requires one or two real projects demonstrating success with data centers specifically. The $120/MWh figure is an estimate, and the efficiency losses remain a drawback relative to batteries—tolerable only if renewable power stays cheap enough and electricity value remains high.
items.title: Hybrid Thermal Power as a Fast, Clean Alternative to Gas for Off-Grid Data Centers

visual.alt: Bar chart. Hybrid Thermal 'Brick' System (incl. renewables) 120 $; Dedicated Gas Plant, West Texas Data Center 72 $; Off-Grid Gas Power Plant (Meta, Ohio) 165 $.

items.summary: A report from the energy think tank Ember argues that diversifying electricity generation with wind power lowers costs and improves reliability compared to solar alone. Daan Walter of Ember explained that relying on a single source is risky, comparing it to depending on one crop; batteries serve as storage for daytime solar output. The analysis found that in the United States and Europe, achieving 90 percent uptime requires about 20 hours of battery storage with solar only, but adding wind reduces this to roughly 12 hours, cutting lithium-ion installation needs. Globally, combining wind could lower the median cost of meeting 90 percent demand from $105 per megawatt-hour (solar alone) to around $86. Reliability varies by latitude: near the equator, solar and batteries reach 90 percent uptime for under $60 per megawatt-hour, while areas above 55 degrees north cost about $280 without wind; adding wind brings costs below $100 at every latitude tested. Al-Amin Bugaje of Project Drawdown, who was not involved in the research, noted that these figures suggest clean power can be competitively priced and reliable enough to avoid continued fossil-fuel development. The report also addresses dunkelflaute—periods with simultaneously low sun and wind—which occur on average about four times yearly for solar and eight for wind globally; combining both sources reduces such combined outages to roughly once every four years, though sufficient storage would still be needed to bridge them without resorting to gas or coal. The findings are drawn from Ember's analysis and represent projections rather than established outcomes.
items.title: Combining Solar and Wind Reduces Battery Needs and Grid Costs, Per Ember Report

visual.alt: Bar chart. Solar only (equator) 60 $; Wind + solar (above 55°N) 100 $.

items.summary: A record-strength 'super' or 'Godzilla' El Niño event, the strongest on record and expected to persist through March, is producing sharply divergent starts to the 2024-25 ski season across regions. In the Northeast, unseasonably warm conditions—highs approaching 60°F at Sugarbush in Vermont over much of November—are delaying openings; Sugarbush had hoped to run lifts and open slopes by Thanksgiving but has not yet done so. This pattern is shared across many eastern resorts, from Sugarloaf in Maine to Snowshoe Mountain in West Virginia. Conversely, California's Lake Tahoe area received more than 4 feet of snow after a recent storm series, prompting the Sierra Avalanche Center to warn of 'considerable' slide risk and allowing Kirkwood Mountain Resort to open nearly two weeks ahead of schedule; general manager Ricky Newberry called early opening 'a huge win.' In Colorado, Wolf Creek has opened all its terrain despite an initially slow start. Meteorologist Chris Tomer attributes these contrasts to El Niño's regional effects—wetter-than-normal California and the Northeast versus a drier Northwest—and projects that Sierra Nevada resorts could receive 100 to 200 inches more snow than usual over the season, while northeastern storms may fall as rain given warmer temperatures. The article notes this year resembles the 2015-16 'super' El Niño in blessing the West and stressing the East, but cautions that accelerating climate change is making skiable-snow guarantees harder to achieve even in normal years; resorts have invested millions in advanced snow-making equipment—modern guns can operate when temperatures dip for only hours—to extend operational windows. However, Sugarbush's John Bleh warns against over-relying on the technology, noting it still depends on sufficiently cold temperatures and long enough windows to be worthwhile.
items.title: El Niño is already scrambling your ski season

items.summary:
The COP31 summit held in Antalya, Turkey, ended as the longest-running climate talks in UN history to fail on its central political agreement—the Antalya Pacts—primarily because nations could not agree on including language about fossil fuels and on how much additional money rich countries should provide for developing-nation adaptation. The failure occurred despite Australia and Turkey co-hosting the negotiations and came at a time when evidence of climate change was prominent, with 2026 marked by glacier collapses, record European heat, and Asian wildfires.

The talks took place after the UN warned that global temperatures are expected to exceed 1.5C above pre-industrial levels—the threshold countries agreed not to breach in the 2015 Paris Climate Agreement—and a draft agreement had acknowledged this overshoot would occur. Scientists from the IPCC, roughly a decade earlier, projected consequences of exceeding 1.5C versus 2C: sea level rise about 10cm higher (exposing an additional ~10 million people to flooding), increased ocean acidity risking marine life, and extreme heat in every inhabited region.

Despite the failure on the central agreement, some progress was made among other agenda items; funds from a global carbon-credit system were directed toward helping developing countries adapt, and a just transition framework protecting workers during shifts to clean energy was advanced. The article notes that 164 other agenda items were being negotiated at COP31.

Separately, the International Energy Agency's World Energy Outlook attributes continued renewable-energy growth partly to energy security concerns—citing disruption from oil and gas supplies through the Strait of Hormuz as the largest supply shock in history—and changing economics making solar panels, batteries, and electric vehicles increasingly competitive. IEA head Fatih Birol stated that "we have arrived at the age of electricity," while Dr Jennie Dodson of the World Business Council for Sustainable Development noted cost competitiveness but flagged policy barriers around infrastructure and permitting.

The article frames COP31 as an "implementation COP"—the first since Paris in 2015 established the framework, with subsequent agreements (a climate-damage fund at COP27, a fossil-fuel transition commitment at COP28, a new finance target at COP29, and increased adaptation support at COP30) building that architecture. It suggests future conferences may become more procedural, possibly abandoning cover texts like the Antalya Pacts.

The text notes fundamental limitations: under the Paris Agreement there is no mechanism to force countries to meet emissions targets, so critics blaming the process are criticized by negotiator Alden Meyer of E3G as misdirected—the COP "is like a mirror that we hold up to ourselves every year," with disappointing reflections reflecting governments rather than the system. The article also notes contested interpretations of prior commitments, including last year's pledge to triple adaptation funding from $40bn (£30bn) by 2035.
items.title: Failed COP31 Climate Talks in Turkey

items.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party initiated the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) Awareness Pad Yatra in Karimnagar as part of a nationwide campaign, with the stated aim of educating citizens on the democratic process and the benefits of the voter-list revision exercise. The party framed the event around protecting eligible voters' rights while distinguishing its public engagement from opposition rallies; according to the report, attendees expressed confidence in democracy and rejected claims by opponents regarding voter lists and election procedures. Separately, a review petition was filed concerning lamp-lighting arrangements at Tirupparankundram hill for Karthigai Deepam amid law-and-order concerns. The accompanying news items—regional industrial investment competition between Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, the launch of an actor-focused forum in Tamil Nadu, and India–Nepal agreements including a direct Ayodhya–Janakpur rail service—are listed without further detail or connection to the main event.
items.title: BJP Launches SIR Awareness Pad Yatra in Karimnagar

items.summary:
A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson stated that China is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both countries, in response to reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals. According to PTI, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly granted visas to attend this month's China International Import Expo in Shanghai, and Beijing has stopped the China Visa Application Centre—a private service provider—from accepting applications, with embassies now handling them directly amid rising demand for business visas.

The remarks come against a backdrop of ongoing efforts to normalize bilateral relations. India resumed issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July after a five-year gap, part of broader measures that also included resuming direct air connectivity between cities such as Beijing and New Delhi following the 2020 Galwan Valley clashes. Indian officials report that visa rejection rates for Chinese nationals have fallen to around seven percent recently.

China launched its "China Online Visa Application System" for Indian applicants in December, allowing online applications. Separately addressing bilateral relations after a Modi–Xi meeting at the September Brics summit in New Delhi, the spokesperson said both leaders agreed China and India should be partners, with each side working to strengthen ties and support mutual development.

The article notes that visa arrangements have improved since July but does not provide details on how many visas were denied or confirm whether a formal dispute over issuance has been formally raised between the two governments.
items.title: China Offers Cooperation on Business Visa Arrangements Amid Reports of Reduced Issuance

items.summary: The opposition YSRCP, through Tirupati MP Maddila Gurumoorthy, demanded that the Election Commission of India (EC) investigate an alleged discrepancy in post-6 pm voter queues during the May 13, 2024 simultaneous polls for the Chittoor Lok Sabha constituency and its seven Assembly segments. The demand follows a report by 'The Reporters' Collective,' which claimed officials recorded 56,067 voters waiting after the 6 pm deadline for the Chittoor parliamentary seat, compared with only 24,596 across the seven Assembly constituencies under it—Kuppam, Nagari, Chandragiri, Nellore, Chittoor, Palamaner, and Puthalapattu. Gurumoorthy characterized this gap as exceeding 31,000 voters or over 100 percent between the two counts, arguing that such a divergence warrants an independent inquiry alongside public disclosure of polling records and action taken. He framed the issue within broader concerns about ECINet, electoral rolls, objections raised internally at the Commission, and prior ignored appeals related to Andhra Pradesh's SIR and local body delimitation. Additionally, Gurumoorthy called on the Union Government to amend a 2023 law governing election commissioner appointments—legislation YSRCP had previously supported—to restore a selection committee comprising the Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India, and Leader of the Opposition, arguing this would strengthen Commission independence and public trust. TDP national spokesperson Deepak Reddy responded via PTI that the ruling party could not address the allegations and deferred to the poll body. The article notes as context that in 2024's simultaneous elections, the NDA coalition (BJP, TDP, Janasena) won a landslide of 164 of 175 Assembly seats and 21 of 25 Lok Sabha constituencies.
items.title: YSRCP Demands EC Probe Over Voter-Queue Discrepancy in Chittoor Polls

items.summary: At a joint press conference in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed Nepalese counterpart Balen Shah on his first visit to the Indian capital and emphasized that India shares deep cultural and religious ties with Nepal. Modi recalled his 2018 state visit to Janakpur, where he had declared Lord Ram was 'incomplete without Nepal,' a statement he repeated during the meeting. He attributed the strength of bilateral relations to shared history, faith, culture, and people-to-people connections, noting that both leaders framed these ties as rooted in the sacred era of Lord Ram and Mata Janaki. Shah echoed Modi's sentiments, describing India-Nepal bonds as 'as strong as the Himalayas.' The two leaders flagged off the Sarayu-Kamala Express connecting Ayodhya with Janakpur Dham to strengthen connectivity between the countries. Beyond symbolic gestures, the visit produced concrete agreements: at least eight memorandums of understanding covering satellite technology, governance, education, healthcare, urban development, and traditional medicine; a development cooperation package worth 24,000 crore Nepali rupees (₹15,000 crore) in response to Nepal's recent flash floods; and an announced plan for India to establish an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), alongside a startup incubator and innovation hub. Shah invited Modi to visit Nepal and encouraged Indians to travel to religious sites such as Pashupatinath.
items.title: Modi and Balen Shah Frame India-Nepal Ties Around Shared Ramayana Heritage

items.summary: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam administration filed a review petition with the Supreme Court contesting its interim order of 20 November, which permitted one-time lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon atop Tirupparankundram hill for the Karthigai Deepam festival. The court's conditional permission directed the Madurai Collector and temple authorities to ensure adequate security during the ritual, but the state government raised concerns about both the execution of the order and law-and-order management amid a major conflict over the lighting. Separately reported in the source text are unrelated items: Andhra Pradesh signing MOUs worth nearly nine lakh crore rupees as it competes with Tamil Nadu for industrial and automotive investments; a fan group, Ilaya Puratchi Thalaivi Trisha Peravai, drawing political comparisons between actor Trisha and former CM Jayalalithaa after its launch in Tamil Nadu; India and Nepal signing agreements and launching an Ayodhya–Janakpur rail service during a state visit; and additional local concerns including a missing child and harassment allegations involving an MLA. The source text is a news compilation containing these distinct, unverified claims without supporting evidence or attribution for the figures cited.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Files Review Petition in Supreme Court Over Tirupparankundram Karthigai Deepam Lighting

items.summary:
On Monday, a Supreme Court bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana ruled that only vehicles meeting BS-VI emission standards should be permitted to ply in Delhi during the pollution-prone winter months. The court framed its directive as applying at minimum to Delhi, with language suggesting it may extend to the broader National Capital Region (NCR). While discussing air quality for November, the bench attributed the capital's avoidance of 'severe' category pollution primarily to favourable winds rather than enforcement efforts—a point disputed by additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, who argued that authorities' measures also contributed. The court's directive aligns with and reinforces existing Delhi government restrictions under a notification effective November 1 through January 31 annually, which bars BS-IV-and-older commercial goods vehicles (including light, medium, heavy trucks and buses) from entering the capital while exempting CNG, electric, emergency, and other specified categories. Enforcement is being carried out at entry points such as DND, Rajokri, Ghazipur, Singhu, Tikri, and Badarpur using personnel, special teams, and automatic number plate recognition cameras.

Beyond immediate restrictions, the bench indicated it was considering a more comprehensive approach that could extend beyond Delhi's current framework. It floated a five-year roadmap to progressively eliminate polluting commercial vehicles from Delhi without disrupting essential goods supply, proposing border warehousing where goods would be unloaded and moved into the city via battery-operated or non-polluting transport—though acknowledging this may not be feasible immediately or even next year.

The court's focus on vehicular emissions is contextualized by data from the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology's Air Quality Early Warning System, which estimated that around 21.5% of Delhi's PM2.5 pollution came from intra-city transport while roughly 60% originated outside the city as of November 23—underscoring the need for coordinated regional action. The same estimates placed stubble burning at less than 1% on that day, though noting this figure can vary considerably across the season.

The respite in air quality remained fragile: Delhi's conditions fluctuated between 'poor' and 'very poor,' with the Commission for Air Quality Management invoking Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan on November 6 after forecasting possible deterioration into severe category, before withdrawing emergency measures on November 17 as air quality improved. The bench indicated it would examine further short-term and long-term interventions, with senior advocate Aparajita Singh assisting as amicus curiae.
items.title: Supreme Court Orders BS-VI-Only Vehicles in Delhi During Winter

items.summary: Scientists report that untrained bumblebees can spontaneously devise new solutions to obtain rewards, building on earlier experiments demonstrating their capacity for teamwork and cognition despite small brains. The research involved a series of trials in which the bees encountered an obstacle blocking access to a sweet reward; according to the source's promotional framing, viewers were invited to watch video footage showing how the insects worked through the hurdle. No quantitative data or specific experimental details are provided beyond these qualitative claims.
items.title: Untrained Bumblebees Find Novel Solutions to Reach Rewards

items.summary: After losing eight World Test Championship points in a draw against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve, India can only derive some consolation from their effort to win on an unhelpful surface. Despite looking set for 12 WTC points during Monday's final day, they settled for four after Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips defended a resolute draw dictated by the track's slowness. The ball offered little movement once it was more than 30 overs old, nullifying even Bumrah's early brilliance on day one. India posted their highest-ever Test total overseas of 720 for nine declared, with KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant leading a strong batting display that saw both become only the fifth and sixth Indians to score Test hundreds in South Africa, England, New Zealand, and Australia (the SENA countries). Pant's return from injury was notable as he stood out for his stroke production. However, questions persist over the omissions of Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja; despite Siraj's close to 150 Test wickets since December 2020 debut and Jadeja's 358 wickets from 91 Tests overseas, leadership chose Anshul Kamboj and Washington instead. With just six games remaining in the WTC standings, India need a minimum of five wins to stay in contention for a top-two finish, with their next Test at Christchurch starting Friday.
items.title: India's Draw at Wellington Costs WTC Points Amid Selection Questions

visual.alt: Bar chart. Games remaining 6; Wins needed to stay in hunt 5.

items.summary: Google announced that its Google Search is being made more personalized through the expansion of 'Personal Intelligence,' a system that connects user apps to deliver responses tailored to individual context. Starting today, users can opt in to connect Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence in both AI Mode and the Gemini app; Drive support follows in coming weeks. Gmail, Calendar, and Photos already provide personalization. The Wallet connection enables spending analysis—such as mapping financial milestones and optimizing credit card benefits like cash-back categories—and travel perks based on linked cards, though it can only read account information without moving or managing funds. Google Drive integration allows responses that incorporate context from documents, spreadsheets, and PDFs to help users initiate projects or decisions. Additionally, in coming weeks, users will be able to share context between the Gemini app and AI Mode so searches build on prior exploration; Search history can already be connected within the Gemini app. Opt-in is handled through 'Search Personalization' under 'Connected Apps,' where users control which apps are linked and may view or edit the personalization settings at any time, including instructing AI Mode to change responses such as dietary preferences. Google also noted that more personally relevant responses will appear in both AI Overviews and AI Mode based on recent search context. The announcement did not provide specific rollout dates beyond 'coming weeks' for Drive support and Gemini-to-AI Mode sharing, nor independent verification of the underlying Personal Intelligence technology's accuracy or coverage.
items.title: Google Rolls Out Expanded Personal Intelligence App Connections for Tailored AI Mode and Gemini Responses

items.summary:
On Nov 23, Nvidia shares rose nearly 30% after the board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang as chief executive. The move followed a technology-led market rout earlier in the week during which major indices fell between 7% and 10%. Huang had resigned less than two weeks prior amid an alleged Chinese spy scandal and allegations of an affair with an employee, prompting him to resign. Trump, who advocated for Huang's return, stated on social media that investigators have no reason to believe his reinstatement poses a national security risk.

The news triggered immediate gains in US markets: the Nasdaq rose more than 6%, the Dow added 2.6%, and the S&P 500 climbed 4.5% early in the session, while European markets gained around 1.5%. In contrast, Asian tech stocks remained weak; Seoul slid by more than 3%, with analysts noting that key semiconductor suppliers SK hynix and Samsung continued to underperform.

Investment strategists cautioned that volatility was not over, as Nvidia remained under scrutiny from the FBI and Capitol Hill regarding the spy scandal. To mitigate market declines, authorities in Taiwan restricted short-selling, China eased borrowing for stock purchases, and South Korea considered a stabilization fund last used since the global financial crisis.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Reinstatement Sparks Stock Rally Amid Ongoing Investigation

items.summary: An NVIDIA promotional piece frames the holiday season as an opportunity for consumers to upgrade hobbies—gaming, content creation, or robotics—with its technologies. For gaming, it highlights GeForce RTX 50 Series laptops and desktops built on Blackwell architecture with fifth-generation Tensor Cores and fourth-generation RT Cores, alongside RTX Spark PCs combining RTX graphics with a full-stack AI platform; DLSS 5 (including the new DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering feature) for performance and image quality boosts demonstrated in NBA 2K27; NVIDIA Reflex and G-SYNC for responsiveness and smooth refresh rates; and GeForce NOW cloud gaming, which offers more than 4,500 titles across compatible devices. For creators, the text points to GeForce RTX 50 Series and RTX Spark systems paired with Studio Drivers and AI acceleration tools supporting video editing, 3D design, and livestreaming. For robotics, it describes the NVIDIA Jetson edge AI platform—combining compact computers with the JetPack SDK—to build robots that perform computer vision tasks such as identifying a candy cane or distinguishing frosted from unfrosted gingerbread men under varied lighting; specific examples include Microduck (Jetson Orin Nano Super), agentic robotics via an SO-101 arm on Jetson Orin, and robot companions using Nemotron 3.5 Bolt and Cosmos models locally on the Jetson Orin Nano 8GB. The article notes that advanced projects can use vision language action models and world action models for reasoning and planning beyond simple perception, with tutorials available in Jetson AI Lab. items.title: NVIDIA Promotes Holiday Hobby Upgrades Across Gaming, Creation, and Robotics

items.summary:
On an unspecified date, the NVIDIA board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as President, Chief Executive Officer, and member of the board effective immediately. The decision followed a series of discussions in which the board concluded it was satisfied with Huang's candor and leadership ability; Harvey C. Jones, board chair, stated that the reinstatement is believed to be in the best interests of stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. In reaching its conclusion, the board received input from senior U.S. government levels and expressed confidence that Huang poses no national security risk. Huang issued a statement expressing gratitude for the board's deliberation and his willingness to resume leadership.

The reinstatement follows prior reporting that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board had formed an investigation committee of independent directors with retained counsel, which it said would proceed to conclusion; Huang stated he fully supports the investigation and will cooperate. Separately, the board established a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors overseeing trade compliance, engaging national security–experienced counsel who in turn retain advisors. NVIDIA announced it is searching for a new Chief Compliance Officer reporting to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and said it would continue cooperating with government investigations.

The text presents these actions as board decisions reflecting stated confidence but does not provide independent verification of Huang's candor, leadership ability, or absence of national security risk; those assessments are attributed solely to the board and its reliance on U.S. government input.
items.title: NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After National Security Investigation

items.summary: Amazon has agreed to acquire a portion of Israeli startup Decart for approximately $7.5 billion, according to Bloomberg. The deal centers on the technology behind Decart's Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that improves how AI models run efficiently across Nvidia, Amazon, and Google hardware, along with Decart's founding team and its researchers and engineers. While Decart is publicly known for building interactive real-time world models such as Oasis 3 and AI video generation tools, the acquisition targets DOS specifically. In an internal blog post, Peter DeSantis, senior vice president of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing at Amazon, stated that more efficient compute enables better training, reinforcement learning, faster inference, and lower-cost models for customers. The purchase aligns with Amazon's broader strategy: the company has been using its Trainium chips in-house but is preparing to sell them as a competitor to Nvidia, and Decart's technology could help customers run workloads on Amazon hardware rather than Nvidia's. Both companies declined to comment immediately after the report.
items.title: Amazon to Acquire Decart's AI Optimization Technology for $7.5 Billion

items.summary: The Nasdaq-100 rose 6.6% to close at 26,680.6 points, positioning it for its largest single-day percentage gain since April 2025. The rally was driven primarily by a more than 31% surge in Nvidia shares after the company announced Huang's return as leader—a reversal of his resignation that reportedly followed revelations about extramarital relationships and an alleged association with a Chinese spy, amid calls from President Donald Trump for his reinstatement. Broad-based gains accompanied the move: Alphabet climbed 6%, Meta gained more than 5%, Amazon advanced nearly 5%, Microsoft rose 4%, SpaceX jumped 9%, AMD gained over 8.5%, while neocloud stocks Nebius (more than 30%), CoreWeave, and Iren each rose about 28%. Anthropic shares stayed largely flat after an early premarket spike during its third trading session following a Thursday IPO. The article's figures are drawn from the source outlet ETMarkets; some percentages were rounded in reporting.
items.title: Nasdaq-100 Posts Largest Single-Day Gain Since April 2025 on Nvidia's Leadership Reversal

items.summary: Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas extended his contract to lead the chip designer through 2033, confirming his continued leadership amid speculation that Nvidia could recruit him as its next chief executive. The speculation stems from Jensen Huang's resignation earlier in the month following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. According to the Financial Times, Nvidia's board had approached Haas during its search for a successor; Colette Kress currently serves as interim CEO at Nvidia. Analysts cited Haas's long tenure with Nvidia—rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business before joining Arm in 2013—as making him a strong candidate, alongside his status as a high-profile semiconductor figure familiar with the company. In response to the speculation, US-listed shares of Arm rose nearly 9 per cent in premarket trading on November 23, riding a broader rebound in AI stocks after a selloff the prior week; Haas stated he had never been more confident about Arm's future and remained wholly committed to realizing its potential. Separately, Arm announced that Haas would assume the role of vice chairman of SoftBank Group effective December 1, building on his existing board membership and April takeover of SoftBank's international business operations.
items.title: Arm CEO Rene Haas Extends Contract Through 2033 Amid Nvidia Succession Speculation

items.summary: The NVIDIA board unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as President, Chief Executive Officer, and director with immediate effect, ending his interim absence. In his first public statement, Huang expressed gratitude for the board's decision and thanked interim leaders Harvey Jones (chair) and Colette Kress (interim CEO), who will retain their respective roles. The announcement coincided with a sharp stock rally: NVIDIA shares rose to $168.02 in premarket trading on Monday, up 33.85% from Friday's close of $125.53, adding roughly $1 trillion to market capitalization and potentially becoming the first company ever to add that amount in a single day if it closes at or above those levels. The rebound reversed heavy losses across AI-linked stocks during the prior week. Peer semiconductor companies also advanced—AMD and Broadcom each gained about 4%, Taiwan Semiconductor rose 6%, ASML gained 6%, Micron up roughly 5%, SK Hynix up about 9%—while AI infrastructure names CoreWeave and Nebius surged more than 25%. Anthropic's shares recovered approximately 5% after a Friday decline of 9%. Separately, the board confirmed that an independent investigation into reported foreign intelligence efforts targeting Huang would continue despite his reinstatement. The article presents these figures as premarket or intraday data from Yahoo Finance and does not provide closing prices to confirm whether NVIDIA actually achieved its projected $1 trillion daily market-cap gain.
items.title: NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after board vote, triggering a more than 30% stock surge

items.summary:
NVIDIA, in collaboration with the University of Wisconsin–Madison and DuckLabs, released Sirius—an open-source, GPU-native SQL engine—as a core extension for DuckDB 2.0 to accelerate analytical queries on NVIDIA GPUs without requiring users to rewrite their SQL or alter database schemas. The workflow requires only two commands: INSTALL sirius; and LOAD sirius;, which download the approximately 700 MB extension (download time dependent on connection speed) and activate it in the current session, with DuckDB automatically selecting a compatible CUDA backend for the installed driver.

The integration divides responsibilities between the two engines: DuckDB handles SQL parsing and optimization while Sirius executes supported query plans on the GPU. Queries containing unsupported features automatically fall back to DuckDB's CPU engine. The article demonstrates this using the TPC-H extension with scale factor 0.01, which generates sample tables including lineitem; a CHECKPOINT persists these native DuckDB tables so Sirius can read them directly.

The benchmark evaluation compared tuned two-GPU Sirius configurations against the best tested CPU-based DuckDB setups across four Amazon S3-backed datasets at TPC-H scale factors of 100 (100 GB), 1,000 (1 TB), 3,000 (3 TB), and 10,000 (10 TB). Using pinned development builds with cold runs, Sirius achieved speedups ranging from 3.25x to 5.50x over CPU-based DuckDB under tuned settings. Specific results included a reduction in total query runtime at SF1K from 347.3 seconds to 63.2 seconds and at SF3K from 752.4 seconds to 160.6 seconds (a 4.69x speedup), with query-time compute cost decreasing by approximately 71% at SF3K.

The largest relative advantage appeared at the largest scale: at SF10K, tuned two-GPU Sirius completed in 729.9 seconds versus 2,369.4 seconds for CPU-based DuckDB (a 3.25x speedup and approximately 79% lower query-time compute cost). Configuration choices shifted with workload size—single GPU was lowest-cost at SF100 while two GPUs gave shortest runtime—and tuning proved critical at scale, where the default two-GPU configuration did not finish at SF10K but completed in 729.9 seconds when tuned.

The article notes that Sirius timings exclude result fetch/export and DuckDB timings include CSV output; query-time compute costs cover measured instance runtime while excluding startup, validation, storage, S3, and idle time. The authors caution that results vary with query structure, dataset size, hardware, and cache conditions, as the small example is not intended to demonstrate a performance advantage.
items.title: NVIDIA and DuckLabs Release Sirius as a GPU-Accelerated DuckDB Core Extension

visual.alt: Bar chart. SF100 (100 GB) - runtime speedup 5.5 x; SF3K (3 TB) - total query runtime speedup 4.69 x; SF10K (10 TB) - total query runtime speedup 3.25 x.

items.summary: Indian security and intelligence agencies have detected Pakistani intelligence operatives infiltrating approximately 13-14 private WhatsApp groups used by Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) personnel and defence-civilian officials, according to news agency PTI citing unnamed officials on Monday. In response, the agencies have ordered a comprehensive audit of social communication platforms. The reported figure of around 13-14 affected groups is attributed to official sources cited through PTI rather than independently verified data.
items.title: Pakistani Operatives Detected in Defence and CAPF WhatsApp Groups; Security Agencies Order Platform Audit

items.summary:
President Trump told CNBC that he spoke 'directly and indirectly' with Nvidia's board about reinstating CEO Jensen Huang, saying the administration gave assurances on national security risks after the board requested them. He also said he personally spoke with Huang before his reinstatement was announced, arguing it would be a greater threat to lose Huang's expertise than to bring him back.

The reinstatement follows reports that Alice Huang, Jensen's wife, contacted an official in China's Ministry of State Security for over a year during their affair. Trump claimed the government conducted 'a very thorough investigation' and concluded Huang did nothing wrong but had poor judgment on unrelated matters.

Lawmakers pushed back against the decision. Senator Pete Ricketts said Huang's behavior doesn't support reinstatement, while Senators John Curtis and John Cornyn questioned what basis Nvidia used to conclude there was no national security risk. Elizabeth Warren called it 'reckless,' Illinois Governor JB Pritzker accused Trump of selling out national security for stock market gains, and Ron Wyden claimed the situation shows national security is 'up for sale.'

Huang faces testimony before multiple committees: a closed-door transcribed interview with three House committees on December 1, an open Senate banking committee hearing on December 3 titled 'Protecting America's AI Advantage,' plus Nvidia executives scheduled to testify. California Attorney General Rob Bonta said the reinstatement doesn't change ongoing investigations into whether Nvidia misled investors or sent technology to China.

Separately, Joe Kasper, a former chief of staff to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, told Politico that Hegseth should resign for prioritizing his image over institutional leadership. The article also notes an altered meme image superimposing Huang's face and the Nvidia logo onto Trump-related imagery from 2024.

The reporting reflects claims attributed to Trump, senators, governors, and sources without independent verification of the underlying national security assessments.
items.title: Trump Defends Jensen Huang's Nvidia Reinstatement as Lawmakers Demand National Security Answers

items.summary:
On Monday, President Donald Trump stated that he had spoken with Nvidia's board 'directly and indirectly' and 'convinced them' to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang. The claim was made during a CNBC phone interview in which Trump described feeling strongly about the matter because it concerned an important part of his country, noting that he also spoke personally with Huang on Sunday night before the reinstatement announcement.

The reinstatement followed Huang's resignation earlier in the month amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia announced Huang's return and reported its shares rose 33% following the news.

Trump said the board requested assurances regarding national security risks before deciding to reinstate Huang, stating that 'we gave him assurance at least with everything we know.' He characterized losing Huang as 'a far bigger threat' than retaining him and praised the board for acting responsibly. Trump also posted an altered image on Truth Social depicting Huang holding up a red bra in a pose modeled after his 2024 fist-raising photo taken after surviving an assassination attempt, with Nvidia's flag replacing the American flag.

The account relies entirely on statements attributed to Trump and reported events; it does not independently verify whether he influenced the board's decision or confirm details of Huang's reinstatement beyond Nvidia's own announcement.
items.title: Trump Claims He Convinced Nvidia Board to Reinstate Jensen Huang; Shares Jump 33%

items.summary: Nvidia's stock climbed by nearly 33% to midday ET (17:00 GMT) on the day its board of directors unanimously voted to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive with immediate effect. The move followed his resignation less than two weeks earlier after he admitted an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, during which time Nvidia shares had fallen significantly. On this same day, the tech-heavy Nasdaq rose nearly 7%, and broader tech stocks rebounded from Friday's large declines; Amazon gained about 4% and Microsoft about 3%. Other chipmakers also jumped sharply: Micron Technology up 19% and Intel up nearly 13%. Despite the surge, Nvidia's share price remained roughly 21% below its level a month earlier. The rally preceded Huang's return announcement in pre-market trading, though it followed an unconfirmed report that Nvidia was under SEC investigation over accounting practices; on Friday alone, Nvidia shares fell 13.7%, amid fears of tougher AI regulation after the midterm election victory. Company officials attributed the reinstatement to a series of discussions with Huang, while President Donald Trump claimed he had personally convinced the board. Analysts noted Huang's central role in the AI sector and described the turnaround as remarkable given the spy scandal and unconfirmed investigation, though one analyst cautioned that Huang may adopt a more conservative approach under heightened scrutiny.
items.title: Nvidia shares rose nearly 33% after board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO

visual.alt: Bar chart. Nvidia shares 33 %; Micron Technology 19 %; Intel shares 13 %; Nasdaq (tech-heavy index) 7 %; Amazon shares 4 %; Microsoft shares 3 %.

items.summary: According to columnist Nils Pratley, Nvidia's board reversed its decision to remove co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang within roughly six days of the initial exit. The departure had originally been justified by Harvey Jones, newly installed as chair, citing disclosure of personal behaviour inconsistent with the company's code of conduct; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reinforced this stance, calling for an external hire amid scrutiny over export-control compliance. Pratley attributes the reversal to political pressure from senior levels of the US government: Trump stated he convinced the board to reinstate Huang as "a great patriot and national treasure," asserting that no reason existed to believe his return threatened national security. The investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort—and references to an alleged affair with Alice Huang, whom officials suspect of smuggling Nvidia chips into China—had not been completed at the time of reinstatement. Pratley links the reversal partly to falling AI share prices after the resignation and Trump's interest in preventing a burst of the AI valuation bubble, noting that roughly $1tn was instantly added back to Nvidia's valuation. He flags ongoing risks: Bessent had earlier pressed questions about Huang before his own U-turn, congressional scrutiny of export controls continues despite Nvidia forming a compliance committee, Rubio reportedly circulated an intelligence memo identifying Alice Huang as a Chinese spy, and Huang can no longer be trusted on export-control matters. Pratley concludes that the board reversed its largest decision under political pressure while forfeiting independence and without meaningful checks on Huang's power, arguing the directors should resign out of embarrassment.
items.title: Nvidia Board Reverses Jensen Huang's Ouster Under Political Pressure

items.summary:
More than 150 child safety groups and experts across six continents have urged Amazon and eBay to halt the sale of AI-enabled toys this Christmas until they are proven safe, calling for refunds on already purchased items. The coalition's letter to Amazon president Andy Jassy and eBay president Jamie Iannone cited documented risks, including a plush bunny marketed to ages three and older that was connected to ChatGPT—whose terms require users be 13 or older—and which Alliance 4 Children found suggested children could consent to being touched for pleasure. The group noted nearly 30 such toys were listed on Amazon's UK site in late October, with about 50 recently available in the US, and that several advertised voice-cloning and emotional growth tracking features.

Supporting evidence includes a March 2026 University of Cambridge study for the Childhood Trust finding young children form emotional bonds with AI toys while showing no developmental benefits, and a United States Public Interest Research Group report testing seven toys that found most were too faulty to sell due to privacy issues or inappropriate responses—one even unexpectedly taking photos. The coalition argued the precautionary principle applies, contending products should be proven safe before reaching children rather than withdrawn after harm is discovered.

Separately, a letter signed by 52 MPs and peers was delivered at No 10 requesting business secretary Jonathan Reynolds restrict AI toy sales until safety is established and asking the Office for Product Safety and Standards to issue an alert ahead of Christmas. Signatories included Jess Asato, Sharon Hodgson, Andrea Leadsom, and Caroline Dinenage.

Amazon stated it requires third-party sellers to comply with applicable laws and has removed named products during review; eBay said it continually evaluates policies and complies with regulations; and the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade confirmed it is investigating both the products and AI risks. The OPSS had not yet responded at time of writing.
items.title: Child Safety Groups Urge Amazon and eBay to Stop Selling AI Toys Until Proven Safe
